jobs.title: Enterprise Systems Engineer - Lab Operations
jobs.description:
About the job

Delart is home to a team of world-class engineers and project leaders dedicated to developing the next generation of advanced networking technologies, consumer devices, and innovative technology solutions. Trusted by some of the world’s leading technology companies, we deliver highly scalable, mission-critical solutions that power both consumer and business applications globally. Since our founding in 2017, we have been at the forefront of designing cutting-edge networking, telecommunications, and consumer products, while driving end-to-end project execution and creating transformative technology applications.

Overview

Join a dynamic Lab Operations team as an Enterprise Systems Engineer, providing critical IT and systems support for multi-site R&D labs. You will ensure reliable lab infrastructure by managing device lifecycles, resolving network issues, and developing automations to optimize daily workflows. Expect to work closely with cross-functional partners to maintain secure, scalable, and efficient lab environments.

Responsibilities

• Oversee device lifecycle management: deploy, image, configure, and decommission lab hosts (Linux/Ubuntu/CentOS, Windows, macOS) across multiple labs and buildings.

• Manage OS patching and security updates for lab devices to ensure ongoing compliance and reliability.

• Serve as first-responder for lab network issues, troubleshooting connectivity, IP/DHCP, IPv6, and 802.1x authentication problems.

• Coordinate with network infrastructure, patch management, and network security teams to escalate and resolve complex device issues across labs.

• Provision and onboard new lab devices and networks, including registration, device health monitoring, and handling inactive-device alerts.

• Manage certificate deployment and renewal on lab hosts, particularly for 802.1x authentication.

• Build and maintain automations (primarily using Bash scripting) to streamline device registration, monitoring, and patching workflows.

• Design and implement scalable virtual machine solutions (e.g., VMware, KVM, Proxmox, Hyper-V) for lab infrastructure expansion.

• Support multiple lab teams and programs as a shared operational service, coordinating setup and troubleshooting across different sites.

• Document lab systems, configurations, and standard operating procedures for cross-team accessibility.

Minimum Qualifications

• Associate's or Bachelor's degree in a technical field, or equivalent experience with relevant IT/networking certifications.

• 8+ years’ experience in IT systems administration, lab operations, enterprise systems engineering, or similar technical support roles.

• Proven hands-on expertise with administration and patching of Linux (Ubuntu/CentOS), Windows, and macOS systems.

• Proficiency in Bash scripting and automation for systems administration tasks.

• Demonstrated working knowledge of core networking concepts and protocols (DHCP, IP/IPv6, DNS, 802.1x authentication) to serve as triage and troubleshooting lead.

• Experience deploying, imaging, and managing large fleets of lab or end-user devices.

• Familiarity with device provisioning, registration, and certificate management workflows.

• Strong documentation practices and ability to coordinate across multiple technical teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related technical discipline.

• Certifications such as CCNA, CompTIA Network+, Security+, or Red Hat/Linux credentials.

• Experience architecting and deploying scalable VM infrastructure solutions (VMware, KVM, Proxmox, Hyper-V).

• Familiarity with configuration management and fleet patching tools (Ansible, MDM, SCCM, Chef, Puppet, etc.).

• Background supporting lab or test environments with diverse hardware and OS platforms.

Benefits

Delart provides competitive benefits and compensation across all regions where we operate. In the United States, our benefits package includes premium PPO and HMO medical insurance, dental and vision coverage, flexible spending accounts (FSA), life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance, a company-matched 401(k) plan, and a generous paid time off policy.

Join us in shaping the future of technology. Apply today!

Delart is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are dedicated to fostering an inclusive workplace for all employees. We strictly prohibit discrimination or harassment of any kind based on race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability, genetics, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Vendor Supply Chain Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT ONELEET

Oneleet is one of the fastest-growing security and compliance platforms in history. We are on a mission to change the compliance and security industry by making cybersecurity and compliance effective, easy, and painless. We provide a platform that helps companies build, manage, and monitor their cybersecurity programs and achieve compliance standards such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001 efficiently, without cutting corners.

Having just raised a $33 million Series A, we are rapidly growing in customers and employees. Our team has decades of experience in security and compliance. Join our team of opinionated rebels and help us build a category-defining company reshaping the broken and fragmented compliance and cybersecurity industry.



WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR:

We value passionate self-starters with a growth mindset and a bias for action and personal accountability. If you love solving hard problems, thrive in ambiguity, and want to make a real impact, you’ll fit right in.

We’re especially drawn to:

 - Rebels with a cause — frustrated with the status quo and eager to disrupt it.

 - Opinionated (but not obstinate) builders — decisive yet collaborative, who help us move fast.

 - Clear communicators — who own their ideas and follow through.

Our mission is simple: make effective cybersecurity painless. We believe cybersecurity should empower, not burden. This belief unites our team and drives every decision we make.

If you’re ready to challenge the status quo and help shape the future of cybersecurity, we’d love to meet you.




THE ROLE

Oneleet helps customers understand the security posture of the vendors they use without repeating the same research for every company. Our shared vendor library brings together findings from public sources so customers can make informed decisions faster.

As our Vendor Supply Chain Analyst, you’ll help build and maintain that library. Your core responsibility is verifying AI-generated research: checking findings against saved sources, resolving gaps, and making sure the evidence supports the conclusions. Engineering owns the AI research pipeline; you’ll provide the feedback that makes its output more accurate and useful.

Each shared vendor record has a security posture score. Customer-specific risk scores are calculated separately using each customer’s exposure to that vendor. Your work ensures the underlying vendor research is reliable.

Preliminary research results appear immediately. Human verification follows, with a target turnaround of 1-2 days. The pipeline automatically re-researches vendors every 90 days and routes significant changes for human review.

You’ll help work through an initial backlog of approximately 500–600 vendors, prioritizing those used by the most customers. You’ll also help establish how we measure research accuracy and compare computed scores with existing customer-assigned ratings. This is an opportunity to shape how Oneleet evaluates vendor security at scale.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Verify vendor research. Check AI-generated findings against saved sources, prioritizing vendors by how many customers use them. Correct unsupported claims and distinguish confirmed findings from missing or inconclusive evidence.

 - Build and maintain the vendor library. Research new SaaS vendors, resolve incomplete records, and review significant changes flagged by the pipeline, including breaches and changes to security practices.

 - Resolve source-access gaps. When the pipeline cannot fetch a page or encounters a login barrier, find an accessible source or manually upload an available document.

 - Confirm public security claims. Verify evidence for criteria such as SSO availability, published DPAs, subprocessor lists, and whether a SOC 2 report exists.

 - Measure accuracy and calibrate scoring. Evaluate research accuracy during the proof of concept and beyond. Compare computed scores with existing customer-assigned ratings, investigate differences, and recommend adjustments where the evidence supports them.

 - Improve research quality. Document recurring errors, missed evidence, and ambiguous results, then give engineering actionable feedback to improve the AI pipeline.

 - Recommend criteria updates. Identify gaps or unclear definitions in the evaluation criteria and propose changes as vendor practices and security expectations evolve.

 - Maintain defensible evidence. Keep findings traceable to saved sources, with clear reasoning and research dates, so customers and auditors can understand the basis for a finding months later.

 - Develop verification runbooks. Document repeatable review steps and escalation paths that help the team make consistent decisions.




YOU MIGHT BE A GOOD FIT IF YOU HAVE

 - Hands-on experience conducting vendor security due diligence or third-party security assessments.

 - Strong research skills and the judgment to distinguish evidence from marketing claims.

 - Familiarity with SaaS security practices and public security, privacy, and compliance documentation.

 - An analytical mindset and comfort investigating discrepancies, documenting uncertainty, and checking whether a score reflects the underlying evidence.

 - Clear written communication and careful documentation habits.

 - A self-starter mindset: you take initiative, adapt quickly, thrive in ambiguity, and enjoy building processes from scratch.




BONUS POINTS FOR

 - Experience evaluating AI-generated research or designing human review processes.

 - Experience measuring research accuracy, calibrating scoring systems, or building quality assurance processes.

 - A background in third-party risk, compliance, or security research.

 - Experience helping an early-stage startup grow from Seed to Series A or beyond.

 - Scripting or automation skills that help you analyze results or make verification more efficient.


WHY ONELEET?

At Oneleet, you’ll join a tight-knit team of rebels redefining the cybersecurity industry. We move fast, own our work, and challenge outdated models to make security effortless and effective for companies.

Here’s what makes us special:

 - We value impact over titles, autonomy over micromanagement, and clarity over jargon.

 - You’ll tackle meaningful, hard problems with real-world consequences.

 - You’ll work with smart, kind, and ambitious teammates who lift each other up.



PERKS & BENEFITS

 - Comprehensive health & wellness benefits

 - 20 days PTO per year, plus 8 floating holiday

 - Remote work culture

 - Team off-sites in stunning places (Amsterdam, Italy, etc).

 - Competitive compensation & equity

We hire globally and compensate competitively within each market using geographic pay bands. The range for this role reflects a US national baseline. Offers for candidates in higher cost-of-labor markets (e.g., San Francisco, New York, Zurich) may fall at or above the top of the posted range, while offers in other markets are benchmarked to local standards and are lower. Within any range, individual compensation is determined by work location, skills and experience demonstrated through the interview process, and relevant education or training. This posting reflects base salary only and does not include equity or benefits.


Remote-First & Global Hiring

We’re a remote-first company and hire globally in regions where we can legally engage talent directly or via our employer-of-record (EOR) partner. If you’re based outside the U.S., we’ll explore the most compliant hiring arrangement for your location. We make hiring decisions based on merit, skills, and potential regardless of location.

jobs.title: Enterprise Account Executive
jobs.description:
OpenGov is the leader in AI and ERP solutions for local and state governments in the U.S. More than 2,000 cities, counties, state agencies, school districts, and special districts rely on the OpenGov Public Service Platform to operate efficiently, adapt to change, and strengthen the public trust. Category-leading products include enterprise asset management, procurement and contract management, accounting and budgeting, billing and revenue management, permitting and licensing, and transparency and open data. These solutions come together in the OpenGov ERP, allowing public sector organizations to focus on priorities and deliver maximum ROI with every dollar and decision in sync. Learn about OpenGov’s mission to power more effective and accountable government and the vision of high-performance government for every community at OpenGov.com http://OpenGov.com.




JOB SUMMARY:

The Enterprise Account Executive will lead all sales efforts within their assigned territory for a defined OpenGov Product Suite.  Including, territory planning,  prospect identification, lead generation, sales cycle management, and ownership of sales calls, proposals, and contract negotiation through deal closure.  This individual will work collaboratively with the Enterprise Pod Leader and additional stakeholders throughout the organization to meet sales goals and deliver the highest standard of integrity, quality, and customer service to our customers.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Lead the customer relationship for a defined OpenGov Product Suite driving the overall strategy for a specific territory and marshaling the pre-sales team to grow our new and existing customer accounts

 - Ability to work collaboratively with the Enterprise Pod Leader to aid in closing, complex multi-suite enterprise opportunities with strategic accounts

 - Establish, handle, and manage relationships between OpenGov and senior leaders of the customer and prospect government;

 - Generate new leads through networking and prospecting, including cold calling, as well as using marketing and PR activities of the company.

 - Make sales presentations to customers and prospects at different levels of the organization of leading governments within a prescribed territory.  Including high-level, vision-setting product demonstrations.

 - Quickly develop thorough knowledge of company products and client verticals, including local and state governments, special districts, non-profits, higher education, and school districts

 - Address product use cases, benefits, competitive advantages, and business outcomes; facilitate executive and technical follow-up to close the sale

 - Target account selling (prospecting/lead generation, qualification and scoping, closing strategies, negotiations, etc.)

 - Interface and develop professional relationships with existing customers and prospects throughout all organizational levels. Establish referenceable customers to build the OpenGov brand in your territory

 - In collaboration with OpenGov's marketing team, develop and execute demand-generation campaigns

 - Lead contract negotiations

 - Partner with Marketing on leads from trade shows and campaigns. Help set event strategy for where OpenGov should be present

 - Take ownership of sales process management and participate in sales planning status meetings (MEDDIC methodology, QBRs, and more)

 - Develop and maintain in-depth knowledge of a defined OpenGov Product Suite and the competitive landscape

 - Meet or exceed quota expectations




REQUIREMENTS AND PREFERRED EXPERIENCE:

 - Bachelor's degree or commensurate experience required

 - 4+ years of quota-carrying sales experience and have previously sold software solutions required (State and Local Government vertical is a bonus but not required)

 - Strong work ethic and hunter mentality

 - Ability to thrive in a collaborative environment

 - Curious and coachable when it comes to new challenges

 - Demonstrated a consistent track record of hitting and exceeding quotas

 - Proven ability to close complex, consultative deals

 - Ability to travel up to 50%

 - Passionate about selling technology and what it can do for society

 - Ability to learn to speak with senior executives about the direction of their organization, transformational projects, and budgets required to get there

 - Self-motivated, creative, results-driven, solution-oriented, direct, and convincing when it’s right for the customer

 - Competitive, driven to succeed

 - Ability to remain focused and flexible during rapid change

 - Crisp written communication and fluency of expression

 - Experience with a CRM, ideally SalesForce



Compensation:

Chicago, IL: $190,000 - $260,000

On target ranges above include base plus a portion of variable compensation that is earned based on company and individual performance.

 

The final compensation will be determined by a number of factors such as qualifications, expertise, and the candidate’s geographical location.




WHY OPENGOV?



A Mission That Matters. 

At OpenGov, public service is personal. We are passionate about our mission to power more effective and accountable government. Government that operates efficiently, adapts to change, and strengthens public trust.  Some people say this is boring.  We think it’s the core of our democracy.



Opportunity to Innovate

The next great wave of innovation is unfolding with AI, and it will impact everything—from the way we work to the way governments interact with their residents. Join a trusted team with the passion, technology, and expertise to drive innovation and bring AI to local government. We’ve touched 2,000 communities so far, and we’re just getting started.



A Team of Passionate, Driven People

This isn’t your typical 9-to-5 job; we operate in a fast-paced, results-driven environment where impact matters more than simply clocking in and out. Our global team of 800+ employees is united in our commitment to challenge the status quo. OpenGov is headquartered in San Francisco and has offices in Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Dubuque, Dallas, and Pune.



A Place to Make Your Mark

We pride ourselves on our performance-based culture, where every employee is encouraged to jump in head-first and take action to help us improve. If you have a great idea, we want to hear it. Excellent performance is recognized and rewarded, and we love to promote from within.



Benefits That Work for You

Enjoy an award-winning workplace with the benefits to match, including:

 - Comprehensive healthcare options for individuals and families

 - Flexible vacation policy and paid company holidays

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Paid parental leave, wellness stipends, and HSA contributions

 - Professional development and growth opportunities

 - A collaborative office environment with weekly catered lunches.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Hardware Engineering
jobs.description:
The Senior Director, Central Engineering will lead the development of advanced SoC architecture, modeling methodologies, and design enablement strategies across multiple product lines. This role is responsible for establishing scalable design and verification methodologies, driving SystemC and SystemVerilog model development, and leveraging AI-driven techniques to improve productivity, quality, and time-to-market for complex semiconductor SoCs.

The ideal candidate is a recognized technical leader with deep expertise in SoC architecture, system modeling, RTL development, and engineering process transformation. They will partner with product groups, platform teams, and executive leadership to define and deploy next-generation design methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable reuse across the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Technical Leadership

• Define and drive the strategic roadmap for SoC design methodologies across the company.
• Lead architecture reviews and technical direction for complex SoC and subsystem developments.
• Establish best practices for hardware/software co-design and model-based development.
• Provide technical leadership for cross-functional teams spanning architecture, design, verification, emulation, and software.

System Modeling & Virtual Platforms

• Lead development of transaction-level and architectural models using SystemC/TLM.
• Define methodologies for building executable SoC specifications and virtual platforms.
• Drive alignment between SystemC models, RTL implementations, and software development environments.
• Enable early software development and system validation using virtual prototypes.

Design & Verification Methodology

• Develop and standardize SoC modeling and verification flows using SystemVerilog, UVM, and related methodologies.
• Promote reusable IP, subsystem, and SoC-level modeling frameworks.
• Drive methodology adoption across product groups to improve predictability, quality, and reuse.
• Establish metrics and KPIs to measure design productivity and model accuracy.

AI-Driven Engineering Innovation

• Define and implement AI-enabled methodologies for model generation, verification, and validation.
• Evaluate and deploy Generative AI, LLMs, and automation technologies to improve engineering efficiency.
• Create workflows that leverage AI for:SystemC model generationSystemVerilog model developmentVerification content generationCoverage analysisDesign documentationRequirement traceability
• Lead pilot programs and organization-wide adoption of AI-assisted design methodologies.

Organizational Leadership

• Build and lead high-performing engineering teams.
• Mentor directors, principal engineers, and distinguished engineers.
• Foster collaboration across Central Engineering, Product Groups, and external partners.
• Influence long-term semiconductor technology and platform strategy.

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline.
• Master's degree or Ph.D. preferred.

Experience

• 15+ years of experience in semiconductor or SoC development.
• 8+ years of technical leadership experience managing large engineering organizations and complex programs.
• Proven experience leading SoC architecture, design, or verification teams.

Technical Skills

• Strong understanding of:SoC architecture and integrationDigital design methodologiesIP and subsystem developmentHardware/software co-designSoC verification methodologies
• Hands-on experience with:SystemC/TLM model developmentSystemVerilog and UVM-based verification environmentsVirtual platforms and executable specificationsSoC performance modelingDesign and verification automation flows
• Experience creating organization-wide engineering methodologies and design frameworks.

AI & Automation

• Demonstrated experience applying AI/ML technologies to semiconductor design workflows.
• Understanding of Generative AI and LLM-based engineering productivity solutions.
• Capability to define and scale AI-driven model development methodologies across multiple teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience leading disruptive methodologies and influencing mindset changes
• Experience with heterogeneous compute architectures, AI accelerators, MCUs, MPUs, or automotive SoCs.
• Knowledge of cloud-based EDA infrastructure and advanced design automation technologies.
• Track record of driving transformational improvements in engineering productivity and quality.
• Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills.

Leadership Competencies

• Strategic thinker with strong execution focus.
• Ability to influence across organizational boundaries.
• Strong mentoring and talent-development skills.
• Data-driven decision maker.
• Passion for innovation and continuous improvement.
• Proven ability to lead large-scale engineering transformation initiatives.

Location: USA preferred

Level: Senior Director

Function: ENG and Innovation Office/Design Methodology & SoC Architecture

jobs.title: Copy of Carpenter
jobs.description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Carpenter

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We’re hiring a Carpenter in Jacksonville, FL and we’re looking for someone who’s ready to grow with us, bring energy and drive to their work, and help us build the future of construction.

A carpenter's duties involve reading blueprints, constructing and repairing frameworks (walls, floors, doors, windows), installing fixtures (doors, cabinets, drywall, trim), performing drywall finishing, assisting with basic electrical, plumbing, and concrete work, operating tools, collaborating with teams, and maintaining a clean job site.

Primary Responsibilities

• Read and interpret blueprints, drawings, and specifications

• Construct frameworks such as walls, floors, and door/window frames

• Install structures and fixtures (doors, cabinets, drywall, trim, etc.)

• Perform drywall installation, finishing, and repairs as needed

• Assist with or perform basic electrical and plumbing tasks when required

• Support concrete work including forming, pouring, and finishing

• Inspect and replace damaged framework or structures

• Operate hand tools, power tools, and woodworking machinery

• Collaborate with project managers, contractors, and other trades

• Maintain a clean and organized job site

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive compensation

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• 401(k) + company match

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events, food truck nights

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

• Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

• Proven experience as a carpenter or construction worker

• Strong understanding of carpentry techniques and methods

• Working knowledge of drywall installation and finishing

• Basic knowledge of electrical and plumbing systems (preferred)

• Experience with concrete work (forming, pouring, finishing) is a plus

• Ability to read technical drawings and blueprints

• Proficiency with carpentry tools and equipment

• Solid math and measurement skills

• Physical stamina and strength (lifting, standing)

• Attention to detail and craftsmanship quality

• Trained and experienced in safely operating scissor and boom lifts

• Trained and experienced in safely operating skid steer

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or equivalent

• Completion of an apprenticeship program (preferred)

• Trade school or vocational training (a plus)

Physical Requirements

• Up to 90% travel that will include overnight and weekend travel

• Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at a time

• May be required to drive for long periods of time

• Must be able to reach overhead, kneel, stoop, bend, stand and walk

• Construction sites (indoor and outdoor)

• Exposure to varying weather conditions

• May involve heights, heavy lifting, and loud equipment

• Full-time, often with early mornings or extended hours

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an EOE M/F/D/V.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

jobs.title: Fabricator
jobs.description:
About Harbinger

Harbinger is an American commercial electric vehicle (EV) company on a mission to transform an industry starving for innovation. Harbinger’s best-in-class team of EV, battery, and drivetrain experts have pooled their deep experience to bring a first-of-its-kind EV platform to support the growing demand for medium-duty EVs and Hybrids. Harbinger: Familiar Form, Revolutionary Foundation.

Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced and dedicated Fabricator to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in custom metal fabrication, structural welding, and shop operations, with the ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. This role will focus on creating vehicle prototypes, building custom manufacturing tooling, and solving complex physical build challenges to support the successful electrification of medium-duty trucks.

What You'll Do:

• Fabrication & Welding: Perform high-quality metal fabrication and structural welding (e.g., MIG, TIG) of components, adhering strictly to design specifications and safety standards.

• Vehicle Prototypes: Assist in the development and fabrication of vehicle prototypes, working closely with the engineering team to bring innovative designs to life.

• Manufacturing Tooling: Design, fabricate, and maintain custom tooling and fixtures to support the production process and improve efficiency.

• Equipment & Shop Operations: Safely operate and maintain a wide variety of fabrication tools and shop machinery, including welding rigs, manual cutters, benders, grinders, and layout fixtures.

• Process Optimization: Implement and optimize fabrication processes to increase production efficiency and reduce waste.

• Problem Solving: Troubleshoot and resolve hands-on fabrication and assembly challenges, offering practical solutions for complex custom builds.

• Equipment Expansion: Assist in the expansion of our shop’s capabilities by introducing new equipment and technologies.

• Collaboration: Work closely with engineering and production teams to ensure seamless integration of fabricated components into our electrification projects.

• Safety & Maintenance: Adhere to safety protocols, perform regular maintenance on machines, and maintain a clean and organized work environment.

Who You Are:

• Proven experience as a Fabricator or Welder, preferably in the automotive or prototyping industry.

• High proficiency with diverse welding techniques (e.g., MIG, TIG) and manual metal fabrication tools.

• Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently or as part of a team.

• Ability to read and interpret blueprints and technical drawings.

• Familiarity with GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing).

• Excellent attention to detail and a commitment to producing high-quality work.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.

• Commitment to safety and continuous improvement.

• Formal certification in welding or fabrication techniques is highly preferred.

Key Benefits & Perks:

• Comprehensive Health, Dental & Vision (HDV) – 100% employee covered

• Early-stage Stock Options

• Robust Retirement Savings (401k, HSA, FSA)

• Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) & Parental Leave

• Annual Vacation Bonus

• Wellness & Fertility Benefits

• Cell Phone Stipend

• Complimentary Meals & Stocked Kitchens

California Pay Range

$80,000—$100,000 USD

Equal Opportunity

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at info@harbingermotors.com.

This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. jobs.title: Product Designer, Growth
jobs.description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. Our product teams work across research, engineering, product, data, and design to bring OpenAI’s technology to people and businesses around the world.

Design plays a critical role in making powerful AI intuitive, useful, and trustworthy. We hold a high bar for quality and build experiences that earn users’ confidence, while moving quickly and learning from real-world feedback. We favor early validation and continuous refinement over waiting until every detail is perfect.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Product Designer to shape how startups, small businesses, and growing teams discover, adopt, and unlock lasting value from ChatGPT. You’ll own growth experiences across the customer journey, turning the potential of AI into meaningful, everyday impact for people across the world.

This is a highly hands-on role for a designer who pairs exceptional craft with strong product judgment and an experimental mindset. You’ll tackle some of our most interesting growth challenges, using creativity, product intuition, and experimentation to discover new opportunities. We’re looking for someone who loves treating metrics as puzzles to solve, finding unexpected solutions, and learning quickly through iteration.

Above all, you bring exceptional design craft and believe that driving measurable impact and building beautiful, intuitive experiences should go hand in hand.

This role is based in our San Francisco HQ. We offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own end-to-end design for growth experiences across ChatGPT

 - Design and improve experiences across user lifecycle stages like discovery, onboarding, activation, engagement, collaboration, conversion, and retention.

 - Turn ambiguous opportunities into clear hypotheses, compelling prototypes, and polished product experiences.

 - Set a high bar for interaction design, visual craft, systems thinking, content, and end-to-end coherence.

 - Partner closely with product, engineering, data science, research, and go-to-market teams to shape both strategy and execution.

 - Use quantitative data, experimentation, research, and qualitative insights to identify opportunities and evaluate outcomes.

 - Translate complex and rapidly evolving AI capabilities into approachable experiences for people with a wide range of technical expertise.

 - Move fluidly between longer-term product vision and fast, iterative execution.

 - Contribute reusable patterns and insights that strengthen growth experiences across ChatGPT.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have a portfolio demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft across complex, shipped products.

 - Have led substantial product initiatives from early exploration through launch and iteration.

 - Possess strong product judgment and can connect user needs, business goals, technical possibilities, and measurable outcomes.

 - Are comfortable working with data and experiments while balancing quantitative signals with research, intuition, and design judgment.

 - Can move quickly without compromising clarity, coherence, trust, or craft.

 - Are fluent in using AI to explore, prototype, communicate, and extend what you can build.

 - Can turn ambiguous, fast-moving problems into a clear point of view and actionable product direction.

 - Communicate through strong narratives and prototypes that align cross-functional teams.

 - Are excited to rethink established growth patterns and invent interactions that feel native to AI.

 - Care deeply about building products that are useful, trustworthy, and worthy of users’ time.

Direct experience in growth design or developer products is helpful but not required. We’re most interested in designers with strong product judgment, exceptional craft, and evidence that their work meaningfully changed user behavior or business outcomes.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity.

jobs.title: Director of Marine Environmental Impact
jobs.description:
About the Company

We are a renewable energy and ocean technology company committed to rapidly developing and deploying technologies that will ensure a sustainable future for Earth by unlocking the vast energy potential of its oceans. Our focus is on capturing civilizational levels of ultra-low-cost renewable energy for applications including computing and affordable renewable fuels delivered to shore.

The company is a public benefit corporation headquartered in Portland, Oregon, and backed by leading venture capitalists, philanthropic investors, university endowments, and individual investors. We operate as an idea meritocracy in which the best ideas change the company's direction on a regular basis.

About the Job

This is an opportunity to shape the development, environmental profile, and ultimate impact of a fundamentally new renewable energy technology with the potential to achieve planetary scale.

The ocean is not just a valuable renewable energy resource. It's a dynamic, interconnected, critically important ecosystem. Our ocean technologies must set a new bar for clean, low-impact renewable energy both in how they convert ocean energy and in how they're constructed, repaired, and eventually recycled.

As Director of Marine Environmental Impact, you will help make Panthalassa's ocean energy platform one of the cleanest, lowest-impact energy technologies ever developed. Reporting directly to the CEO, you will work closely with our engineering teams, physicists, scientists, and marine operators to understand the interactions between our technology and the ocean environment and minimize the ecological impact of each successive technology iteration.

You will build a team focused on grounding Panthalassa's engineering and strategy in a deep empirical understanding of our effects on ocean ecosystems. You'll develop environmental standards and measurement practices suited for both pilot and large-scale deployments.

You'll build relationships with marine science organizations, nonprofits, universities, independent researchers, and other scientific institutions, enabling third-party research and scientific collaboration through data-sharing and joint research efforts.

Representing Panthalassa externally, you’ll communicate our findings about our environmental footprint and about the environmental characteristics, potential advantages, and tradeoffs of open-ocean wave energy as compared to other planetary-scale energy options, such as conventional fossil-fuel energy systems.

Strong candidates will have a deep background in marine biology, oceanography, ecology, or a related field; experience studying anthropogenic impacts on the ocean; a passion for advising engineers on the development of new technologies; and significant experience communicating scientific findings to both public and academic audiences.

This role is ideal for someone who is passionate about ocean health, grounded in empirical research, intellectually curious, and excited by the opportunity to shape how a new technology platform interacts with the marine environment.

Responsibilities

Company Strategy

• Build out and lead Panthalassa's internal environmental impact function as the company and its deployments scale

• Expand Panthalassa's scientific research strategy around environmental impact, including determining where the company will conduct research internally and facilitate independent research

• Help determine where scientific uncertainty should change company strategy, engineering priorities, or deployment plans

Environmental Impact Assessment and Mitigation

• Lead the scientific evaluation of how Panthalassa's open-ocean technologies interact with marine ecosystems, including identifying the most important environmental questions as the technology evolves

• Develop and implement environmental assessment protocols, monitoring strategies, and mitigation measures for at-sea deployments

• Establish environmental metrics and standards to evaluate successive generations of Panthalassa's technology and deployments

• Lead the documentation and publication of environmental research methods, findings, and uncertainties

• Develop approaches for independent scientific review and third-party validation of Panthalassa's environmental impact

Partnership with Engineering and Deployment Teams

• Collaborate with engineering and design teams on integrating environmental considerations into the design and operation of hardware

• Develop clear internal guidance so engineering teams can understand environmental tradeoffs early and incorporate findings into device design, deployment methods, ongoing operations, recovery, and end-of-life planning

• Work with engineering teams to determine how Panthalassa’s technologies can be instrumented to measure their own environmental interactions and the surrounding ocean environment

External Engagement

• Build deep partnerships with universities, research institutions, independent scientists, nonprofits, government researchers, and other scientific organizations to study Panthalassa's technologies and inform our environmental strategy

• Create opportunities for independent researchers to study our technologies, challenge our assumptions, and publish useful scientific findings

• Develop approaches for sharing scientifically valuable data generated by Panthalassa's systems with the broader research community

• Represent Panthalassa in the scientific community, including attending conferences and contributing to working groups

• Create scientifically accurate materials for external and internal audiences

Required Qualifications

• A doctorate in marine science, oceanography, ecology, environmental science, or a related discipline, with a substantial record of scientific research and leadership and at least five years of relevant postdoctoral professional experience

• Experience studying the effects of human activities or technologies on marine mammals, fish, seabirds, benthic ecosystems, or other marine organisms

• Experience leading scientific teams, research programs, or multidisciplinary initiatives

• Extensive experience designing, conducting, or leading rigorous scientific research in marine or offshore environments

• Strong scientific judgment and a willingness to communicate uncertainty and inconvenient findings clearly

• Ability to work cross-functionally with engineering, operations, design, and manufacturing teams

• Strong verbal and written communication skills

• A strong commitment to scientific integrity, ocean health, and the responsible development of technologies intended to operate at large scale

Desired Qualifications

• Experience leading a significant research program, laboratory, scientific organization, or research institution, or building major scientific partnerships with research institutions

• Experience with ocean sensing and environmental monitoring systems, including technologies such as passive hydrophones, temperature and salinity sensors, underwater cameras, eDNA, or other marine sensing technologies

• Experience building, analyzing, and publishing large scientific datasets

We encourage you to apply even if you meet only some of these desired qualifications. We value curiosity, integrity, and the ability to learn quickly.

Additional Requirements

• Travel for fieldwork, partner visits, and conferences

• Ability to work occasional extended hours to support deployments

• A cover letter is strongly recommended

Compensation and Benefits

If hired for this full-time role, you will receive:

• Cash compensation of $230,000 - $350,000, based on experience and qualifications.

• Equity in the company. We’re all owners and if we’re successful, this equity should be far and away the most valuable component of your compensation.

• A benefits package that helps you take care of yourself and your family, including: Flexible paid time off Health insurance (the company pays 100% of gold-level PPO plan for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Dental insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Vision insurance (the company pays 100% for full-time employees, their partners, and dependents) Disability insurance (the company pays 100% for a policy to provide long-term financial support if you become disabled) Ability to contribute to tax-advantaged accounts, including 401(k), health FSA, and dependent care FSA

• Relocation assistance to facilitate your move to Portland (if needed).

Location

This is a full-time, on-site position in Portland, Oregon, with flexibility for fieldwork and occasional remote work; exceptional candidates will be considered for remote or hybrid positions.

jobs.title: Global Leaves and Accommodations Analyst
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

OpenAI’s Benefits team helps attract, support, and retain the people advancing our mission to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. As part of the People team, we deliver benefits and experiences for a rapidly growing employee population in and outside the US. We partner across People, Payroll, HR Systems, Legal, and external providers to help employees navigate important moments with clear guidance and reliable support.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Leaves & Accommodations Analyst to support the day-to-day administration of OpenAI’s leave of absence and workplace accommodations programs. You will coordinate assigned cases from intake through closure, keep records and documentation organized, and support accurate, timely handoffs across the teams involved.

This is a hands-on, employee-facing role for someone who enjoys careful execution and helping people understand what comes next. You’ll follow established policies and workflows, take responsibility for routine case tasks, and recognize when a complex, sensitive, or unclear request needs guidance from the appropriate case owner.

You will partner closely with HR Business Partners, Payroll, HR Systems, third-party administrators, and other members of the Benefits team. This role reports to the Senior Manager, Global Leave & Accommodation.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Coordinate assigned leave cases. Support intake, documentation follow-up, case tracking, return-to-work coordination, and closure for U.S. and international requests, including medical, parental, and statutory leaves. Use established workflows and seek guidance when requirements are unclear.

 - Help employees navigate the process. Provide clear, empathetic updates about required information, timelines, and next steps. Respond to routine employee and manager questions using approved guidance, and route questions outside your scope to the right partner.

 - Support the accommodations process. Organize required information, coordinate follow-ups, and document approved next steps for ergonomic, disability-related, and religious accommodations. Handle medical documentation only through approved confidential channels. Escalate eligibility questions, policy exceptions, legal requirements, and accommodation determinations to the appropriate case owner.

 - Keep case records accurate. Maintain leave and accommodations data in HRIS and case-tracking systems. Complete routine checks, investigate discrepancies with the appropriate partners, make approved updates, and support audits or testing with HR Systems.

 - Prepare reliable payroll handoffs. Check approved case and pay information, including company-paid time off, statutory benefits, vendor-reported events, and company top-ups. Flag discrepancies and cutoff risks promptly, and confirm that agreed corrections are completed.

 - Coordinate work across partners. Track outstanding actions with third-party administrators, vendors, HR Business Partners, Payroll, and HR Systems. Make next steps and handoffs clear, follow up on open items, and keep the case owner informed of blockers.

 - Stay on top of deadlines and requests. Keep case trackers current, prioritize routine work against established deadlines, and raise competing priorities or urgent employee needs to your manager early.

 - Improve day-to-day execution. Identify recurring issues and suggest practical changes to checklists, templates, and documentation. Help implement approved improvements that reduce errors and make the process easier for employees and partners.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have hands-on experience supporting leave of absence, workplace accommodations, or related HR operations, including case administration, employee inquiries, or confidential records.

 - Bring working familiarity with U.S. leave and accommodations concepts, such as FMLA, ADA, and applicable state or local requirements, and know when to consult approved guidance or ask for help.

 - Are drawn to detail-oriented, employee-facing work. You enjoy keeping cases organized, following through on commitments, and helping people understand their next steps.

 - Can manage multiple cases, dates, documents, and follow-ups while maintaining accurate records and raising deadline risks early.

 - Have practical experience with an HRIS or case-management system and use spreadsheets to check data. Workday experience is helpful.

 - Communicate clearly and empathetically with employees, managers, and cross-functional partners, making responsibilities and next steps explicit.

 - Exercise sound judgment with confidential information and bring a high standard of accuracy, accountability, and service to your work.

 - Learn from feedback and contribute practical improvements. Experience supporting a multi-state or international employee population is helpful, but not required.

jobs.title: Staff Firmware Engineer - Motors
jobs.description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About You and The Role

As a Motor Control Engineer at Zipline, you’ll be responsible for shipping high-performance motor controller firmware for Zipline’s family of proprietary motor controllers. Expect to work closely with electrical engineers, structures and mechanism designers, flight software developers, and test-site operations teams. Our close-knit engineering culture presents a unique opportunity to learn from a strong multi-disciplinary team, and lets you swiftly ship features that are clearly linked to the delivery experience.

We use C++ in our firmware development, with Rust and Python for tooling that will be deployed to our production systems in the field. The team uses hardware- and software-in-the-loop test infrastructure to validate new features and regression test existing functionality. You’ll often be querying large data-sets from our test operations to make high-quality data-driven engineering decisions and build prototypes of new algorithms. You’ll build analyses in Matlab, Julia, or Python to prove the performance of your controls designs, and execute Monte-Carlo simulations to validate complex dynamics.

What You'll Do

• Design estimators and controllers for propulsion motors and actuators, in close collaboration with the vehicle controls team.

• Implement these controllers in C++, targeting a bare-metal ARM microcontroller.

• Write peripheral drivers for new revisions of Zipline’s motor controller hardware.

• Get your hands dirty validating your firmware on the bench and in flight tests.

• Understand and improve the reliability of the flight software system as a whole, working with hardware and systems engineers to develop comprehensive fault management strategies and hardware-in-the-loop tests.

• Build vehicle simulations in Rust to validate and regression test Zipline’s firmware.

• Collaborate with electrical engineers to bring-up and validate new inverter designs.

• Build and maintain automated systems to monitor the performance of our fleet and direct maintenance activity.

What You'll Bring

• Fluency in C/C++, and excitement about writing code in Rust and Python.

• Mastery of nonlinear estimation techniques and classical control theory.

• Eagerness to learn in a fast-paced safety-critical environment.

• Some experience with mechatronic control systems: hobby projects or professional experience are applicable.

• Curiosity and a willingness to work in a variety of embedded environments, from running on bare metal, to using a RTOS and integrating with embedded Linux.

• Experience supporting robotic systems in the real-world, in particular addressing the long-tail of edge-cases and rare events to guarantee safety, reliability, and performance.

• A systems-engineering mindset, and an eye for finding efficient solutions to problems that may lie outside your core competencies. Strong executive communication skills, to efficiently communicate about your work with stakeholders outside your technical domain.

• You must be able to work on-site in South San Francisco, CA.

• A background in electronics design would be appreciated, but is not required.

What Else You Need To Know

The starting cash range for this role is $210,000 - $250,000. Please note that this is a target, starting cash range for a candidate who meets the minimum qualifications for this role. The final cash pay for this role will depend on a variety of factors, including a specific candidate's experience, qualifications, skills, working location, and projected impact. jobs.title: Lead Hardware Reliability Engineer (Starshield)
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

LEAD HARDWARE RELIABILITY ENGINEER (STARSHIELD)

Starshield leverages SpaceX’s Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.

This is an opportunity to build and lead a hardware reliability team for Starshield production. You will identify, analyze, and resolve hardware and process failures to improve the robustness, yield, and documentation of Starshield subassemblies. This role spans PCBA production, battery builds, solar arrays, tanks, and mechanical assemblies such as actuators, reaction wheels, torque rods, and star trackers. You will partner with manufacturing, design, quality, and supply chain teams to strengthen build processes, raise first-pass yield, and lead containment when hardware or process issues put production at risk.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead and hire a team of hardware reliability engineers supporting Starshield production

• Provide technical mentorship and guidance to team members leading root cause investigations of subassembly and process failures

• Align goals and priorities with production and partner engineering teams to achieve program reliability, yield, and rate objectives

• Collaborate with team members to create personalized career growth plans that build their technical capabilities and accelerate progress toward their professional goals

• Drive improvements to products and processes that are not meeting design or production requirements through data-driven decisions, using yield and defect monitoring to identify common failure modes

• Lead containment activities for nonconforming hardware, including isolation of suspect product, impact assessment, and coordination of disposition and recovery

• Improve build processes, work instructions, and production documentation to reduce defects and increase first-pass yield across assigned subassemblies

• Lead qualification of production processes for assigned subassemblies, establishing process readiness before rate production

• Lead PFMEA reviews with manufacturing and design partners to identify process risks, prioritize controls, and drive risk reduction

• Proactively escalate major hardware and process concerns, secure appropriate resources, and maintain clear communication to drive timely resolution and team alignment

• Maintain thorough documentation of failure analysis findings, process investigations, test results, and corrective actions

• Collaborate with the on-orbit reliability team, driving timely improvements to production through on-orbit investigation findings

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, chemical engineering, process engineering, materials science, or other engineering discipline

• 3+ years of experience in hardware development, manufacturing process engineering, failure analysis, or reliability engineering

• 1+ years of experience leading a project, team, or people

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Strong analytical skills with an excellent ability to communicate and collaborate with partners in all disciplines at multiple levels in the organization

• Demonstrated ability to advocate for and implement robust solutions that stand the test of time

• Experience deploying large-scale and/or high-impact solutions in a manufacturing environment

• Experience improving manufacturing processes, work instructions, and production documentation to increase yield and reduce defects

• Experience leading containment, material review, or nonconformance response for production hardware

• Hands-on experience with one or more of the following: PCBA production, battery assembly, solar array manufacturing, pressure vessels or tanks, or electromechanical assemblies (actuators, reaction wheels, torque rods, star trackers, or similar)

• Demonstrated experience troubleshooting and root causing hardware or process failures

• Experience with statistical process control, process capability analysis, yield analysis, and defect Pareto methods

• Familiarity with manufacturing process controls such as soldering, bonding, welding, torque, cleanliness, leak/pressure testing, or similar process-critical operations

• Experience with environmental testing such as HALT/HASS, thermal, vibration, and TVAC

• Active Top Secret, Top Secret SCI, or DOE Level Q clearance, or the ability and willingness to obtain one

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Able to work extended hours and weekends as needed

• An active clearance may provide the opportunity for you to work on sensitive SpaceX missions; if so, you will be subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol test.

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay range:
Lead: $155,000.00 - $215,000.00/per year

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

• To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Director, DTC Channel
jobs.description:
DESCRIPTION

quip is rebuilding how it acquires and keeps direct-to-consumer customers, and the Director, DTC Channel owns that rebuild. Subscription is the heart of our business, and this seat owns whether it grows: the channel P&L, the acquisition budget, and the full funnel from first click through first repeat purchase.

This is a hands-on role. You’ll set the strategy and then get into the work to prove it out, in the numbers, the funnel, and the platforms themselves. Expect to move from a spend review to a checkout conversion problem to a subscriber churn cohort in the same week, and to own the number across all three.

In your first 90 days we’d expect a clean baseline of the funnel and a prioritized, sized list of where we’re losing customers. From there, measurable movement in blended CAC and payback, and a testing cadence that leaves a record of what worked.

This is a hybrid role based in our DUMBO, Brooklyn office two days per week.

Base Salary: $170k to $190k

This range represents anticipated base salary range for this position, in addition to competitive benefits and equity (as applicable). We carefully assess and consider several factors with each candidate, including location, role-related knowledge, experience and skills. Compensation may vary based on these considerations

RESPONSIBILITIES

Channel Ownership

• Own the DTC channel P&L, setting the growth and profitability targets and the plan to hit them

• Partner with finance on budget, planning, and forecasting, and own the variance when the number moves

• Keep promotional strategy in lockstep with quip’s other channel owners so offers don’t compete against each other

• Build the cohort view of our customers, behavioral and demographic, and use it to shape strategy from acquisition through repeat and subscription rather than optimizing the base as one group

Paid Acquisition

• Own the DTC acquisition budget against CAC, payback, and contribution-margin targets rather than channel ROAS alone

• Own paid acquisition driving quip.com across Meta, Google, TikTok, and affiliate, working with our external media partner; set the allocation and hold it to target

• Hold external partners to the same standard of rigor, and keep paid strategy aligned with quip’s other channels

• Make the buy-versus-build calls on the tools and data the channel runs on

Funnel and Conversion

• Own conversion at every step of the funnel, from traffic to PDP through cart, checkout, and first repeat purchase

• Set the priority order on what gets fixed, and quantify the lift on each change

• Set offer and bundle architecture that grows AOV and margin without training customers to wait for a discount

Lifecycle and Retention

• Own the lifecycle program end to end: welcome, post-purchase, replenishment, winback, and subscriber retention across email and SMS

• Drive subscription growth through enrollment, plan design, and the skip, swap, and pause mechanics that keep subscribers active

• Define the volume and variety of creative that paid and lifecycle require, and close the loop with content and creative on what performs

Customer Experience

• Build the end-to-end customer experience in partnership with digital product and CX, with subscription management ease as the priority

• Own CSAT and NPS for the channel, and bring what the community is telling us back into the roadmap

Measurement and Reporting

• Own the reporting growth decisions are made from: CAC and blended CAC, contribution margin per order, LTV and payback, conversion by step, AOV, repeat rate, and subscription churn

• Build and maintain the weekly growth reporting leadership and the board see, and explain any variance in it

• Set the testing agenda across creative, offer, audience, and landing page, and hold a documented cadence of what won and what got cut

Team

• Lead and develop the team, setting goals, priorities, and resourcing across the channel’s work

• Hold the bar on analytical rigor, and make sure recommendations arrive sized and defensible

REQUIREMENTS

• 8+ years in DTC or e-commerce, with meaningful time in CPG: physical product, real COGS and margin math, and repeat-purchase dynamics

• Experience owning a paid acquisition budget against CAC and payback targets, whether run in-house or through external partners

• Hands-on experience with Shopify and Recharge, including building and managing subscription plans, offers, and retention flows

• Deep subscription mechanics: enrollment, plan design, skip, swap and pause behavior, churn, and lifetime value

• Full-funnel range across lifecycle, merchandising, and site conversion, not traffic alone

• Experience managing managers or senior individual contributors

• A quantitative operating style: you lead with the model, size an opportunity before chasing it, and can defend your numbers

• Fluency across the stack: Meta and Google Ads managers, Klaviyo or similar, GA4, and at least one BI or attribution layer

• Track record of identifying where AI-powered tools meaningfully improve a team’s output, and putting them into practice

• Comfort in SQL or a query tool is a plus

• Experience in oral care, personal care, beauty, or supplements is a plus

Benefits:

• Hybrid working environment, with an office located in the heart of DUMBO with breathtaking views of Manhattan Bridge

• Year round early “summer Fridays”

• WiFi enabled rooftop

• Competitive medical benefit package

• Commuter benefits for parking & transit

• Competitive paid parental leave policy for qualifying employees

• Open vacation policy

• Dog-friendly office space

• 401k Tax Benefits

• Competitive compensation package

• Fully stocked kitchen with snacks (make sure to use your quip after snacking!)

• Your very own quip with employee discount packages

• The opportunity to help us make oral care more simple, effective and accessible!

About quip

quip is a design-led oral health and wellness company on a mission to transform oral care from a "have-to" chore into a "want-to" ritual. Launched in 2015, we provide effective, simple and well-designed oral health products with electric toothbrushing at the center. Our award-winning product lineup includes sonic and oscillating toothbrushes, smart brushes that track habits, water flossers, and refillable essentials like floss, and whitening strips. Our products are available for subscription on our site as well as on Amazon, in most major retailers and for sale to Dental Offices.

quip empowers millions of users to take proactive control of their oral health. We believe that by combining science-backed design with intuitive technology, we can guide a lifetime of better habits for every mouth. At quip, we work as one team, stay agile, bring positive energy to everything we do, and play to win for our customers and each other.

quip is committed to promoting equality, inclusion, and diversity beyond your brushing routine. We believe our company is better equipped to care for every mouth when we listen to fresh perspectives from every voice, and in doing so, we build an equal-opportunity team of the brightest minds (and mouths)—regardless of race, gender, age, religion, sexual orientation, identity, or any other trait that makes you you. By celebrating and supporting our differences, we will thrive in our mission to improve oral health for all.

jobs.description:
About Stepful:



Stepful is a workforce platform redefining how America's largest health systems build, train, and retain their talent. Since our founding in 2021, Stepful’s trained over 32,000 practice-ready healthcare workers.


Layering onto our successful direct-to-consumer training, Stepful partners with leading healthcare institutions to address the growing national shortage of healthcare workers. We’re improving access to quality healthcare for everyone, everywhere, and improving access to healthcare career ladders for those who need them most.


Our students form the talent pipelines for major employers such as NY-Presbyterian, Mt. Sinai, HCA, Providence, CVS, and Walgreens. We have partnerships with half of the top 10 health systems in the US and are in process with many more.


Stepful is backed by Y Combinator, Reach Capital, and AlleyCorp, with a recent $55M Series C led by Oak HC/FT https://www.stepful.com/post/stepful-announces-55m-series-c-to-scale-its-ai-powered-training-platform-across-the-healthcare-workforce. We were named the #1 EdTech company in the U.S. by TIME for 2025 https://www.stepful.com/post/stepful-named-1-edtech-company-in-us-top-10-globally-times-2025-list.



Our values:



We credit much of our success to our exceptional team. We’re looking for mission-driven builders who thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments, and embody our four core values:

 - Care first: We do whatever it takes for our students to succeed.

 - Learn quickly: We test, learn with data, and iterate.

 - Build together: We win when we rely on each other.

 - Own it: We show up, take initiative, and show pride.




THE OPPORTUNITY:



Stepful is launching a Radiologic Technology A.A.S. program leading to ARRT (R) certification eligibility.



We're partnering directly with employers to help them build their own RadTech programs, powered by Stepful: they sponsor the education of new talent, and we bring the accreditation, curriculum, instruction, and operations. Labs and clinicals happen inside their facilities, so students train where they'll eventually work, and employers build their own talent pipelines exactly where they need them.



We're scaling this model across the country and are looking for the academic leader who can bring it to life.



As Program Director of record, you'll shape program design and carry accountability for the program's credentialing, completion, and job placement outcomes — success will be measured by program completion and graduation rate, ARRT credentialing exam pass rate, and job placement rate. You'll be supported by dedicated curriculum, operations, partnerships, and policy teams who build against the standards you set. This is a build role, not a maintenance role, for someone who wants their name on the outcomes.



This role is remote with regular travel to partner sites, reporting into our Imaging Programs Lead.




WHAT YOU'LL DO:



Program design and curriculum

 - Support the development of curriculum, ensuring our didactic content meets accreditor standards

 - Lead the development of clinical playbooks that govern supervision, competency progression, and rotation quality, so that students get the practical learning the credential demands

Outcomes, accreditation, and compliance

 - Own program outcomes: carry accountability for metrics such as program completion and graduation rate, ARRT credentialing exam pass rate, and job placement rate; track leading indicators and identify interventions for improvement

 - Lead accreditation and monitor compliance: serve as the primary academic point of contact for ABHES compliance across the program, including annual reporting, substantive change filings, and site visit readiness

Partnerships and faculty leadership

 - Support conversations with our employer partners as a clinical SME: join calls or meetings led by our partnerships team, as your availability allows, speaking to the program's clinical design and answering questions from an informed practitioner's perspective

 - Build and lead faculty: hire, onboard, observe, and develop didactic faculty, lab instructors, and clinical preceptors, in alignment with your vision for the program

Travel and teaching

 - Travel to partner sites for site feasibility assessments, lab observations, preceptor development, and accreditation visits, weighted toward new site launches — likely once monthly in 2026, scaling to up to 50% travel starting 2027; all travel and program-related expenses reimbursed

 - Option to instruct our first cohort, either virtually in didactic courses or on the ground as a clinical educator




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Graduate from an accredited radiography program

 - A Master's degree from a qualified institution

 - Current ARRT R.T.(R) certification

 - Prior Program Director experience of an accredited radiography program

 - 3+ years of full-time clinical experience in medical imaging

 - 2+ years of experience as an instructor in a program at a qualified institution

 - Familiarity with program accreditation and regulatory compliance, including JRCERT and ABHES accreditation requirements and process

 - Strong data and technical literacy, prioritizing leading indicators over retrospective, end-of-year metrics




BONUS POINTS IF:

 - You've built or launched a new academic program from the ground up, rather than only maintained an existing one

 - You have direct experience partnering with employer or health-system stakeholders on workforce pipelines

 - You hold an advanced degree (e.g., MEd, MHA) or certifications beyond ARRT R.T.(R)

 - You've worked in a fast-growing startup or EdTech environment

 - Current Texas GMRT certificate from the Texas Board of Medical Radiologic Technology




INTERVIEW PROCESS:

 - Introductory call with Talent Acquisition

 - Interview with Hiring Manager

 - Take-Home Assignment

 - Final Panel Interviews




BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION:

 - Meaningful Equity Stake

 - Subsidized Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plan options

 - 401(k)

 - FSA, HSA and commuter benefits

 - Learning stipend

 - Open vacation policy, including:

 - Guidance of 15 days PTO annually

 - Stepful closed the last week of December

 - 15 work-from-anywhere days

 - 10 public holidays observed for 2026



The target base salary range for this opportunity is $100,000 - $125,000, and is part of a competitive total rewards package including equity and benefits. Individual pay may vary from the target range and is determined by a number of factors including experience, internal pay equity and other relevant business considerations.
