jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)
jobs.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

Our mission requires an extraordinary team, specifically one that will mold tomorrow's critical technologies while deploying today's best. We are an intrinsically motivated organization with a passion for solving complex technical problems and empowering each other every day, knowing that there is always room for growth.

About The Role

Ursa Major is seeking an executive technology leader to serve as our Chief Information Security Officer (CISO w/ clearance). Reporting to the executive leadership team, the CISO will establish enterprise-wide information security ownership across our multi-site engineering, manufacturing, and test facilities. Working in direct, strategic lockstep with our Facility Security Officer (FSO), who leads personnel clearances, physical security, and overall NISPOM facility compliance, the CISO serves as the ultimate authority for digital, technical, and operational cybersecurity.

We are not looking for an administrator who leads from behind a desk or relies on enterprise bureaucracy. We need a builder who leads from the front—an executive with deep roots in Aerospace & Defense (A&D) who knows what mature security infrastructure looks like and possesses the hands-on drive to build, scale, and mature our systems from the ground up.

Sitting at the intersection of defense compliance, manufacturing velocity, and enterprise IT, you will own the overarching risk management strategy for both unclassified and classified programs. You will champion our hybrid CMMC Level 2 enclave expansion, govern the technical architecture of classified defense enclaves (Secret / SAP), protect critical Intellectual Property, and establish the cyber risk governance required for a high-growth defense firm preparing for public-company operations.

Responsibilities:

• Define and execute Ursa Major’s enterprise cybersecurity and information assurance strategy across all corporate, manufacturing, engineering, and classified program environments.

• Lead from the front to build, mentor, and inspire a world-class cybersecurity engineering and compliance team, fostering a culture of operational enablement, technical rigor, and deep cross-functional partnership.

• Direct the continuous advancement and accreditation of our CMMC Level 2 / NIST SP 800-171 architecture, ensuring Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and defense technical data flow securely across multi-site operations without impeding engineering velocity.

• In close partnership with the FSO and program security, lead the digital architecture, technical authorization packages, and continuous monitoring of classified information systems (Secret, Top Secret, and Special Access Programs) in strict alignment with RMF, JSIG, NIST SP 800-53, and DCSA standards.

• Establish an enterprise cyber risk register, translating technical vulnerabilities into clear operational and business risk metrics for executive leadership and the Board of Directors.

• Partner closely with IT, DevOps, and Digital Manufacturing to embed Zero Trust network segmentation, identity governance (Entra ID), and robust endpoint detection into physical shop floors, test stands, and cloud environments.

• Establish a collaborative, locked-in operating rhythm with the FSO and physical security teams to unify technical cyber defenses with physical enclave controls, COMSEC, and cleared personnel governance.

• Serve as the executive authority for technical and cyber assessments, partnering with the FSO on DCSA security reviews, customer audits, DCMA evaluations, and third-party CMMC assessments (C3PAO).

• Build public-company-grade cybersecurity governance, including incident response playbooks, third-party vendor risk management (TPRM), SEC disclosure readiness, and SOX IT General Controls (ITGC).

• Act as the senior escalation authority for incident handling, crisis communications, threat intelligence integration, and technical remediation.

Minimum Qualifications:

• 12+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, information assurance, and secure systems architecture, with at least 5+ years in senior leadership or technical management roles within the Aerospace & Defense (A&D) sector.

• Active U.S. Government Security Clearance (Top Secret required, with active or recent SCI/SAP eligibility preferred).

• Demonstrated track record of partnering successfully with Facility Security Officers (FSOs), government Authorizing Officials (AOs), and program leadership to secure facility authorizations and system ATOs.

• Deep technical and regulatory mastery of federal security standards, including NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-53, Risk Management Framework (RMF), JSIG, and NISPOM.

• Demonstrated ability to lead hands-on technical initiatives, conduct rigorous architectural reviews with engineering teams, and articulate strategic risk and vision to executive leadership and government customers.

• Experience managing enterprise-wide incident response, endpoint detection (EDR), identity federation, and Zero Trust micro-segmentation in hybrid IT/OT manufacturing environments.

• Current industry certification: CISSP, CISM, or equivalent executive-level security credential.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Active TS/SCI with current SAP/SAR access.

• Experience leading an organization through a successful DCSA security inspection or C3PAO CMMC Level 2 assessment.

• Practical familiarity with public-company readiness, including SOX compliance, cyber risk disclosures, and enterprise business continuity planning.

• Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Information Assurance, or related field.

Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $240,000 - $300,000, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

Backed by over $1 billion in total funding from leading investors including Altimeter Capital, ICONIQ, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Redpoint Ventures, and T. Rowe Price — and with over $1 billion in signed contracts across commercial and US government customers, we're mass-producing the highest-power satellite platforms ever built for missions from LEO to deep space.

With multiple launches in 2027 and plans to scale to 100 satellites a year, we're Building Bigger — helping develop the solar system and build toward a Kardashev Type II (K2) civilization. If you are a motivated individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and you're excited about contributing to the success of a high-growth Series D-funded company, we'd love for you to apply.

The Role

You will play a critical role in the hands-on fabrication, assembly, and testing of the Mega-Class satellite solar array hardware. This role spans solar blanket build, module welding, mechanical assembly, and production testing, while also providing occasional support to the module SMT line.

Responsibilities

• Assemble and build solar array blankets, including module welding, bonding, and integration of electrical hardware

• Perform mechanical assembly of solar array support hardware, fixtures, and sub-assemblies

• Operate light fabrication equipment and tools including welders, presses, cutters, crimpers, torque tools, drills, rivet guns, and custom tooling

jobs.title: Operations Manager, Bookkeeping
jobs.description:
ABOUT LAYER

Over the last decade, a vibrant ecosystem of SMB software tools has emerged to help SMBs manage and run their businesses. These tools help SMBs with everything from payments to payroll, but accounting has lagged behind. Small business owners are still struggling with disconnected, generic, accounting software and expensive bookkeepers.



At Layer, we’re building a new kind of accounting software and bookkeeping that lives within the existing software tools SMBs use every day. Our platform allows software companies to quickly launch modern accounting software and bookkeeping services to their SMB customers, eliminating the need for them to use legacy accounting tools or bookkeepers.




THE ROLE

As a Bookkeeping Operations Manager at Layer, you’ll help us scale our bookkeeping business to meet the rapidly growing demand of our customers. You’ll manage our automated bookkeeping service that already serves close to a thousand SMBs today and help us scale it to tens of thousands.



We’re growing quickly, and our bookkeeping operations need to scale alongside our customer base. We’re building a combination of great people, efficient processes, and software automation to deliver a consistently excellent bookkeeping experience for our customers. In this role, you’ll be responsible for keeping our day-to-day bookkeeping operations running smoothly while helping build the systems that allow us to operate at a much larger scale.



You’ll work closely with our operations, bookkeeping, partnerships, and engineering teams to improve execution, eliminate bottlenecks, and make our team more effective. This is a hands-on role for someone who loves bringing structure to ambiguity, takes ownership of outcomes, and gets satisfaction from making complex operations run better.



Key responsibilities include:

 - Build deep expertise in small business bookkeeping processes and Layer’s bookkeeping systems.

 - Triage and investigate customer issues surfaced by our frontline bookkeeping team.

 - Document and improve our standard operating procedures across our bookkeeping service.

 - Identify opportunities to streamline workflows, reduce manual work, and increase team efficiency.

 - Manage our Philippines-based bookkeeping team. Track performance metrics and SLAs.


SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

This role will suit strong generalists with a growth mindset. If you’re invigorated by the idea of learning quickly, owning results and having a significant impact at a fast growing startup, this role is for you.



We’re looking for candidates who are:

 - Driven by impact - You consistently see the possibility in what could be. You like seeing the results of your work out in the world. You’re energized when surrounded by others that share this ambition.

 - Fast Learner - You’re eager to become a subject matter expert on Layer’s bookkeeping processes & policies

 - Organized and structured - You approach problems methodically and systematize your approach into a repeatable, scalable process that doesn’t drop important details.

 - Biased towards action - You enjoy getting things done and are undeterred by setbacks. You actively seek to understand which problems are most important and you tackle those problems head on.

 - Clear communicators - You’re an exceptional written and verbal communicator. You can efficiently and empathetically interact with everyone from customers, to teammates, to candidates.



Ideal candidates have 2-5 years of experience in startup operations, investment banking, management consulting, or any role that requires exceptional independent execution.

jobs.title: Employee Relations Partner
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

At Anduril, we build the hardware that defines the mission. Arsenal-1 is our advanced manufacturing facility, and its hourly production workforce — operators, technicians, and frontline managers — is the engine behind everything we ship.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a floor-first Employee Relations Specialist to own investigations and proactive ER programs for Arsenal-1's production workforce. You'll run a steady caseload end-to-end while standing up the manager training, trend analysis, and culture initiatives that let the site scale without scaling risk. The split is roughly 60% casework, 40% building. The ER framework exists; you're executing it, pressure-testing it, and improving it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Investigations & Casework:

• Own end-to-end workplace investigations for Arsenal-1's hourly workforce: intake, evidence gathering, interviews, findings, written reports, and recommendations across the full spectrum — policy violations, discrimination, harassment, improper conduct, theft, fraud

• Deliver investigation reports that hold up to Legal and senior leadership review — clear narrative, sound analysis, defensible conclusions

• Partner with PBPs on case review and recommendations; the business makes the final call on outcomes

• Flag risk early and work effectively with in-house employment counsel (and outside counsel when needed) to navigate sensitive or escalating matters

Floor Presence & Relationship Building:

• Build trusted, in-person relationships with frontline managers and shift leads — many operators don't have laptops or Zoom, so you have to be physically present

• Serve as a credible, approachable resource for managers navigating employee issues before they become formal complaints

• Get in front of trends: if a team is generating repeat complaints, you're having the conversation with their manager about expectations, not waiting for the next intake

Program Building & Scale:

• Operationalize and improve the existing investigation workflow — build consistency, documentation standards, and tracking as caseload grows

• Design and deliver proactive ER programs: manager training on policies and behavioral expectations, harassment prevention, investigation awareness

• Identify patterns across casework and translate them into actionable recommendations for PBPs and site leadership

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 4+ years of workplace investigations and employee relations advisory experience — you can run a case solo on day one, intake through written report and recommendation

• Direct experience supporting hourly/non-exempt workforces in production, manufacturing, warehousing, or distribution environments

• Strong written and verbal communication — investigation reports are BLUF, structured for a Legal and leadership audience

• Employment law fluency — you know policy, can interpret it, can spot risk, and have good instincts for when to loop in counsel

• Self-sufficient operator who has worked in environments where the playbook wasn't fully built and the manager wasn't co-located

• Program-building experience — you've built or meaningfully improved ER training, investigation processes, or proactive manager education programs

• Comfortable with ambiguity and operational tempo — you adapt process to the business, not the other way around

• U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Defense, aerospace, or advanced manufacturing background

• Non-union hourly workforce experience (union experience is fine, but non-union dynamics are the primary environment)

• Experience partnering closely with People Business Partners in a matrixed or shared-services model

US Salary Range

$93,000—$124,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker II Complex Care Full-time Days
jobs.description:
Location: 11845 SW Hwy, Palos Heights, IL 60463

The Community Health Worker II reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The NMHC Community Health Worker (CHW) is a frontline health professional who is a trusted member or has a very close understanding of the community served.  This trusting relationship enables the CHW to serve as bridge between health system, social services, and the community.  The CHW facilitates access to services and improves the quality and cultural competence of service delivery.  A CHW also builds individual and community capacity by increasing health knowledge and self-sufficiency through outreach, community education, informal counseling, social support and advocacy.  The CHW reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Responsibilities:

• Act as liaison between health system, social services, and the community.
• Acts as patient advocate to ensure patient receives necessary care and resources that are clinically and culturally appropriate.
• Serve panel of assigned patients across the episode of care to promote trust, continuity, and connection to appropriate services.
• Develop trusting relationships with patients to provide effective, longitudinal support, assist patients in achieving social stability, and close caps in care.
• As part of an interdisciplinary care team, provide services in an outpatient clinic, in the community, and via telephonic support.
• Supports individuals, families, and communities to build capacity and strengthen their access to resources related to NM’s social drivers of health screening, patient education, and other related NM resources.
• Facilitates patient and family education which promotes social wellness and increases knowledge of the health care system.
• Actively participates as a member of an inter-professional team, working with physicians, pharmacists, social workers, therapists, and clinicians to provide comprehensive patient care.
• Collaborates with the Complex Care Clinics, Population Health team, Primary Care, Community Affairs and FQHCs as appropriate to provide comprehensive patient support.
• Complete social drivers of health screenings and provide appropriate resources.
• Basic understanding of chronic, complex diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, COPD, and heart failure.
• Follows regulatory reporting requirements
• Documents appropriate data in the electronic medical record to support the care plan.
• Utilizes motivational interviewing and conflict resolution skills as necessary to ensure timely resolution of issues and system problems.
• Enhance professional growth and development through participation in appropriate educational activities, volunteering events, and community work.
• Train and orientate new community health workers
• Perform other administrative responsibilities as needed

Required:

• Associates Degree or commensurate experience
• Community Health Worker Certification or commitment to complete certification within 2 years
• Minimum two years of customer service experience in a clinical environment.

Preferred:

• Community outreach and education experience.
• Experience in patient facing role.
• Volunteer Experience

If you are offered a position with us, you will be required to complete an authorization and disclosure form that gives Northwestern Medicine permission to run the background check.  Results are evaluated on a case-by-case basis, and we follow all local, state, and federal laws, including the Illinois Health Care Worker Background Check Act.

jobs.title: Principal Recruiter
jobs.description:
TITLE: Principal Recruiter

DEPARTMENT: People and Culture

REPORTS TO: Chief People Officer

TYPE: Full-Time Regular

FLSA: Exempt

ROLE TYPE:  Individual Contributor

OUR CLUBS

Seattle Sounders FC and Seattle Reign FC are united as one soccer family, driven by a shared commitment to excellence, growth, and impact on and off the pitch. Each club has independently forged a rich history of performance while connecting deeply with the community. Our clubs are continually pushing the boundaries of what's possible while fostering an inclusive culture- championing causes and building community connections to expand our reach and impact. Each match is an opportunity to bring together our community, celebrating our resilience, inclusivity, and a commitment to excellence. United in professional dedication- we are two clubs with one shared vision of progress and greatness.

POSITION SUMMARY

The success of Seattle Sounders FC and Seattle Reign FC starts with the people who make our clubs what they are, on and off the pitch. As two clubs united by a shared ambition, we're building a stronger organization for the future, starting with how we attract, develop, and bring talented people together.

As our Principal Recruiter, you'll be our lead expert in talent acquisition and hiring for Seattle Sounders FC, Seattle Reign FC and RAVE Foundation. You'll lead searches, own the hiring process, and set the standards and partnerships that make hiring more effective, consistent, and inclusive. This is a senior individual contributor position reporting to our Chief People Officer.

Working directly with executive leadership, you'll shape hiring strategies, advise on workforce planning, and introduce innovative approaches to recruiting, including responsible applications of AI and automation. You'll have the autonomy to challenge conventional thinking, improve the experience for candidates and hiring managers, and build systems that strengthen how our clubs hire for years to come.

This is an opportunity for a hands-on recruiter, strategic advisor, and builder who believes that assembling exceptional teams, grounded in shared values, is one of the most important ways to shape the future of our clubs.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Lead talent acquisition and hiring across Seattle Sounders FC, Seattle Reign FC, and the RAVE Foundation, owning the hiring process from role definition through offer for every hire.

• Run complex searches with discretion, building trusted relationships with leaders and candidates.

• Hire for the culture we are growing. In every search, partner with leadership to define the behaviors that strengthen our culture, describe what great looks like in each role, and assess candidates through structured, evidence-based evaluation.

• Advise executive leadership on workforce planning, hiring priorities, and talent decisions, bringing market insight, recruiting expertise, and sound judgment.

• Set and uphold the hiring standard, in partnership with the Chief People Officer, through consistent practices, tools, and workflows that keep hiring evidence-based, inclusive, and high quality across every department.

• Lead the use of responsible AI, automation, and recruiting technology to improve effectiveness, reduce unnecessary work, and create new opportunities to strengthen how our clubs attract and evaluate talent.

• Establish meaningful recruiting measurement and reporting capabilities that provide visibility into hiring performance, inform decisions, and identify opportunities for improvement.

• Equip hiring managers to make better hiring decisions and run more effective recruitments through training, guidance, coaching, and consistent evaluation practices.

• Build proactive talent pipelines and sourcing strategies across both clubs, including passive and hard-to-reach talent.

• Mentor and guide the Senior HR Generalist and People & Culture partners on recruiting practice, standards, and tools.

• Partner across People & Culture and the broader organization to align recruiting with business needs, compensation practices, and organizational priorities.

• Champion responsible, equitable, and compliant recruiting practices, maintaining appropriate human oversight, candidate privacy, and accountability in hiring decisions.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

We're looking for an experienced recruiter and talent acquisition expert who combines strong execution with strategic thinking, sound judgment, and passion for building better systems.

Required Qualifications

• 10+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, including hiring for individual contributor, leadership, and executive positions.

• A track record of raising the standard of hiring by designing, improving, or scaling recruiting processes and systems.

• Experience leading complex and confidential searches and advising senior leaders on hiring decisions.

• Strong knowledge of structured interviewing, candidate assessment, and consistent evaluation practices.

• Hands-on experience evaluating or implementing recruiting tools, automation, or related technologies.

• Demonstrated experience designing, building, and implementing agentic AI workflows that automate or improve complex, multistep work processes.

• Hands-on proficiency using AI assistants, automation platforms, and connected tools to improve personal productivity and organizational effectiveness, with the judgment to evaluate outputs and maintain appropriate human oversight.

• Experience partnering with leadership on hiring strategy, workforce planning, and talent priorities.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence, coach, and build trust across different teams.

• Working knowledge of federal, state, and local employment and hiring laws, including equal employment opportunity, pay transparency, fair chance hiring, and background check requirements, with the judgment to know when to involve Legal.

• A commitment to fair, inclusive, and responsible hiring practices.

A college degree is not required. We value demonstrated experience, sound judgment, and the ability to deliver meaningful results.

Competencies, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

• Strategic Thinking and Judgment: Connects talent decisions to organizational priorities, anticipates future needs, and balances data, experience, and human judgment to make sound decisions.

• Builder Mentality and Systems Thinking: Sees opportunities to improve how things work, creates structure where needed, and develops solutions that are practical, connected, and sustainable.

• Curiosity and Innovation: Challenges conventional approaches, embraces emerging technologies, and identifies meaningful opportunities to improve outcomes.

• Influence and Partnership: Builds trust across teams and with executive leadership, communicates with clarity, challenges assumptions constructively, and helps others make better decisions.

• Ownership and Accountability: Takes initiative, follows through on commitments, measures impact, and demonstrates sound judgment, integrity, and a commitment to equitable and inclusive practices.

• Demonstrates a commitment to our values and mission (Create Moments, Enrich Lives, and Unify & Uplift Through Soccer) in all interactions with colleagues, partners, vendors, and fans.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

This position is based at our headquarters and training facility, the Providence Swedish Performance Center & Clubhouse in Renton, Washington.

We work together in person Monday through Thursday, with flexibility to work remotely on Fridays. Our work follows the rhythm of the soccer calendar, so occasional evenings and weekends are part of the role, and workloads may vary throughout the season, particularly during peak hiring periods.

Additional requirements include:

• Must reside within Washington state upon date of hire.

• Must be able to facilitate own local travel.

• Must be eligible to work in the US without sponsorship.

• Responsibilities may include regular work outdoors and require standing on feet for long periods of time, as well as some lifting of up to 20 pounds.

COMPENSATION, BENEFITS AND PERKS

We offer competitive compensation and an engaging, supportive environment that prioritizes the health and well-being of our people.

The salary range for this position is $140,000 - $190,000. Positioning within the range at time of offer is based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, internal equity, and current market conditions.

In addition to financial compensation, we provide a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your overall well-being and professional growth, including:

• Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: We offer 100% employer-sponsored medical, dental, and vision premiums for you and your dependents. For employees enrolled in our HSA healthcare plan, we provide employer contributions to a Health Savings Account (HSA) — $1,000 per year for employee-only coverage and $2,000 per year for spouse or family coverage.

• Generous Paid Time Off & Leave: We offer unlimited paid vacation, paid company holidays, and paid sick leave in compliance with Seattle’s Paid Sick and Safe Time ordinance. We also provide paid bereavement leave and paid jury duty leave to support you during life’s critical moments.

• Retirement Planning Support: 401(k) retirement plan matching, helping you secure your financial future with ease.

• Fertility & Family-Building Support: We provide a $10,000 lifetime maximum fertility benefit through our healthcare plan to support employees in their family-building journeys. This benefit includes coverage for infertility treatment, IVF, IUI, embryo transfer, fertility preservation, and related medications.

• Inclusive Parental Leave: Our gender-neutral parental leave program provides 12–16 weeks of paid leave, inclusive of Washington Paid Family & Medical Leave (PFML), giving new parents the time and support they need during this important life stage.

• Peace of Mind Coverage: Employer-paid long-term disability coverage, as well as basic life insurance and accidental death & dismemberment (AD&D) coverage, providing financial protection and peace of mind for you and your family.

• Exclusive Perks: Enjoy complimentary tickets to matches and employer-funded ORCA cards for public transit, making it easier for you to experience the excitement firsthand.

• Continuous Growth Opportunities: We invest in your learning and development through various programs and resources.

• Community Engagement: We provide a variety of volunteer opportunities that align with our social impact goals and RAVE Foundation initiatives, empowering you to make a meaningful difference in the Seattle community.

OUR COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY, EQUITY, AND INCLUSION

We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where every employee is respected, valued, and supported. We celebrate our diverse work environment and welcome team members of all backgrounds and perspectives. If you do not meet every job requirement listed, we still encourage you to apply. We believe your relevant experience and expertise will help us become a high-performing best-in-class workplace for all. Women, gender-nonbinary, people of color, LGBTQIA+ people and people with disabilities are encouraged to apply.

Sounders FC and Reign FC provide equal employment opportunity to all applicants and employees. We do not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law, including race, color, creed, religion, national origin, citizenship or immigration status, age, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, disability, genetic information, veteran or military status, and caste.

The physical demands reflected in the duties and work environment herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. If you’d like to request an accommodation in the application or interview process, please contact the People & Culture Team at careers@soundersfc.com.

In compliance with federal law, all persons hired will be required to verify identity and eligibility to work in the United States and to complete the required employment eligibility verification document form upon hire.

PRIVACY POLICY

By clicking Submit Application, you agree to the terms of the MLS Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Clinical Operations Manager
jobs.description:
About Aegis Ventures

Aegis Ventures is a next-generation startup studio that partners with entrepreneurs and industry leaders to originate, launch, and scale transformative companies, with a focus on artificial intelligence. The Aegis platform brings together market-shaping ideas, permanent growth capital, and ambitious individuals who are driven to solve major societal problems. Our companies use technology to transform healthcare by dramatically improving quality, access, and cost. Aegis creates new companies with substantial input from our Digital Consortium of a dozen leading health systems and other ecosystem partners. We have launched 6 innovative companies to date and are just getting started.

About the Company

Optain is a revolutionary healthcare company that uses groundbreaking software and hardware technology to rethink care. We use the eye as a window to the body to improve the way we detect and manage eye and systemic conditions. Optain is committed to expanding and improving care through the introduction of AI and machine learning technology frontline care settings at an accessible price. This not only promotes greater access to care, but promises to reduce the strains of overburdened healthcare systems.

Originally founded in Australia in 2019, Optain seeks to commercialize the inventions of Professor Mingguang He, a preeminent clinician-scientist and scholar in the field of ophthalmology. Optain has achieved regulatory approval and commercial adoption of its product suite in global markets, including Australia, Europe, and more.

In 2025, Optain received US FDA clearance for its Resolve retinal camera. Optain also recently closed a Series A funding round led by Insight Partners with participation from seven leading U.S. health system investors, including Memorial Hermann Health System, Northwell Health, Novant Health, The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, and UPMC. These systems collectively deliver care to 28 million patients across 25 states and have begun deploying Optain's platform across their networks, rapidly accelerating the company's footprint and expanding screening access nationwide. Optain also acquired EyePACS, a teleophthalmology platform with a 15-year history and an established network of licensed optometrists and ophthalmologists who read retinal images for diabetic retinopathy screening.

About the Job

As the Clinical Operations Manager, you will own the operations of Optain's provider network -- the optometrists and ophthalmologists who read retinal images for health systems, clinics, and community health centers across the United States. The network has run for 15 years on the judgment and relationships of a small number of people. Your job is to turn that into documented policy, a measurable quality program, a capacity model that runs ahead of demand, and a governance rhythm in alignment with Optain’s Medical Director. You will report to the VP of Operations and work day to day with Optain's Medical Director. This is a non-clinical role for someone who has managed a network of contracted clinicians before, writes policy that physicians sign, and knows the difference between running a process and building one that doesn't need you.

Optain is at an inflection point. We have FDA clearance, a growing camera footprint, and a commercial pipeline that is moving fast. Behind every screening exam is a licensed grader reading the images through our EyePACS platform, and the operational infrastructure around that network is being built in real time. This role sits at the center of that work.

This is a remote, US-based position.

What You'll Do

• Own the grading playbook, SOPs, onboarding materials, and the provider network policy library -- author, version, and maintain them, and route clinical content to the Medical Director for review and sign-off.

• Establish documentation governance for the network -- ownership, versioning, review cadence, and sign-off -- so operating knowledge lives in documents rather than in individuals.

• Design and run the grader quality program, including sampling, over-read and discordance review, turnaround accountability, and performance feedback -- establish error rates and trends where today review is periodic and manual.

• Prepare quality reviews and escalations for Medical Director adjudication and carry out the resulting actions, including performance conversations and offboarding.

• Build and maintain a capacity model by state, customer, and license coverage, and set recruitment triggers ahead of turnaround breaches.

• Run the grader recruitment pipeline from sourcing through interview and recommendation, working with the Operations Manager on credentialing and onboarding execution.

• Own intake, triage, and routing of customer and grader complaints, including urgent findings workflows -- route clinical questions to the Medical Director, close the loop with the customer, and trend issues over time.

• Set the agenda, prepare decisions, and follow through so the Medical Director's time goes to clinical judgment rather than logistics.

• Partner with Product and Engineering on platform improvements that reduce manual work, including documenting current-state workflows so feature development is accurate and fast, and contribute network measurables to the weekly grader operations rhythm and company scorecard.

What You'll Need

• 5+ years in healthcare operations, with 2+ years managing a network of contracted or affiliated clinicians -- telehealth, teleradiology, or virtual care strongly preferred over traditional medical group or IPA settings.

• Has written clinical or operational policy that a physician leader signed, and maintained it afterward.

• Has run or materially contributed to a clinical quality, peer review, or provider performance program.

• Prior experience operating a clinician network under a medical director's clinical oversight is a strong plus.

• Exposure to credentialing, medical staff services, or multistate clinician licensing is a plus; teleophthalmology background is a plus, not a requirement.

• Experience participating in product discovery or operationalizing new feature launches is a plus.

• Comfortable building and reading operational dashboards and capacity models in spreadsheets or BI tools.

• Startup experience is strongly preferred -- you have built a process where little existed and can show the result.

• Clear, direct written communicator who is comfortable working with physicians as a non-clinician.

• Has driven adoption of new processes across teams without direct reporting authority.

• US-based, comfortable with remote work and occasional travel for team offsites and customer engagements.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

• The grading playbook, onboarding materials, and network policy library are current, versioned, and signed, with a documented review cadence.

• A grader quality program is running, with error rates and turnaround trends reported monthly and at least one full cycle of performance feedback completed.

• A capacity model by state and customer is in use, and recruitment is triggered by the model rather than by turnaround breaches.

• A complaint intake and escalation process is documented and running, with clinical questions routed to the Medical Director.

• The Medical Director's time goes to clinical decisions, with decision prep and follow-through owned by this role.

• At least two manual network processes have moved into the platform in partnership with Product and Engineering.

What We Offer

• Competitive compensation package, including a strong base salary, performance-based bonus, and the chance to earn upside.

• Top-tier health, vision, dental, and commuter benefits.

• Generous monthly health and wellness reimbursement.

• Unparalleled exposure to new business building at the intersection of artificial intelligence and healthcare.

• The opportunity to help solve difficult problems and collaborate with world-class experts from healthcare provider networks, academia, and industry.

• A chance to work with a highly talented, close-knit team and world-leading mentors who can act as a support network and sounding board throughout your entrepreneurial journey.

Salary Range

Why Optain? Make a real difference: Your work will help solve difficult problems as you collaborate with world-class experts from healthcare provider networks, academia, and industry. Join Optain in transforming healthcare with AI!

jobs.title: Program Manager, Commercial Solutions
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Global Business Services’ (GBS) Commercial Solutions team ensures operational and programmatic excellence across deal cycles, increases revenue through the development of transformative commercial constructs, and drives closure of Stripe’s sold portfolio. The team's reach is widespread across Stripe, not exclusive to one sales segment or geographical region; GBS drives change across go-to-market, positively impacting Stripe users, and cross-functional teams. GBS’s priorities are set through the direction of Stripe leadership and executive vision, partnership with sales and cross-functional organizations, as well as User feedback and market insights. This role sits within Global Business Practices’ Commercial Solutions team, responsible for developing, launching, and maintaining commercial constructs and programs to drive revenue for Stripe.

What you’ll do

Stripe’s Global Business Services’ Commercial Solutions team is looking for a Commercial Solutions Program Manager to own the end-to-end programmatic development of commercial and GBS launch readiness programs that drive revenue for Stripe. Programs have a large scope and/or impact in nature, including owning the development and support of first-of-its-kind commercialization efforts, ongoing program support (pre to post-launch), custom deal support related to the program, ownership of related enablement and communications, as well as acting as a change agent across the business.

You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of commercial and/or GBS launch readiness programs, driving cross-organizational alignment through the delivery of related outputs. This role requires a background in program management and commercial program experience, change management, a strong understanding of and experience in scaling global, cross-organizational mechanisms.

The candidate will have experience in program ownership and management, custom pricing strategies, and a background in supporting selling motions. The candidate will have strong communication skills and executive presence to effectively communicate with Stripes from sellers and Deal Strategies through to senior leadership. You will love this job if you are a natural relationship and mechanism builder.

Responsibilities

• Independently lead large scale, cross-functional commercial or GBS launch readiness programs that have Stripe-wide impact, often first-of-their-kind programs and initiatives

• Manage and lead a highly complex program/s which require considerable resources and high levels of complex functional and technical integration and knowledge

• Support the commercial program deal motion, partnering with Deal Pricing and/or Deal Strategy Strategists, sellers, and internal stakeholders to create custom commercial approaches

• Work cross-functionally with sales teams, sales leaders, services/support teams, product teams, and cross-functional teams to develop, launch, and scale the commercial program (continuously evolving the ways Stripe goes to market) to support commercialization efforts

• Identify, surface, and action systemic, broad issues and gaps, proposing holistic solutions to address root causes

• Navigate, and propose creative solutions, through complex programmatic problems at scale across Go-To-Market and Stripe

• Partner with cross-functional teams such as Legal, Finance, Accounting, Service Teams, Product Teams, etc to resolve and remove internal blockers

• Act as liaison within Sales, Deal Pricing and Deal Strategy Strategists, and other stakeholders for custom elements

• Facilitate meetings, working sessions, and exercises that assist the leadership team in optimizing effectiveness amongst themselves and across the organization in general

• Advocate on behalf of a position and quickly gain cross-functional alignment on the position

• Quickly build credibility and trust with internal stakeholders

• Lead projects to solve existing commercialization issues

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

• BA/BS degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or Economics

• 10+ years of experience in program management/commercial strategy/economics/deal management/pricing with experience owning program strategy or business operations

• 5+ years of direct commercial pricing model program management skills/knowledge/experience/deal management, and/or oversight

• Experience driving cross-team mechanism development end to end (ideation, planning, execution, launch, post-launch support)

• Experience working in ambiguous, quickly scaling environments, comfortable with high-agency

• Experience engaging with senior executives on high priority initiatives, as well as the ability to work effectively across internal and external organizations

• Be able to articulate and understand business strategy at the C-Suite level to gain credibility and advise organizations on how best to achieve their business goals through the use of commercial programs

• Strong written and verbal communication, presentation, negotiation, and project management skills

• Establish credibility and maintain working relationships with internal stakeholders involved with commercial constructs (Legal, Finance, Accounting, etc.)

• Experience presenting data and metrics to senior leadership to report on metrics

• Strong ability to advocate for a position even in the face of pushback

Preferred qualifications

• Direct commercial construct launch oversight and experience

• Payments industry experience

• MBA degree in Business, Technology, Finance, or Economics

• Possess PgMP or PMP certification

jobs.title: Senior Growth Marketing Lead
jobs.description:
About Fora

Fora is the modern travel agency, empowering the next generation of entrepreneurs to build thriving travel advisory businesses. We're modernizing the $100B+ travel industry with AI woven through every part of the advisor's workflow, plus global supplier relationships, personalized training, and a vibrant community, all in one place. That's what lets advisors build businesses that scale, while their taste and service create trips no algorithm alone could plan. At the heart of it all is our mission: to help the next generation of travel entrepreneurs turn their love for travel into a fulfilling career, whether full-time or part-time.

We're mission-driven and obsessed with our customers, and we believe humans and AI are both essential: the best work here comes from people and technology at their best, together. That's not just a philosophy about our product, it's how we build our team. Everyone at Fora gets hands-on with frontier AI tooling as part of the job. At Fora, you'll learn to be AI-fluent, with real experience applying AI to solve problems day to day, wherever you sit in the company.

Founded in 2021, Fora has grown to a team of 250+ full-time employees based in downtown New York City. In 2026, we closed a $60 million Series D led by Forerunner and Tactile Ventures, with continued backing from Thrive Capital, Insight Partners, and Heartcore Capital. We've been named a LinkedIn Top Startup (2024), one of Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies (2023 and 2025), and one of TIME's 100 Most Influential Companies (2026).

Come build something that hasn't existed before.

About The Role

Most of Fora's advisor acquisition comes from Meta and Google today. Our next stage of growth will come from channels we haven't found or scaled yet. You'll help find them. For the channels you own, there's no playbook. You'll write it. Advisor acquisition is the starting focus. As you prove out wins, the role can expand into other growth areas across the business.

This is a player-coach role. You'll shape acquisition strategy with our growth leadership team, then run with it for the channels you own: launch the tests yourself, read the results, and decide what to scale, fix, or kill. Then you'll do it again, faster. We goal on advisors who go on to book meaningful, repeat travel, not on raw signups.

Experimentation is in your DNA. Every idea is a hypothesis, every launch is a test, and every result makes the next test better. You're never satisfied with the status quo, including your own last win.

You'll partner with Data, Creative, Product, and Site & Conversion. Most of them won't report to you, so this role runs on clarity, data, and a strong point of view. You'll be the go-to expert on experimentation and work directly with senior leaders. AI is core to how you work: you'll use it to research, build creative, analyze results, and automate the work that slows the team down.

Fora is growing fast, and growing our advisor base is one of the company's top priorities. If you're a self-starter who wants to move fast and grow your career, there's a lot of room to grow here. As the work outgrows one person, you'll help shape and build the team.

Key Responsibilities

• Shape the strategy, then own your part of it. Bring a strong point of view to acquisition strategy alongside growth leadership. Own the roadmap for your channels, partnerships, and growth bets: what to test first, how much to invest, and when to scale.

• Launch it yourself. Get hands-on with the campaigns, briefs, budgets, and platforms. Take channels from first test to sustained investment.

• Run the experimentation engine. Every test has a hypothesis, success metrics, a decision date, and predefined criteria to scale, iterate, or kill. Increase test velocity every quarter.

• Prove incrementality. Partner with Data on holdouts, geo tests, and matched-market tests. Make investment calls on incremental impact, LTV, and CAC, not platform attribution.

• Iterate on creative, offers, and landing pages. Partner with Creative and Site & Conversion to test channel-specific assets, offers, and pages. Own the test plan, the read, and the recommendation.

• Run the operating cadence. Own daily pacing, weekly scorecards, and monthly cohort and channel reviews. Bring a clear point of view on what to do next.

• Build with AI. Build and run agents and automations for reporting, research, creative analysis, and performance monitoring that stay in use.

• Raise the bar. Define the testing best practices the team follows and be the go-to expert on experimentation. Mentor others and direct the work of partners and agencies. Help shape the team and the role's scope as the work grows

Requirements

• 8+ years in growth or performance marketing at a consumer, marketplace, or technology company

• Has owned acquisition strategy for a channel or portfolio, not just execution, and set its budget and goals

• Has taken at least one new acquisition channel from first test to scaled, sustained investment

• Has built and run a structured experimentation program, and can walk us through specific tests: the hypothesis, the result, and what changed because of it

• Has designed or run incrementality tests (holdouts, geo, or matched market)

• Has owned or reported on CAC, LTV, and ROAS for a funnel, and optimized for quality over volume

• Can name the AI tools in your current workflow and an agent or automation you built that is still in use

• Has coached or mentored other marketers, or set the standards a team works to

• Has led high-visibility, cross-functional initiatives and influenced senior leaders without direct authority

• Moves fast and works independently in ambiguous, fast-changing environments

Strongly Preferred

• Experience acquiring supply-side participants (partners, creators, sellers, or affiliates) in a two-sided marketplace

• Experience across offline or non-traditional channels (podcast, OOH, affiliate, creator, partnerships)

• Experience bringing work in-house from agencies

• Experience at a high-growth startup through a period of rapid scale

Compensation

Compensation for this role varies based on experience, with an indicative range of $165K–$205K base salary + equity.

• Unlimited vacation

• Health Insurance (including an option completely covered by Fora HQ)

• Dental & Vision Insurance

• Wellhub Memberships

• 401k plan with company match

• Commuter Benefits

• Supplemental Life Insurance

• Stock Options

This role can be based in our New York City office or remote within the U.S. Remote team members travel to the NYC office as needed.

Our Values

We’re forging our own path

Fora has always been about driving change within the industry. We’re not interested in maintaining the status quo.

We’re stronger together

Community is our cornerstone and collective power is our strength. We believe we can all go further when we operate together, using our combined leverage to unlock better opportunities and outcomes for our advisors, partners, and travelers.

We believe in technology

We believe technology is an answer to some of the most fundamental challenges the travel industry faces. We believe advancements in AI, bold investments in our platforms, and a world-class data infrastructure will transform the work of our advisors and our partners, while creating better travel experiences for travelers.

We’re here to serve

We operate in service of our community and believe that when they’re empowered to focus on what they do best, we all win. It’s why we relentlessly advocate for our advisors and prioritize their best interest every step of the way.

We mean business

Fora is equal parts fun, meaningful work and serious travel business. We’re unlocking opportunities for thousands of travel entrepreneurs, delivering a stream of high-quality guests at scale for our partners, and providing a superior travel experience for our travelers. It’s a better equation for the future of our industry.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

Authorization to work in the United States is required for full-time roles based in our New York City office. Fora is unable to sponsor or assist with U.S. work authorization. Roles based outside of the United States are not subject to this requirement.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Fora is committed to an equitable hiring process and an inclusive work environment. BIPOC and traditionally underrepresented candidates are strongly encouraged to apply. We will not discriminate and will take action to ensure against discrimination in employment, recruitment, advertisements for employment, compensation, termination, upgrading, promotions, and other conditions of employment against any employee or job applicant on the bases of race, color, gender, national origin, age, religion, creed, disability, veteran's status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression or any other characteristic protected by law.
