jobs.title: Staff Data Scientist, Marketing Analytics
jobs.description:
About the role

When people sign up for Chime, we want to know which marketing efforts brought them in and which ones brought in members who stay and use their account. You will set the direction for how Chime answers that question.

You will be the senior analytics leader for paid marketing. You will decide how we measure a very large paid media budget and how that measurement turns into spending decisions. This is a high-visibility role. Marketing, Growth, Finance and executive leaders will treat your work as the main reference for how marketing performs. You will join the Marketing Analytics team and work across Marketing, Finance, Data Engineering and Data Science/ML.

In this role, you can expect to

• Own the paid performance story. Track spend and results across channels every week. Explain why numbers moved, in plain words that a non-analyst can act on.

• Measure new-member offers. Show whether our sign-up offers bring in better members and whether they are worth the cost. Compare offer groups against fair, matched groups.

• Set the bar for experiments and offers. Define how tests are designed and read, and how we decide whether sign-up offers are worth the cost.

• Improve how we give credit to marketing channels. Find where our attribution rules fall short, propose better ones, and work with Data Engineering to build and maintain them.

• Turn marketing mix modeling into budget advice. Use the output of our Marketing Mix Model to advise Marketing on how to allocate budget across channels.

• Help plan the work ahead. Estimate the likely impact of new marketing ideas so the team can prioritize.

• Use AI to work faster and go deeper. Use AI tools to speed up analysis, check your work, and build things others can reuse.

• Raise the level of the team. Coach senior data scientists, guide contractors and set the quality bar for high-stakes work.

To thrive in this role, you have

• A Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years of experience in analytics or data science, with deep experience in marketing, growth or consumer products

• A track record of setting measurement strategy across several teams, not only delivering analyses within one team

• Deep expertise in marketing measurement: attribution, incrementality, MMM, cost per acquisition and LTV:CAC, including designing these systems from scratch

• Expert-level experimentation and causal inference skills, including knowing when standard methods don’t fit and building approaches that do

• Strong SQL and experience shaping data models and pipelines in large data warehouses (we use Snowflake)

• Advanced Python or a similar language for analysis

• Experience using Marketing Mix Model output to guide budget decisions at significant scale

• Hands-on experience bringing AI tools into analytics work for a team, and good judgment about their limits

• A history of influencing VP-level and executive decisions without formal authority, including settling disagreements between competing stakeholders

• Clear writing and speaking for senior, non-technical audiences

• A track record of growing other senior data scientists’ skills through mentorship, frameworks and shared tools

• Comfort with problems that have no precedent, where you have to define both the question and the approach

jobs.title: Production Planner (Supply)
jobs.description:
CHAOS Industries is redefining modern defense with a multi-product portfolio that gives the ultimate advantage—domain dominance. The company's products are powered by Coherent Distributed Networks (CDN™), empowering warfighters, commercial air operators, and border protection teams to act faster, adapt rapidly, and stay ahead of evolving threats.

• Own production work order release, queue management, and execution flow within radar and RF manufacturing environments.

• Serve as the coordination hub between Manufacturing Engineering (MEs), Lab Supervisors, Production Leads, and Inventory/Material Control.

• Maintain and analyze Line of Balance (LOB) to ensure production rate adherence and milestone execution.

• Ensure work orders are complete, kitted, technically valid, and configuration-controlled prior to release.

• Provide schedule visibility, risk identification, and performance reporting to Operations and Program leadership.

Responsibilities:

• Work Order Review & Release Review and release production work orders aligned to master production schedule and program milestones. Verify work order completeness, including: Correct revision levels Approved MBOM structure Routing accuracy Required documentation and traveler inclusion Ensure ECO/ECN changes are properly incorporated before release. Coordinate with Manufacturing Engineering to resolve discrepancies or missing requirements. Prevent release of incomplete or non-kitted work orders.

• Production Queue & Flow Management Interface daily with: Manufacturing Engineers Lab Supervisors Production Leads Inventory/Material Control Prioritize and sequence work orders based on: Material readiness Capacity constraints Test station availability Program deadlines Monitor WIP levels and aging. Identify and escalate bottlenecks impacting throughput or milestone delivery. Support controlled re-prioritization when program or leadership direction shifts.

• Line of Balance (LOB) Management Develop and maintain Line of Balance tracking across radar subsystem and system-level builds. Monitor build progression against planned rate and milestone commitments. Identify variance between planned vs actual production performance. Provide early warning indicators of schedule slip or capacity shortfall. Support rate ramp analysis and LRIP → FRP transition tracking.

• Work Order Schedule Reporting & Analysis Generate and maintain production schedule performance reports, including: Work order release vs plan Completion status vs required date Cycle time performance WIP aging Schedule adherence Analyze trends in: Late starts Late completions Rework-driven delays Material-driven delays Support executive and program-level reporting requirements. Ensure ERP/MES schedule data integrity.

• Kitting & Material Coordination Coordinate with Inventory and Material Control to confirm full kit availability prior to work order release. Validate shortages, substitutions, and serialized component allocation. Ensure traceability-controlled hardware is properly staged. Escalate material risks affecting Line of Balance.

• As-Built & Configuration Verification Verify accuracy of as-built documentation and traveler completion. Ensure serial number tracking, substitutions, and deviations are documented. Confirm required inspections and quality checkpoints are complete. Support configuration audits and program reviews.

• Cross-Functional Coordination Lead or support daily production scheduling reviews. Communicate schedule status, risk, and mitigation plans to Operations leadership. Coordinate rework prioritization without destabilizing production flow. Support milestone builds and surge production events.

Minimum Requirements:

• Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain, Operations Management, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience).

• 5-7+ years of experience in production scheduling, production control, or manufacturing planning.

• Experience managing work orders within ERP and/or MES systems.

• Working knowledge of: Bills of Material (BOM/MBOM) Routing structures Revision control Work order lifecycle

• Experience building and maintaining Line of Balance (LOB) tracking.

• Strong analytical capability for schedule performance reporting.

• Ability to coordinate across engineering, production, and inventory teams.

• U.S. Citizenship (if required for program access).

Preferred Requirements:

• Experience in aerospace, defense, electronics, or RF/radar production environments.

• Experience supporting LRIP or rate ramp production.

• Familiarity with: Serialized hardware tracking Engineering Change Orders (ECO/ECN) Configuration-controlled products Experience generating executive-level production performance reporting.

• Working knowledge of: Capacity planning concepts Lean manufacturing principles Production forecasting tools

• Experience with PLM systems integrated with ERP/MES.

Why CHAOS?

• Health Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision benefits 100% paid for by the company

• Additional benefits: 401k (+ 50% company match up to 6% of pay), FSA, HSA, life insurance, and more

• Our Perks: Free daily lunch while you're working onsite, fully-stocked kitchen, unlimited PTO, casual dress code

• Compensation Components: Competitive base salaries, generous pre-IPO stock option grants, relocation assistance, and (coming soon!) annual bonuses

• Team Growth: 500+ employees and counting across 5 global offices

Salary Range: $100,000-$135,000

jobs.title: Senior Director FP&A
jobs.description:
Kikoff: The Fintech Powering Financial Security at Scale
Kikoff is a profitable, pre-IPO fintech company on a mission to empower everyone to achieve financial security. With record revenue growth in 2025 and a unicorn valuation, we've built a suite of products that help millions of people build credit, access liquidity, and save money.
We're scaling fast. Join us if you want to build something meaningful and help millions of people move forward financially.

Why Kikoff:

This is a consumer fintech startup, and you will be working with serial entrepreneurs who have built strong consumer brands and innovative products. We value extreme ownership, clear communication, a strong sense of craftsmanship, and the desire to create lasting work and work relationships. Yes, you can build an exciting business AND have real-life real-customer impact.

About the Role:

As the Senior Director of FP&A, you will report to the CFO and serve as a key financial thought partner to Kikoff's leadership team as the company continues its significant and profitable growth. You will own the company's financial planning, forecasting, and analysis functions, translating complex business dynamics into actionable financial insight that drives strategic decision-making. You will work closely with the CFO and cross-functional leaders to build the financial infrastructure, analytical frameworks, and planning processes that a late-stage fintech company demands. The ideal candidate combines rigorous financial analysis with strong business instincts, an AI-first mindset, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders with clarity and confidence.

The Senior Director of FP&A will initially manage a team of 3–4, with the opportunity to grow the function as Kikoff's business continues to scale. This role is based in our San Francisco office (in office three days a week).

• Lead a team that oversees all aspects of FP&A at Kikoff

• Own Kikoff's annual operating budget, quarterly plans, weekly and daily forecasts, and long-range financial model, ensuring they reflect business realities and support strategic decision-making

• Prepare and present executive and board-level reporting packages, including the monthly financial package, board decks, KPI dashboards, and forward-looking commentary

• Build, develop, and grow a high-performing FP&A team, setting a high bar for analytical rigor, business judgment, communication, and cross-functional collaboration

• Champion the use of AI across FP&A workflows to automate routine work and speed up analysis

• Serve as a trusted financial partner to business leaders across marketing, product, engineering, risk, and operations — translating financial data into clear guidance and actionable recommendations

• Partner with the Corporate Controller and Accounting team to ensure alignment between financial reporting and operational forecasts

• Help define the company’s key metrics and drive alignment and adoption in close partnership with our Data team

• Build and maintain financial models that capture unit economics, customer acquisition and retention, cohort dynamics, and revenue drivers specific to Kikoff's businesses

• Lead scenario planning and sensitivity analysis to support strategic initiatives, new product launches, and capital allocation decisions

• Own the selection and development of Kikoff's planning systems and financial infrastructure, driving adoption of best-in-class tools and processes

• Support fundraising, investor relations, and M&A processes as needed, including preparation of investor materials and financial due diligence

About You:

• 15+ years of experience in FP&A, investment banking, or a related financial discipline, with significant operating experience at a high-growth company

• Background at a late-stage or public fintech, e-commerce, marketplace, or internet company with high transaction volumes preferred

• Demonstrated track record of financial leadership at a late-stage private or newly public company strongly valued

• AI-first mindset with a track record of driving cross-functional adoption of AI tools in financial analysis and planning workflows

• Experience with modern planning systems: Adaptive Planning, Anaplan, or comparable tools; ability to own the roadmap and optimization of Kikoff's planning infrastructure

• Demonstrated ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear, compelling narratives for executive and board audiences

• Expert financial modeler with deep experience building driver-based models that capture unit economics, cohort behavior, and multi-product revenue dynamics

• Comfortable operating as a player-coach - willing to roll up your sleeves on detailed analysis and models while managing and developing a growing team

• Strong business acumen, intellectual curiosity, and a track record of building credibility and trust with senior cross-functional stakeholders

📈 Meaningful equity in the form of RSU's

🏝️ 20 days of paid time off per year — we encourage taking real time away to recharge and do your best work

💵 401(k) plan with an employer match to help you invest in your future

jobs.title: Sales Development Manager
jobs.description:
Develop Health is on a mission to use AI to radically accelerate access to life-saving medications. By automating complex, manual healthcare processes—like benefit verification and prior authorization— we've been growing rapidly and over the past couple of years have helped over 2.5 million patients!

We’re partnering with some of the largest pharmacy benefit managers and payers in the nation, revolutionizing how healthcare interactions occur by eliminating human delays and inefficiencies. Our small, elite team of founders and engineers have previously launched and exited successful healthcare startups including Rupa Health and Canvas Medical. We are now scaling rapidly following a major funding round.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're hiring a Sales Development Manager to run the team that calls provider offices on behalf of the pharmacies we work with.

When a pharmacy sends us a prescription that needs a prior authorization, we usually need something from the prescriber's office first, most often the clinical notes. Many of those offices have never heard of us. Our calling team reaches them by phone, gets the request to the person who handles prior authorizations, and returns their callbacks. Whether that call happens quickly and gets a response often decides whether a patient starts their medication this week or next.

You'll run that team, reporting to our Head of Provider Growth (to our CEO until that role is filled). It's small today, and it works in a calling tool our engineers built and keep improving. You'll own how much calling capacity we have, how fast calls and callbacks happen, and how many offices respond.

Three things define success in this role:

 1. You own speed and capacity. Calling tasks get worked while they still matter, and callbacks are returned the same day. You know how many calls the team can make, how many we need, and when to hire.

 2. You own the response rate on calls. You know how often we reach someone, how often they respond, and why calls fail (wrong number, voicemail, wrong desk). You change scripts, timing, and process to move those numbers.

 3. You make the tooling better. You work in the calling tool every day and turn what you see into specific, prioritized asks for our engineers.

You don't need a healthcare background, but you do need to pick up a complex domain quickly. Startup experience is a strong plus.

This role will be based in Salt Lake City, initially on a remote basis but hybrid longer-term, as we're building out a hub there. 

You'd also be working an earlier shift (7am-4pm) in order to catch East Coast prospects.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Run the team

 - Hire, train, coach, and schedule callers. Set the daily cadence, listen to calls, and give feedback.

 - Make calls yourself, especially early on.

 - Decide when to add headcount or bring in outside help, with the numbers to back it.

Run the numbers

 - Own the calling metrics: capacity against demand, time from task to first call, callback response time, reach rate, and response rate.

 - Report them weekly and explain what moved.

Improve how we call

 - Own call scripts and talking points for different kinds of offices, and test changes.

 - Work with our growth marketing lead, who owns fax, email, and messaging, so phone and digital touches work together on the same offices.

 - Work with engineering on the calling tool: what slows callers down, what data is missing, and what to fix first.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING ON DAY 1

 - You've managed an outbound calling team. SDR, inside sales, patient access, or similar, with phone as a main channel. You've hired and coached callers.

 - You run a team on numbers. Activity, speed to lead, connect rate, conversion. You can walk us through a metric you moved and how.

 - You're good on the phone. You can get past a front desk politely and get a busy office to act.

 - You build process. You've fixed a queue, written a playbook, or set up a workflow in a CRM or dialer, and given useful feedback to whoever built the tool.

 - Quantitative fluency. You can break a funnel into its steps and tell which one is broken.

 - Fast and self-directed. You take direction well, then run with it.




WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO LEARN QUICKLY

 - Our domain: prior authorization and medication access, and what a provider office needs from us to complete a request.

 - How a provider office works: who answers the phone, who handles prior authorizations, and who to ask for.

 - The rules: what HIPAA allows on a call, and with whom.




BONUS POINTS

 - Phone outreach in healthcare: specialty pharmacy, hub services, revenue cycle, or a medical office.

 - Early hire at a high-growth or early-stage startup.

 - Experience with AI voice agents or modern dialer tooling.




THIS MIGHT NOT BE THE RIGHT FIT IF

 - You want to manage managers or a large org right away. This is a small team you'll build.

 - You'd rather not make calls yourself. You will, especially early.

 - You need polished process and tools on day one. Building them is part of the job.

 - You want to own digital channels. Fax, email, and messaging belong to our growth marketing lead. You'll share the same funnel.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive base salary plus meaningful early-stage equity.

 - Modern calling and AI tooling, built in-house and improving every week.

 - Work that directly accelerates access to medication for hundreds of thousands of patients, with room to grow as the team scales.

Whoever you are, wherever you’re from, whoever you love or follow in faith, whatever your disability or superpower status, whichever ethnicity or gender you identify with, you are welcome at SanMar.

SanMar participates in E-Verify.

 1. You work the queue fast. New calling tasks get a first dial within a business day, and callbacks are returned the same day.

 2. Offices respond. You reach the right person and get a commitment more often than not, and your response rate goes up as you learn.

jobs.title: Head of Design
jobs.description:
Introducing Moonlake, AI for creating world simulations.


ABOUT MOONLAKE

Moonlake is building the frontier of interactive world models: systems that generate, simulate, and reason over 3D environments for embodied AI, robotics and gaming. We develop the simulation infrastructure to build worlds (e.g., assets, scenes, digital twins) at scale.

Our team sits at the intersection of:

 - Embodied AI

 - Robotics simulation

 - Interactive 3D worlds

 - World models

 - Real-time generation

 - AI infrastructure

Moonlake is building the next generation of AI infrastructure for interactive digital worlds. Our mission is to enable anyone to create, simulate, and interact with rich environments using natural language and multimodal inputs, turning simple ideas into worlds with structure, logic, and agents that can perceive and act.

Our team has raised $28M in seed funding from NVIDIA Ventures, Threshold Ventures, AIX ventures and notable angels including Naval Ravikant and Jeff Dean to build the foundational layer for the future of AI - powering everything from robotics training, simulations, and digital twins. Our goal is to make building and experimenting with these environments as accessible and scalable as publishing video on the internet.

We are looking for exceptional research engineers and applied researchers to help push the frontier of interactive AI.


THE ROLE

We're looking for an exceptional Head of Design to shape the future of how people interact with AI-generated worlds. This is a rare opportunity to define the user experience for a new category of software at the intersection of AI, simulation, and creative tooling.

You'll work closely with researchers and engineers to translate cutting-edge AI capabilities into intuitive, elegant, and highly interactive product experiences. From rapid prototyping to polished production features, you'll own the end-to-end design and implementation of products that make complex AI systems feel simple and delightful.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build intuitive user experiences for AI-powered creative and simulation tools.

 - Rapidly prototype new product concepts from idea to working implementation.

 - Collaborate closely with AI researchers and engineers to bring frontier capabilities into production.

 - Own product features end-to-end, from interaction design and frontend architecture to implementation.

 - Build interfaces that simplify complex workflows across world generation, simulation, and multimodal AI.

 - Continuously refine the product through user feedback, experimentation, and iteration.

 - Help establish the design language and product direction for an entirely new category of AI software.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Exceptional product intuition with a passion for crafting polished user experiences.

 - Strong frontend engineering experience with modern web technologies such as React, Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.

 - Experience designing and building products from zero to one.

 - Ability to rapidly prototype ideas and iterate with minimal direction.

 - Strong visual design skills with meticulous attention to detail.

 - Comfort working across design, product, and engineering disciplines.

 - Experience with AI products, creative tools, developer platforms, or simulation software is a plus.


WHY THIS MATTERS

The interface is the product. As AI systems become increasingly capable, the challenge is no longer just building better models—it's making those capabilities intuitive, accessible, and effortless to use. At Moonlake, you'll define how researchers, developers, and creators interact with the next generation of AI infrastructure for simulation and Physical AI. Your work won't just improve the user experience; it will shape how entirely new categories of AI products are discovered, understood, and adopted.

We are committed to being an on-site, in-person team currently based in San Francisco.

jobs.title: 3D Art Intern [Spring 2027]
jobs.description:
Crystal Dynamics is constantly seeking the best gaming talent worldwide to add to our 30-plus year legacy of game development creating new and iconic franchises. We are committed to making great games with great people and living the dream while doing it.

Benefits for our regular full-time positions include, but are not limited to, a competitive regional salary, 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision insurance options, professional development reimbursement, flexible hybrid on-site/off-site work opportunities, company paid holidays, plus additional paid days in December when the studio is closed for holiday break, and the ability to accrue additional paid time-off.

Join us and help shape an amazing studio culture, where we’re building award-winning franchises like Tomb Raider and more!

Crystal Dynamics is now accepting applications for a remote spring internship, open to candidates across most U.S. states. As part of this 12-week program, you will take part in meaningful, hands-on work that contributes directly to active AAA projects. Throughout the program, you will step into a professional development environment where ongoing projects, experienced mentors, and collaborative teams give you a direct view into AAA game creation. This internship is designed to help you build industry ready skills, form strong professional relationships, and deepen your understanding of how world class games are made!

Eligibility Criteria:

• Graduated from a college or university program in 2026 (Spring, Summer, Fall, or Winter).

• Degree in Animation, Art, Game Art, Technical Art, Game Design, Game Development, Engineering, or related fields.

• Availability to work full-time (40 hrs / week), during core business hours, for the duration of the program (February 1st – April 23rd, 2027), including the first week onsite at our studio in San Carlos, CA for onboarding.

• Legal eligibility to work in the United States.

• Submission of a complete application that includes a resume, cover letter, and a link to your portfolio.

What You Will Gain:

• Practical Project Involvement: Contribute to active game development efforts while learning production scope, workflows, and the advanced tools used across modern AAA pipelines.

• Professional Mentorship: Receive guidance from experienced professionals with deep industry knowledge.

• Skill Development: Expand your skill set, establishing a solid foundation for your professional journey.

• Team Collaboration: Work alongside our dedicated onsite and remote teams including fellow interns, building valuable professional relationships within the gaming industry.

What You Will Do:

• Acquire essential skills using industry-standard tools and software such as Unreal Engine, ZBrush, Blender, and Substance Painter/Designer.

• Participate in various aspects of the 3D art pipeline including modeling, sculpting, UVs, texturing, material creation, mesh optimization, and in-engine implementation.

• Assist with world building, set dressing, and environment creation within Unreal Engine.

• Support mid, senior, and lead artists by polishing existing assets, helping fix issues, and contributing to a variety of art production tasks as assigned.

• Enhance your understanding of advanced game development technology, focusing on Unreal Engine 5.

What Makes You Stand Out:

• Portfolio demonstrating foundational environment art skills, including one or more of the following: 3D art examples showing strong perspective, composition, mood, lighting, and material definition. Understanding of color theory and PBR.

• Industry involvement outside classroom curriculum such as game jams, personal projects and/or contributions to group projects that show going above and beyond.

• Exposure to industry-standard development software tools and engines.

• Willingness to tackle challenges, learn from feedback, and adapt to new tools or workflows.

• Ability to communicate your ideas with eagerness to learn and put feedback into action.

Compensation & Benefits:
Compensation for this internship is $20-23/hr. Compensation is location-based and will be aligned to the intern’s confirmed work location during the program. Interns are also eligible for a medical, dental, and vision benefits package. Your recruiter can provide more information about total compensation.

Your recruiter will be able to share more information about total compensation.

jobs.title: Research Associate I/II, Cloning/IVT (Contract)
jobs.description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Founded through Flagship Pioneering’s venture creation engine, Terrana Biosciences is a cutting-edge agricultural biotechnology company developing innovative RNA-based products to address global agricultural challenges. We are committed to advancing sustainable farming solutions through precision technologies that ensure environmental safety and regulatory compliance.

THE ROLE

Terrana Biosciences is building a new generation of RNA-based technologies to transform agriculture. We are seeking a Research Associate I to join our IVT Production team and support the generation of high-quality RNA materials that enable discovery, platform development, and product advancement across the company.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Execute DNA assembly and molecular cloning workflows to generate constructs supporting research and RNA production.

• Perform bacterial transformation, colony screening, plasmid preparation, and sequence verification to identify and confirm successful constructs.

• Execute in vitro transcription (IVT) workflows to produce RNA supporting research and development programs.

• Perform RNA synthesis, purification, quantification, and quality control using established laboratory methods.

• Prepare DNA templates, reagents, and materials required for IVT production workflows.

• Conduct routine molecular biology techniques including PCR, gel electrophoresis, and nucleic acid quantification.

• Maintain accurate experimental records and track samples using electronic laboratory systems.

• Support high-throughput RNA production operations while ensuring quality, reproducibility, and timely delivery.

• Contribute to workflow optimization, process improvements, and laboratory organization.

• Collaborate with Molecular Biology, Discovery, Sequencing, and Bioinformatics teams to support project objectives.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS

Required

• B.S. or M.S. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Genetics, or a related field. RA I: B.S. Degree and up to 2 years of relevant laboratory experience in academic or industry settings RA II: B.S. Degree and 2–4 years or M.S. and up to 2 years of relevant laboratory experience in academic or industry settings

• Experience with basic molecular biology techniques, including PCR, nucleic acid handling, and gel electrophoresis.

• Strong attention to detail, organization, and record-keeping skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, fast-paced environment.

Preferred

• Experience with RNA handling, in vitro transcription, or nucleic acid purification workflows.

• Familiarity with high-throughput laboratory operations, automation platforms, or LIMS systems.

• Experience in synthetic biology, RNA biology, or agricultural biotechnology.

Location: Cambridge, MA

ABOUT FLAGSHIP PIONEERING:

Flagship Pioneering invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health, sustainability and beyond. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated more than 100 companies. Many of these companies have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com.

At Flagship, we accept impossible missions to enable bigger leaps. Our core values guide us through uncertainty and toward lasting impact.

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We recognize that great candidates often bring unique strengths without fulfilling every qualification. If you have some of the experience listed above but not all, please apply anyway. We are dedicated to building diverse and inclusive teams and look forward to learning more about your background and interest in Flagship.

Recruitment & Staffing Agencies: Flagship Pioneering and its affiliated Flagship Lab companies (collectively, “FSP”) do not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to FSP or its employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Flagship Pioneering’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of FSP, and FSP will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

#LI-TL1

The pay range for this role is $31 - $45 per hour and the contractor will be employed by a third-party staffing company. Certain employee benefits may be available to the contractor through the staffing company after meeting minimum criteria. Compensation and benefits information is based on Terrana Biosciences, Inc.'s good faith estimate as of the date of publication and may be modified in the future.

Your application data is processed through Greenhouse, our applicant tracking system, and may also be reviewed using AI-assisted screening tools. We do not sell your personal information. California residents have rights under the CCPA/CPRA including to know, delete, and opt out of the sharing of their personal information. jobs.title: Plant Security Officer Lead
jobs.description:
Nestled in San Francisco's Excelsior neighborhood on a nine-acre campus, the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL) is the leading senior services organization in Northern California. Our continuum of care includes: the Frank Residences assisted living and memory care; the Jewish Home and Rehabilitation Center, offering long-term skilled nursing, short-term rehabilitation, an acute geriatric psychiatric unit for adults over the age of 65; and our Foundation.

Founded in 1871 and formerly known as the Jewish Home, our legacy grounds us as our vision propels us forward. Today, we've evolved to support more than 2,500 older adults each year through innovative, comprehensive programs rooted in the Jewish values of compassion, community, and excellence. We are equally proud of our inclusive culture, where 950 team members of diverse faiths and backgrounds work together in shared purpose.

WHY WORK WITH US

• Mission-driven nonprofit organization

• Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

• Meaningful work that positively impacts the lives of older adults every day

• Inclusive community, welcoming to all (you do not need to be Jewish to live or work here)

• Supportive, team-oriented environment

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

• Collaborative leadership focused on enhancing the employee experience

POSITION SUMMARY

As the Lead Security Supervisor, you will assist the Security Manager in overseeing security operations across the San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living (SFCJL), including the Jewish Home & Rehab Center (JHRC) and Frank Residences. You will support the safety and protection of residents, visitors, staff, and property while helping maintain a secure environment against potential threats, including fire, theft, vandalism, and other emergencies. This role provides direct supervision of security personnel and plays a key role in daily security operations, staff scheduling and development, incident response and investigations, emergency preparedness, access control, and security training.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

• Assist with the development and implementation of security policies, procedures, and training programs.
• Supervise all Shift Supervisors and Plant Security Guards.
• Oversee daily security operations, ensuring compliance with established protocols and providing immediate support during emergency situations.
• Manage the security staff schedule and ensure adequate staffing levels are maintained at all times.
• Conduct security training and oversee ongoing staff development.
• Complete and deliver annual performance evaluations for direct reports, including salary recommendations and performance improvement plans as appropriate.
• Conduct interviews and coordinate orientation for new security staff.
• Ensure security personnel accurately complete Daily Activity Reports (DARs) and Supplemental Security Reports.
• Assist with preparing and delivering monthly fire drill training, including practical demonstrations of fire extinguisher use and emergency exit procedures.
• Coordinate facility-wide security drills and emergency action planning.
• Provide support during security incidents and ensure responses are consistent with campus security policies and procedures.
• Provide after-hours support to security personnel as needed.
• Oversee the employee, visitor, and resident badge program, ensuring appropriate access and troubleshooting issues involving access control systems.
• Work closely with the Security Manager and other departments to ensure security and safety protocols are followed consistently.
• Collaborate with law enforcement, emergency services, and other external partners to maintain campus safety and security standards.
• Conduct regular audits of security operations and identify and implement improvements as necessary.
• Participate in meetings, seminars, and workshops related to safety and security management.
• Provide operational support to the Facilities team as needed.
• Perform other duties as assigned to maintain a safe and secure campus environment.

JOB DETAILS

• Pay Rate: $90,000 - $99,000 Annually
• Hours: Full-Time, Exempt
• Shift Schedule: 11:30 AM - 8:00 PM
• Days Off: Friday & Saturday
• Working Days: Sunday through Thursday

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• High school diploma or GED required.
• Minimum of two (2) to three (3) years of experience as a Security Supervisor or in a comparable security role.
• Experience with security and emergency management systems, including CCTV, card access, and visitor management systems.
• Experience conducting training and leading large training sessions.
• Demonstrated ability to lead, coach, supervise, and develop a security team.
• Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, and Excel.
• Familiarity with security management software.
• Ability to maintain confidentiality and work collaboratively in a sensitive and adaptive environment.
• Ability to interact professionally and effectively with residents, staff, families, law enforcement, emergency responders, and external partners.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Associate degree preferred.
• Previous security experience in senior care, skilled nursing, healthcare, or a similar environment preferred.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

• Ability to stand and walk for extended periods while monitoring campus operations.
• Ability to move throughout campus buildings, grounds, and security posts as needed.
• Ability to respond promptly to security incidents and emergency situations.
• Ability to sit and work at a computer or security monitoring station for extended periods.
• Ability to communicate effectively in person, by telephone, and through security communication systems.
• Ability to perform the physical functions associated with security drills, emergency response, and staff training.

OUR INVESTMENT IN YOU

Comprehensive benefits, including Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage; a 403(b) Retirement Plan; Paid Time Off (PTO); Tuition Reimbursement; Commuter Benefits; and Weekday Shuttle Service to and from Glen Park BART Station.

The San Francisco Campus for Jewish Living is committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified individuals without regard to race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, genetic information, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

jobs.title: Supervisor, Fleet Maintenance
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SpaceXSI is hiring a Fleet Maintenance Supervisor for our AI supercompute facilities in Memphis. You will own fleet maintenance for automotive assets, heavy transit vehicles, trailers, UTVs, and industrial equipment. You will run the work-order schedule, cover emergency breakdowns, and occasionally do the work alongside your technicians.

This role requires 24/7 on-call coverage for critical breakdowns, and may include nights, weekends, and long hours with limited notice.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead technicians through daily repairs, preventative maintenance, and continuous improvement projects, to increase uptime and ensure maximum asset availability across our Memphis facilities

• Set the weekly plan, assign work, and triage requests from internal customers by priority and available resources.

• Source third-party vendors for parts acquisition, documentation, training, and on-site repairs as needed

• Be the subject matter expert for all things related to the fleet

• Provide developmental leadership to technicians, facilitating training and advancement of skills

• Track team utilization and the maintenance KPIs used to improve uptime

• Facilitate all Title and Registration needs for the fleet

• Oversee the lifecycle of all fleet assets from acquisition through disposition

• Perform other related duties, as assigned, to ensure smooth operation of the fleet maintenance team

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalent.

• Functional knowledge of mechanical, electrical, hydraulic and pneumatic systems

• 4+ years maintaining or repairing vehicles, fleet equipment, or industrial equipment.

• 2+ years leading people, including assigning work and running maintenance jobs to completion.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or completion of a related trade school

• ASE/OEM certifications

• Proficiency in Microsoft applications such as Excel, Outlook, Word, and PowerPoint

• Experience in a CMMS or other asset-management system

• Experience managing a maintenance budget, third-party vendors, and service contracts

• Ability to work independently with little direction

• Ability to meet deadlines in a fast-paced, ever-changing priorities environment

• Ability to anticipate needs and develop innovative solutions

• Ability to effectively communicate (verbal and written) with engineering, production, build, and support teams

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Ability to lift 50 lbs. unassisted, lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position

• Must be willing to work at elevated heights and in tight spaces

• Must be willing to work long hours, nights, and weekends with limited notice to meet the business needs

• Provide 24/7 on-call support for all critical activities and emergency situations

• Willingness to travel to support the business

SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Director, Touring
jobs.description:
For more than 20 years, AEG has played a pivotal role in transforming sports and live entertainment. Annually, we host more than 160 million guests, promote more than 10,000 shows and present more than 22,000 events around the world. We are committed to innovation, artistry, and community, and leverage the power of our 300+ venues, leading sports franchises, marquee music brands, integrated entertainment districts, premier ticketing platform and global sponsorship activations, to create memorable moments that give the world reason to cheer.

Our business is interwoven with the human mind and heart, and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive company that reflects the artists, athletes, and fans that we host; reach beyond traditional boundaries to support the communities in which we operate; and minimize our impact on the environment by adopting sustainable practices throughout our business operations.

If you want to be challenged to up your game and make a difference, then join us in giving the world reason to cheer!

Position Summary:

As a Director Touring, you will undertake the pivotal role of overseeing the management of multiple tours, with a focus on operations from the promoter's standpoint. This entails strategic planning, logistical coordination, and ensuring seamless execution to meet touring team and clients objectives. Lead and closely collaborate with the touring department, overseeing various projects such as developing and evaluating financial models, as well as preparing tour offers for theaters, arenas, and stadiums at a directorial level.

Essential Functions:

• Lead and review ticket sales, holds, and other appropriate ticketing items for assigned tours, working with tour ticketing director to manage these items.

• Oversee and work directly with various departments (i.e. marketing, operations, ticketing, production, legal) on overall aspects for assigned tours.

• Guide and closely collaborate with the touring department, overseeing various projects such as developing and evaluating financial models, as well as preparing tour offers for theaters, arenas, and stadiums at a directorial level.

• Negotiate venue deals for each tour at the theater, arena and stadium level. Maintain regular communication with client representatives for each assigned tour.

• May focus on developing strategies to expand AEG’s global footprint with each artist and oversee all aspects of tour cycle – Offer Creation, Contracting, On Sale, Inventory Management, final settlement

• May be responsible for completing nightly settlements at each show as well as in addition to overall tour settlement, work to open additional ticket inventory for sales and/or day-of- show ticketing needs on site at the venue.

• May entail overseeing all tour logistics, ensuring timely dissemination of information to relevant departments to all parties, and drafting artist and venue contracts, overseeing various departments to ensure advancement of production requirements have been met.

Required Qualifications:

• BA/BS Degree (4-year)

• 6-8 years Of related work experience

• Understanding of accounting and ability to complete accurate show settlements (inclusive of working knowledge of global exchange rates)

• Understanding of and experience in touring music business both domestic and international (i.e. has worked on at least one touring project that has extended beyond North America).

• Ability to build effective working relationships with clients, venues, and co-workers

• Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook)

• Excellent written, verbal and listening communication skills

• Strong organizational skills

• Self-motivated and takes initiative

• May require heavy travel for long period of time of the road.

Pay scale: $108,244 - $165,685

jobs.title: 2027 Summer IT Infrastructure & Automation Intern
jobs.description:
The future of aerospace and defense starts here.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.

As a member of our Digital Operations team, you will have the opportunity to work alongside experienced IT professionals while gaining hands-on experience applying software engineering and automation principles to real-world IT operations.

The IT Infrastructure & Automation Intern will focus on improving the way IT operates by identifying manual, repetitive, and error-prone processes and transforming them into automated, reliable, and repeatable workflows. This role will have a strong emphasis on Infrastructure as Code (IaC), Terraform, and automation across the systems and processes managed by IT.

This may include automating infrastructure provisioning, user and access management, service desk workflows, application and device management, cloud services, and other operational processes. The goal is to reduce manual "click-ops," improve consistency, and build processes that can be reliably executed and maintained over time.

The ideal candidate is someone who enjoys solving problems, writing code, and finding better ways to accomplish repetitive tasks. They should have a foundational understanding of IT systems and programming concepts and be excited to apply those skills to enterprise IT automation.

This role will report to the IT Manager.

Responsibilities:

• Identify manual, repetitive, or error-prone IT processes that are candidates for automation

• Design and implement automation using Terraform, scripting, APIs, and other appropriate technologies

• Apply Infrastructure as Code principles to make infrastructure and IT processes reliable, repeatable, and maintainable

• Automate service desk and IT operational processes to improve efficiency and reduce manual intervention

• Develop reusable Terraform configurations and modules for common IT infrastructure and services

• Use version control, documentation, testing, and change management practices when developing automation

• Troubleshoot, improve, and maintain existing automation and infrastructure

• Partner with IT team members to understand business processes and translate them into technical solutions

• Assist with select day-to-day IT operations and projects as needed

Experience/Requirements:

• Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree, certification program, or equivalent coursework in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related technical field

• Foundational experience with IT systems, cloud platforms, systems administration, networking, or related technologies through coursework, internships, employment, labs, or personal projects

• Hands-on experience with Terraform through coursework, personal projects, labs, internships, or professional experience

• Understanding of Infrastructure as Code and basic software development concepts

• Familiarity with a scripting or programming language such as PowerShell, Python, or similar

• Familiarity with Git or another version control system

• Experience working with structured data such as JSON or YAML is preferred

• Familiarity with APIs and cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure is a plus

Critical Skills:

• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

• Ability to recognize opportunities to eliminate manual work through automation

• Ability to break complex problems into smaller, manageable components

• Strong attention to detail and an understanding of the importance of reliable, repeatable processes

• Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly

• Eagerness to learn and take ownership of technical challenges

• Demonstrated technical curiosity through coursework, internships, labs, or personal projects

What You Will Learn:

• Terraform and Infrastructure as Code in an enterprise IT environment

• Automation of IT infrastructure and service desk processes

• Cloud and identity management automation

• API-driven IT operations

• Version control and collaborative development practices

• Testing, deploying, and maintaining production automation

• Applying software engineering principles to IT operations

• Designing reliable and repeatable processes that reduce manual work

Colorado law requires us to tell you the base compensation range of this role, which is $30.00/hour, determined by your education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities. What we can’t quantify for you are the exciting challenges, supportive team, and amazing culture we enjoy.

Classification: Full-time Non-Exempt

• Paid Parental and Adoptive Leave

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Customer Success
jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

As Senior Manager of Customer Success for Justice & Corrections at Axon, you will lead a team of approximately 8–12 Customer Success Managers supporting two growing and strategically important markets.

You will be responsible for developing a high-performing team, driving product adoption and customer outcomes, and building the operating rhythms and processes needed to scale. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable coaching CSMs, meeting with customers, navigating escalations, using data to identify risk, and partnering across Axon to improve the customer experience.

Success in this role means creating a proactive, accountable, and customer-obsessed team that helps Justice and Corrections customers realize the full value of their partnership with Axon.

What You'll Do

Location: Axon Hub (Boston, Scottsdale, Seattle, Atlanta, New York, San Francisco)
Travel: Approximately 25–50%
Direct Reports: Approximately 8–12 Customer Success Managers

Lead & Develop the Team

• Lead, coach, and develop a team of Customer Success Managers across Justice and Corrections

• Set clear expectations around customer engagement, adoption, account ownership, risk management, and performance

• Establish consistent 1:1s, account reviews, performance management, and development planning

• Develop high-potential talent, address performance gaps, and help hire and onboard strong CS talent

Drive Customer Outcomes

• Coach CSMs to proactively identify adoption gaps, customer risk, and opportunities to improve customer value

Build & Scale Customer Success

• Establish consistent operating rhythms and expectations across the team

• Build and improve repeatable playbooks for onboarding, adoption, account planning, customer health, executive engagement, and escalations

• Use Salesforce, Gainsight, product usage, and other customer signals to identify trends, prioritize action, and improve outcomes

• Identify processes that create unnecessary complexity and partner across Axon to improve them

• Bring forward customer trends, risks, and opportunities that can strengthen the broader Customer Success organization

Partner Across Axon

• Build strong partnerships with Sales leaders and sellers supporting Justice and Corrections

• Partner with Sales on customer strategy, adoption, retention, risk, and opportunities to deepen relationships

• Collaborate across Product, Professional Services, Support, Operations, and other teams to solve complex customer challenges

• Represent the voice of the customer internally and translate recurring feedback into actionable insights

• Clarify ownership across teams and ensure customers receive a coordinated experience

What You Bring

• 8+ years of experience in Customer Success, Customer Experience, SaaS, account management, customer-facing operations, or a related field

• 3+ years of direct people-management experience, ideally leading Customer Success Managers or another customer-facing team

• Proven ability to coach and develop teams with varying levels of experience

• Experience building or scaling Customer Success programs, processes, playbooks, and operating rhythms

• Strong track record of partnering with Sales to drive customer and business outcomes

• Experience using data and customer signals to identify risk, prioritize accounts, and improve customer outcomes

• Ability to lead through change, challenge existing ways of working, and create structure in ambiguous environments

• Experience managing complex customer situations and escalations

• High ownership, sound judgment, curiosity, and a bias toward action

• Experience in public safety, Justice, Corrections, government technology, or another complex customer environment is a plus, but not required

jobs.title: Hospice Clinical Director (Philadelphia, PA)
jobs.description:
About Us

Ennoble Care is a mobile primary care, palliative care, and hospice service provider with patients in New York, New Jersey, Maryland, DC, Virginia, Oklahoma, Kansas, Pennsylvania, Texas, Florida, and Georgia. Ennoble Care’s clinicians go to the home of the patient, providing continuum of care for those with chronic conditions and limited mobility. Ennoble Care offers a variety of programs including, remote patient monitoring, behavioral health management, and chronic care management, to ensure that our patients receive the highest quality of care by a team they know and trust. We seek individuals who are driven to make a difference and embody our motto, “To Care is an Honor.” Join Ennoble Care today!

The Hospice Clinical Director is responsible for ensuring the coordination and management of patient care. The Hospice Clinical Director will assist the Executive Director in maintaining the quality of patient care in accordance with the Agency’s objectives and policies, through planning, coordination, implementation and evaluation of the hospice services provided.  This market services the Philadelphia region in Pennsylvania.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITES

• Coordinate and oversee direct and indirect patient services provided by clinical personnel.

• Provide supervision and guidance to clinical staff to ensure the quality of services and maintenance of standards.

• Perform chart audits.

• Gather data for QAPI and participates in QAPI activities.

• Appraise clinical staff performance during their probationary period and annually, provides the teaching and counseling necessary to enhance the delivery of services and the professional development of nursing and health aide staff.

• Identify and evaluate patient needs and appropriateness of home care by reviewing the initial intake screening form before assignment of direct care staff. Assist with the orientation of new staff. See patients in the home setting as needed. Maintains adequate and appropriate Medical Supplies.

• Assists with orientation of new personnel as well as in-services for current staff.

• Responsible for ensuring Medicare, State and ACHC regulations are followed by all clinical staff.

• Assists the Executive Director with responsibilities as requested.

• Assume responsibility for self-development by continually striving to improve his/her Nursing/management practice through formal education, attendance at workshops and conferences, active participation in professional and related organizational meetings, and/or individual research and reading.

JOB CONDITIONS

• Position may be stressful.

• Primarily a desk job which involves minimal and occasional lifting of medical supplies and charts.

• On occasion, one may be required to bend, stoop, reach and move patient weight up to 250 pounds lift and/or carry up to 30 pounds.

• Travel is required to and from patient's home when supervision of care is scheduled.

• The ability to access patients’ homes which may not be routinely wheelchair accessible is required.

• Hearing, eyesight and physical dexterity must be sufficient to perform a physical assessment of the patient's condition and to perform patient care.

• Use of computer, multi- line telephone, calculator, copier, and other office and medical equipment.

COMPANY INFORMATION

• Has access to all patient medical records and patient financial accounts as well as personnel records of department staff.

QUALIFICATIONS

• Must be a graduate of an accredited School of Nursing.

• Must be a Registered Nurse licensed by the state of Pennsylvania.

• Must have a minimum of 2 years nursing experience in home hospice or skilled home care (hospice preferred).

• At least one (1) year of supervisory experience.

• Ability to market and deal tactfully with customers and the community.

• Knowledge of business management, governmental regulations and ACHC standards.

• The ability to communicate well, both verbally and in writing.

• Must have the ability to demonstrate self-confidence and positive attitude toward self and others and maintain commitment and enthusiasm to goal achievement.

jobs.title: Megapack Field Technician - Memphis
jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a hands-on, safety-focused Megapack Field Technician to support the operation, maintenance, and expansion of our Megapack energy storage fleet powering SpaceXSI's AI infrastructure in Memphis. Working directly with the Energy Storage Asset Manager, you will own the low-voltage side of the fleet, support daily medium-voltage switching operations, and help manage construction and commissioning across multiple sites for one of the largest and most critical battery deployments powering AI training.

This is a full-time, onsite role based in Memphis, Tennessee, with regular travel between Memphis-area sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Own the low-voltage (LV) side of the Megapack fleet, including AC and DC LV systems, 480V auxiliary power, breakers, and LV terminations.

• Perform Megapack enable/disable, isolation, and return-to-service procedures in support of maintenance, switching, and construction activities.

• Troubleshoot Megapack-side faults and alarms in the field, gather logs, data, and photos, and drive issues to resolution with OEM field service and support engineering.

• Act as an onsite point of contact for Tesla Field Service technicians, coordinating access, isolations, and work scope to remove blockers and ensure high-quality, timely completion of work.

• Support execution of the daily medium-voltage (MV) switching plan, including de-energizing and re-energizing Megapack strings in coordination with MV electricians, testing contractors, and site operations.

• Perform and verify lockout/tagout (LOTO) and maintain switching and isolation records in accordance with site safety procedures.

• Provide day-to-day oversight of electrical and civil contractors, verifying work against drawings, specifications, and schedule.

• Perform quality checks on LV and MV terminations, installations, and repairs, and document findings for correction and closeout.

• Coordinate installation and commissioning activities for new Megapack deployments and their integration with SpaceXSI facilities.

• Build, track, and close out punch lists, performing field verification before items are closed.

• Use drawings, single-line diagrams, and project management platforms (e.g., Procore) to track RFIs, submittals, and site issues.

• Support transformer issue intake and documentation, and assist with dehumidification and environmental controls during outages and construction.

• Conduct routine site walks and inspections to identify safety, reliability, and serviceability issues before they impact operations.

• Maintain accurate records of field work, switching activity, service events, and equipment status.

• Ensure full compliance with all safety protocols, NFPA 70E requirements, manufacturer guidelines, and local regulations.

• Provide on-call support for urgent operational and maintenance issues as required.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• 3+ years of field service, commissioning, or maintenance experience on utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) or comparable power infrastructure.

• Hands-on experience with low-voltage AC/DC electrical systems, breakers, and terminations, including safe isolation and verification of energy states.

• Working knowledge of NFPA 70E, arc flash safety, and lockout/tagout procedures.

• Ability to read and work from electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, and equipment documentation.

• Strong communication and organizational skills with the ability to coordinate multiple contractors and vendors in the field.

• Comfortable working onsite in an industrial/data center and active construction environment.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Utility-scale BESS field service experience (Megapack preferred), including Megapack 2 / 2XL installation, commissioning, service, and troubleshooting.

• Experience with OEM service and diagnostic tools, firmware updates, and site controller workflows.

• Experience supporting medium-voltage switching operations, string energization, or utility/data center switching programs.

• Construction management or field engineering experience, including contractor oversight, QA/QC, punch lists, and Procore or similar platforms.

• Familiarity with pad-mount transformers, medium-voltage cable and terminations, and fire protection standards for energy storage.

• Previous experience in 24/7 operational environments with on-call responsibilities.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Position is subject to pre-employment and annual post-employment background checks.

• Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to noise, outdoor weather, and industrial conditions.

• Available to work evenings, weekends, and provide on-call support as needed for urgent operational issues and planned outages.

• Ability to lift 50+ pounds, climb, and work at heights and in confined spaces as required.

• Valid driver's license and ability to travel between Memphis-area sites.

SpaceXSI is an equal opportunity employer. For details on data processing, view our Recruitment Privacy Notice.

jobs.title: Environmental Technician
jobs.description:
AECOM has an exciting opportunity for an Environmental Technician to join our Remediation team in our Chicago, IL office.

In this role, you will primarily support remedial operations maintenance and monitoring projects at client facilities and field sites. The candidate will ideally have experience in general construction and environmental remediation/sampling and an interest in hands-on mechanical problem solving).

Typical project work includes groundwater treatment systems, in situ and ex situ remediation systems, closed landfills, construction oversight with management of contaminated soil, asbestos, and regulated waste, construction oversight of support buildings/facilities, various media sampling (groundwater, vapor, surface water, sediment, and soil), and wastewater treatment. The successful candidate will have the ability to communicate effectively with members of the project team and be able to work independently.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Performs soil, groundwater, surface water, waste, sediment, air, vapor sampling.
• Performs various operation and maintenance (O&M) and inspection of environmental remediation systems involving extraction of hydrocarbons, impacted vapor, impacted soil, and impacted groundwater.
• Uses field instruments and equipment as necessary to meet health and safety, field sampling, and O&M requirements.
• Other activities may include setting up and operating equipment, inspecting equipment and installations for compliance with specifications and maintaining proper project documentation.
• Documents all field activities and notes.
• Performs subcontractor oversight.
• Communicates effectively with project team.
• Has a high degree of health and safety awareness.
• Works within defined scopes, schedules and budgets while producing quality work.
• Maintains knowledge of sampling procedures and protocols in accordance with recognized industry standards.

Candidate must also be able to work as part of a project team comprised of AECOM staff and subcontractors. Flexibility to work on a multitude of diverse projects, a positive attitude, and commitment to workplace health and safety are imperative. Field work will be required including oversight of subcontractors.

• A valid driver's license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy
• US Citizen or US Permanent Resident.
• Ability to travel up to 90% to various job sites locally throughout the United States.

Preferred Qualifications

• Associates Degree(s) or trade certification.
• 2 years of experience in a similar capacity.
• Physically able to work in outdoor environments with uneven terrain, variable outdoor conditions including heat, cold, noise, and/or chemicals.
• Physically able to lift equipment or objects weighing 25 pounds or less.

• Aptitude for operation and maintenance of mechanical and electrical equipment.
• Experience sampling various media (groundwater, soil, vapor).
• OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER training.

• MDH Asbestos Certification (Inspector or Supervisor)
• A mature sense of professional responsibility and awareness of accepted standards of professional behavior.
• Proficient technical writing skills and ability to effectively express his or herself orally in project reviews conducted among internal staff.
• Be able to independently perform field work.
• Be able to perform contractor oversight.
• Excellent attention to Health and Safety.
• Ability to record data neatly, accurately, and legibly.
• Possess strong work ethic and problem-solving skills.
• Proficient with basic computer programs: MS Word and MS Excel.

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. jobs.title: Commercial Counsel
jobs.description:
ABOUT CROSBY

Crosby is built on a simple conviction: a great legal system is the watermark of a great society — and the best legal work comes from combining human expertise with the right technology, not replacing one with the other.

Crosby is the first AI-native law firm, helping ambitious companies like Cursor, Ramp, and Cognition sign commercial contracts faster.

Legal work is both art and science, and we're mapping the frontier between the two — codifying what can be systematized, amplifying human judgment where it matters most. That's why the right way to bring AI into law isn't to sell software and walk away. It's to own the outcome together: higher-quality work, delivered faster. We build proprietary tools and human-in-the-loop workflows that change what's possible for corporate legal teams.

Crosby was founded by Ryan (Stanford Law, Cooley, startup GC) and John (Penn, first 15 engineers at Ramp).  Help us transform one of society's most important industries.


The Role:

 - Sit at the center of modern deal-making. You’ll review and negotiate the commercial contracts that get deals to signature for companies like Cursor, Ramp, and Cognition.

 - Direct AI, don’t babysit it. You’ll orchestrate Crosby’s tooling over a contract and spend your judgment where it counts.

 - Own outcomes end-to-end and chase the small touches that turn a closed deal into one a client can’t help but tell others about at dinner.

 - This is a high-impact role for a lawyer excited to apply AI to their own practice, obsessive about quality execution, and drawn to leverage over billable hours.

What You'll Do:

 - Review and negotiate commercial contracts with speed and precision, catching the obligations, risks, and off-market terms that matter.

 - Collaborate with other Crosby legal team members to interpret contract terms and surface the anomalies and edge cases that need an expert’s read.

 - Spot inefficiencies and recurring patterns in how contracts get reviewed, and turn them into improvements that sharpen how the whole team works.

 - Help standardize and codify recurring contract types and playbooks so the team’s judgment compounds instead of resetting on every deal.

 - Partner with engineering and operations to evolve our legal service delivery model.

Who You Are:

 - 4+ years reviewing commercial contracts in private practice or in-house

 - You have impeccable attention to detail, and sound, commercial judgment. You catch buried clauses, the wrong cross-reference, and can distinguish signal from noise.

 - You hold a high bar for your own work and get restless when something could be better.

 - You embrace change and move confidently in a fast-paced, sometimes ambiguous environment.

 - You write and speak clearly, and can explain a hard call simply.

 - You’re already tinkering with AI, or excited to, and drawn to the frontier of legal work.

Benefits & Perks

 - Equity and bonus compensation

 - Flexible, generous PTO

 - Medical insurance (multiple plan options through Anthem & Cigna)

 - HSA or FSA, depending on your plan choice

 - Dental insurance

 - Vision insurance

 - One Medical membership

 - 401(k) match


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

The Fabrication & Manufacturing Manager of Projects is responsible for the safe, profitable, and timely delivery of multiple projects executed across Loenbro's fabrication and manufacturing network.
