jobs.title: GEOINT Analyst, Scams
jobs.description:
BUILD A SAFER WORLD.

TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The Scam Disruption team is TRM's tip of the spear against pig butchering syndicates, romance fraud networks, and investment scam operations that steal billions from victims each year. As a GEOINT Analyst, you’ll be the team's location specialist: finding where scam compounds are, who is operating them, and how they move, then turning that picture into intelligence law enforcement partners can act on.

 


THE IMPACT YOU WILL HAVE

 - Locate and map scam compounds, people, and devices

 - Fuse intelligence with on-chain attribution and OSINT to identify operators and controllers

 - Find the seams: pivot from a single address, IP, photo, or victim lead to the compound and the people running it

 - Partner with the Threat Intelligence Analyst (Scams Expert), the CTI Analyst, and the All-Source Lead to translate disruption strategy into targeting packages that influence law enforcement and government action
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3 to 5 years of hands-on GEOINT experience: military, IC, law enforcement, or a GEOINT/OSINT firm

 - Works beyond the government toolkit: you can get answers from open-source and commercial tools when classified systems and data aren't available

 - Creative tactical thinking — demonstrated ability to pivot from a single point to a network view, identifying operators behind operations

 - Link and pattern analysis fluency — ability to correlate disparate data sources to generate defensible target packages

 - Clear written and verbal communication: you can explain your methods, your confidence, and your own role in plain terms, and write memos, attribution write-ups, and leads that are actionable

 - AI fluency (required) — you use AI tools in your workflow, synthesizing data, drafting outputs, and accelerating analysis, with examples of how AI has impacted your work

 - Crypto experience is a plus, not a requirement — we teach on-chain tradecraft; we cannot teach the targeter's instinct

 - Familiarity with Southeast Asia scam compounds or Chinese-run criminal networks is a plus

 - Location: remote in the UK, EMEA, or US (including Washington, DC). You must already have the right to work where you're based.


ABOUT THE TEAM

 - The Scam Disruption team operates within TRM’s Blockchain Intelligence organization, alongside threat intelligence analysts, on-chain investigators, and federal partners

 - All-Source Investigators are the operational core, converting strategy and tooling into prosecutable, actionable intelligence

 - Distributed team with an async-first approach via Slack and Notion, plus structured syncs for alignment

 - High autonomy, high standards, low bureaucracy — work directly with analysts, engineers, and customers who depend on your output

 


TEAM OPERATING RHYTHMS

 - Weekly team syncs to align targeting priorities and review disruption opportunities

 - Daily async standups via Slack on active work, returns, and target packages in flight

 - Primary time zone overlap: US Eastern / Central

 - All output documented in Notion and TRM’s investigative tools

 - Surge availability expected during time-sensitive disruption windows


APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS

If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.

Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.

If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.




INTERVIEWING WITH TRM

Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.

 - Recruiter Intro: Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.

 - Hiring Manager: Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.

 - First Round: 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.

 - Final Round: Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.

 - References: Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.

 - Offer: Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.

 - Welcome to TRM: We're excited to build a safer world with you!

Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.




AI FLUENCY AT TRM

AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.

We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.

At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:

 - Accelerate repeatable workflows

 - Structure and solve problems

 - Improve output quality

 - Increase speed and leverage

You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.




LIFE AT TRM

We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.

TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.

Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.

At TRM, you should expect:

 - Priorities and targets to change quickly

 - Operating with a high degree of ambiguity

 - A high level of personal ownership and accountability

 - Close collaboration across teams and functions

 - Frequent, high-touch communication

 - Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking

 - A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes

This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.

We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.

If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute. 




LEADERSHIP PRINCIPLES

We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.

 - Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.

 - Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‑to‑end, and invest in getting better everyday.

 - Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‑team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.





JOIN OUR MISSION

At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.

TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore. 





PRIVACY POLICY AND ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy https://www.trmlabs.com/policies/privacy-policy.

We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

Because our hiring cycles for certain positions may span 24 to 36 months, we retain your personal information for up to 36 months from the date of your application. After that period, your data is deleted unless a different retention period is required or permitted by law.

If you are located in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or another jurisdiction with applicable data protection laws, you have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data at any time before that period ends. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at privacy@trmlabs.com.

To notify TRM Labs that you believe this job posting is non-compliant, please submit a report through this form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSc6e8jRCl2cQwgIzXLpIGQXtwvMQh__TcokvO2toAAkT44A6Q/viewform?usp=dialog. No response will be provided to inquiries unrelated to job posting compliance.

The use of AI tools of any kind (including but not limited to notetakers, interview assistants, and real-time coaching tools such as Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom, Cluey, or similar) during TRM interviews is not permitted without prior approval from TRM. TRM uses its own internal tools for note-taking to ensure a consistent and confidential experience for all candidates. 

We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made via this form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSevmAzPxWOYm_7kMHb9lEJlX3tpdBeHvvvNWjsI_6xhUfnXjw/viewform?usp=dialog.




RECRUITMENT AGENCIES

TRM Labs does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to TRM employees. TRM Labs is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company without a signed agreement.

jobs.title: Director of HSE – Fabrication & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps expand the reach of the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Director of Health, Safety & Environmental (HSE) – Fabrication & Manufacturing provides strategic and operational HSE leadership across Loenbro's fabrication, manufacturing, and prefabrication network. Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing, this role is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving a standardized, fit-for-purpose HSE management system that supports Loenbro's strategy to build a scalable, high-performing manufacturing organization.

The Director will work in close partnership with shop management, operations, quality, engineering, project teams, and Corporate HSE to establish practical standards that protect employees while supporting safe, efficient, disciplined, and repeatable manufacturing operations. This position is expected to be highly visible in the shops and to build credibility through engagement with the people performing and leading the work.

A critical responsibility of this position is partnering with the SVP of Manufacturing and operational leaders to foster a culture grounded in Human and Organizational Performance (HOP) principles. The Director will reinforce that people make mistakes, error is predictable, systems and organizational conditions influence behavior, learning is essential, and leadership response to failure matters.

Success requires strong technical HSE knowledge, operational credibility, systems thinking, and the ability to translate regulatory and industry requirements into practical standards that improve both safety and operational performance.

Essential Job Responsibilities

HSE Strategy & Leadership

• Develop and execute the Fabrication & Manufacturing HSE strategy in alignment with the overall business strategy, Loenbro requirements, and applicable regulatory obligations.

• Serve as the primary HSE advisor to the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing and the Fabrication & Manufacturing leadership team.

• Establish an HSE operating model capable of supporting a multi-site manufacturing organization, continued growth, new facilities, acquisitions, and increasingly complex end markets.

• Integrate HSE considerations into operational planning, facility design, equipment selection, production processes, productization, capacity expansion, and acquisition integration.

• Establish clear HSE expectations, accountabilities, governance, and performance measures across all Fabrication & Manufacturing facilities.

• Maintain strong alignment with Corporate HSE while ensuring requirements are practical and appropriately tailored to fabrication and manufacturing operations.

Standardization & Fit-for-Purpose Best Practices

• Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of standardized Fabrication & Manufacturing HSE policies, procedures, standards, and work practices across the network.

• Assess existing facility practices, identify gaps and leading practices, and establish common standards while recognizing legitimate differences in operations, equipment, workforce, and risk.

• Develop practical standards for material handling; pipe storage and stacking; rigging and lifting; overhead cranes; welding, cutting and hot work; machine guarding; hazardous energy control; powered industrial trucks; electrical safety; compressed gases; industrial hygiene; PPE; chemical management; housekeeping; working at heights; emergency response; and contractor safety.

• Ensure standards meet applicable regulatory requirements and recognized industry practices while remaining understandable and executable at the shop-floor level.

• Partner with Operations, Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain to incorporate HSE into shop layouts, equipment, tooling, material flow, workstations, production planning, and work methods.

• Establish a controlled process for issuing, communicating, training, auditing, and periodically reviewing F&M HSE standards.

Human & Organizational Performance (HOP)

• Partner with the SVP of Manufacturing and shop leadership to establish HOP principles as a foundational element of the Fabrication & Manufacturing safety and operational culture.

• Reinforce the principles that people make mistakes, error is predictable, organizational systems influence behavior, learning is essential, and leadership response to failure matters.

• Help shift the organization from a primarily event-driven safety model toward proactive understanding of how work is actually performed and the conditions that create or increase risk.

• Develop leadership capability to respond constructively to incidents, near misses, errors, stop-work events, and employee concerns.

• Promote learning teams, operational learning reviews, pre-job discussions, field and shop engagement, and other methods that involve the people performing the work in identifying risk and developing solutions.

• Encourage employees to identify weak signals, raise concerns, stop work when appropriate, and participate openly in learning without fear of inappropriate blame.

• Ensure investigations look beyond individual actions to understand system conditions, organizational influences, equipment, processes, planning, supervision, and other contributing factors.

• Balance accountability with learning by distinguishing human error and system-induced behavior from reckless or intentional disregard of established requirements.

Shop Leadership Partnership & Employee Engagement

• Build strong working relationships with fabrication and manufacturing managers, supervisors, foremen, and frontline employees.

• Maintain a visible presence within manufacturing facilities and regularly engage employees where work is performed to understand normal work, constraints, and emerging risks.

• Serve as a coach and operational partner to shop leadership rather than functioning solely as a compliance or enforcement resource.

• Help managers translate HSE expectations into practical daily operating behaviors and effective frontline leadership.

• Support shop leaders in conducting effective safety meetings, pre-task planning, observations, learning discussions, stand-downs, and corrective-action follow-up.

• Develop operational ownership of safety so that HSE provides expertise, coaching, assurance, and systems support while line leadership remains accountable for safe execution.

Risk Management & Operational Assurance

• Develop a risk-based approach for identifying and managing critical fabrication and manufacturing hazards and high-energy exposures.

• Establish consistent facility HSE assessments, audits, inspections, risk reviews, and operational assurance processes.

• Develop leading and lagging indicators that provide meaningful visibility into HSE performance, exposure, control effectiveness, and emerging risk.

• Identify recurring risks and systemic trends across facilities and lead network-wide corrective actions where appropriate.

• Ensure corrective actions are appropriately prioritized, assigned, tracked, verified for effectiveness, and closed.

• Support new facility start-ups, expansions, equipment installations, process changes, acquisitions, and integration activities from an HSE perspective.

Incident Management & Operational Learning

• Establish consistent expectations for incident and near-miss reporting, high-potential event identification, investigation, causal analysis, corrective action, and communication.

• Lead or facilitate significant incident and high-potential event reviews and ensure appropriate executive visibility.

• Focus investigations on what happened, how work normally occurs, what conditions influenced the outcome, and what system improvements can reduce future risk.

• Identify lessons that should be shared across the manufacturing network and verify that meaningful improvements are implemented.

• Partner with leadership to ensure responses to incidents reinforce trust, accountability, learning, and continuous improvement.

• Track recurring event themes and use organizational learning to influence standards, training, engineering controls, supervision, planning, and work design.

Training & Workforce Development

• Establish an HSE training framework appropriate for fabrication and manufacturing employees, supervisors, managers, and leaders.

• Identify regulatory, technical, task-specific, and leadership training requirements by role and exposure.

• Develop HOP and operational-learning training for Fabrication & Manufacturing leadership.

• Partner with Operations and HR to incorporate HSE expectations into onboarding, qualification, supervisor development, craft training, and leadership development.

• Ensure training is practical, field-oriented, and relevant to the hazards employees encounter in actual fabrication and manufacturing work.

• Develop and coach HSE personnel supporting the Fabrication & Manufacturing organization and establish consistent expectations for their role as operational partners.

Environmental & Regulatory Compliance

• Ensure Fabrication & Manufacturing facilities maintain compliance with applicable federal, state, and local HSE requirements.

• Partner with appropriate internal and external resources on environmental permitting, waste management, hazardous materials, air emissions, spill prevention, and other facility environmental obligations.

• Maintain effective processes for regulatory inspections, required records, reporting, corrective actions, and agency interactions.

• Monitor changes in regulations and industry requirements and translate them into practical actions for the manufacturing network.

Performance & Continuous Improvement

• Develop and maintain a Fabrication & Manufacturing HSE scorecard with meaningful leading and lagging indicators.

• Analyze trends across incidents, observations, near misses, high-potential events, employee feedback, audits, and operational data.

• Benchmark practices against relevant fabrication, manufacturing, construction, and industrial best practices.

• Partner with Quality and Operational Excellence to integrate HSE into continuous-improvement initiatives and management systems.

• Provide regular HSE performance, risk, organizational-learning, and improvement updates to the SVP of Manufacturing and other senior leadership.

• Use HSE data and employee feedback to identify opportunities to improve work design, reliability, quality, productivity, and employee experience.

Key Performance Indicators

• Reduction of serious-injury and high-potential exposure through effective critical-risk controls.

• Consistent implementation and audit performance of standardized F&M HSE policies and procedures.

• Leadership and employee participation in HOP, learning teams, operational learning, and proactive risk identification.

• Timely closure and verified effectiveness of corrective actions.

• Quality and timeliness of incident investigations and organizational learning.

• Regulatory compliance and environmental performance.

• Training and qualification completion for required roles and critical tasks.

• Improvement in leading indicators, employee engagement, and safety-culture measures.

• Successful HSE integration of new facilities, acquisitions, equipment, and processes.

Key Qualifications

Required

• 10+ years of progressive HSE experience within fabrication, manufacturing, industrial construction, energy, heavy industry, or a comparable environment.

• Demonstrated experience leading HSE programs across multiple facilities, operating locations, or business units.

• Strong working knowledge of OSHA requirements and recognized industry practices applicable to fabrication and manufacturing environments.

• Demonstrated experience developing and implementing HSE policies, procedures, standards, management systems, and assurance processes.

• Strong knowledge of high-risk fabrication activities including welding, lifting and rigging, cranes, material handling, machine safety, hazardous energy control, powered industrial equipment, and industrial hygiene.

• Experience conducting incident investigations, causal analysis, risk assessments, audits, and corrective-action programs.

• Demonstrated ability to influence operational leaders and frontline employees and to build strong partnerships without relying solely on positional authority.

• Strong written, verbal, facilitation, coaching, and executive communication skills.

• Ability and willingness to travel regularly among Loenbro fabrication and manufacturing facilities.

Preferred

• CSP, CIH, CHST, ASP, or similar professional HSE certification.

• Formal training or practical experience implementing Human and Organizational Performance (HOP), Learning Teams, operational learning, or similar contemporary safety approaches.

• Experience developing HSE systems within a growing, decentralized, or transforming manufacturing organization.

• Experience supporting nuclear, mission-critical, power, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or other highly regulated industrial markets.

• Experience integrating newly acquired facilities or standardizing HSE practices across previously decentralized operations.

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Occupational Safety, Environmental Health, Engineering, Industrial Technology, Construction Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent significant industry experience may be considered.

Leadership Competencies

• Operational Credibility — Understands how fabrication and manufacturing work is actually planned and performed.

• Visible Leadership — Spends meaningful time in the shops engaging employees, supervisors, and managers.

• Partnership Mindset — Works with operations to solve problems rather than operating as a separate compliance function.

• Learning Orientation — Seeks to understand why outcomes occur and how systems can be improved before assigning corrective action.

• Practical Judgment — Develops standards that appropriately manage risk while allowing the business to execute efficiently.

• Influence & Communication — Effectively engages craft employees, supervisors, managers, executives, customers, and external stakeholders.

• Systems Thinking — Recognizes the interaction among people, processes, equipment, organizational systems, and leadership decisions.

• Continuous Improvement — Uses operational learning and performance data to make work safer, more reliable, and more efficient.

Success Profile

Success in this role will be demonstrated through a consistent Fabrication & Manufacturing HSE operating system across Loenbro facilities; strong partnerships between HSE and shop leadership; improved identification and control of critical risks; increased leadership and employee engagement in operational learning; effective adoption of HOP principles; timely resolution of systemic issues; and measurable strengthening of the safety culture as the Fabrication & Manufacturing business continues to scale.

The objective is not simply compliance. The Director of HSE will help create a manufacturing organization where safe work, operational discipline, employee engagement, learning, quality, and productivity reinforce one another.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

• Combination of office/remote work and frequent travel to fabrication and manufacturing facilities; travel of approximately 40–60%, based on business and facility needs.

• Regular, hands-on presence on shop floors and at fabrication facilities to engage employees, supervisors, and shop leadership where work is performed.

• Exposure to typical fabrication and manufacturing shop environments, including noise, dust, welding fumes, moving equipment, and other industrial hazards while touring facilities.

• Regular engagement with employees, shop leadership, and executive leadership, which may require regional and national travel by air and ground transportation.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Benefits

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) retirement plan with company match

• Performance-based bonus plan

• Long-term Incentives

• Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay

• Life and disability insurance

• Professional development and training opportunities

• Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities. If you're ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

• Living with Integrity

• Exceeding Expectations

…we want to hear from you.

jobs.title: Accounting Manager
jobs.description:
We're looking for an Accounting Manager to take ownership of Lemonade's parent company accounting operations and help drive greater efficiency, accuracy, and transparency across our financial ecosystem. You'll sit within our Finance team, leading the month-end close process, managing a broad range of financial schedules, and acting as a key partner to our Controller and Director of Technical Accounting on SEC reporting and audit deliverables. This is a high-ownership role that touches nearly every corner of the business — from intercompany transactions to share-based compensation to lease accounting.

We believe three things matter for every role at Lemonade: drive to push through challenges, efficiency that keeps standards high while moving fast, and adaptability that lets you pivot with data and AI insights. These aren't buzzwords, they're how we actually work.

Our AI-first approach isn't just a tagline either. We're building the future of insurance with AI at the center, and we need people who are genuinely excited to learn and grow alongside these tools.




IN THIS ROLE YOU'LL

 - Lead the month-end close process for Lemonade Inc., Agency, and Life Agency — including P&L analytics, vendor breakdown reviews, and detailed expense reviews across entities

 - Manage all parent company accrual schedules, including contract and vendor accruals, professional and legal fee schedules, and underwriting expenses

 - Own share-based compensation accounting in partnership with Fidelity — preparing entries for all subsidiaries, footnote disclosures, and recording of stock option exercises

 - Oversee intercompany relationships, settlement of transactions, translation true-ups, and cost-plus relationship recording

 - Manage ASC 842 lease schedules in Trullion, prepare monthly entries, and support lease disclosure preparation

 - Lead the organization and delivery of year-end and quarterly audit procedures, and support annual SOX testing

 - Support the Controller and Director of Technical Accounting in quarterly SEC financial reporting — including financial reporting packages, footnote and disclosure preparation, and audit review support

 - Act as Finance-level AP approver for the vast majority of invoices, ensuring accuracy and appropriate tagging before escalation to cost center managers

 - Run monthly allocations, prepare allocation review schedules, reperform occupancy calculations, and support monthly GAAP ULAE entries

 - Partner cross-functionally with Business Development, Offline Media, Production, and Growth Development on financial operations including invoices, accruals, and processing


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 5+ years of experience in public or private accounting, with demonstrated ownership of complex, multi-entity close processes

 - Strong command of U.S. GAAP, including working knowledge of ASC 842, share-based compensation, intercompany accounting, and SEC reporting requirements

 - Advanced Excel and Google Sheets skills

 - Experience with Workday ERP is a plus

 - Comfortable operating across multiple entities and legal structures simultaneously

 - Sharp attention to detail with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines without dropping the ball

 - A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field

 - Ability to work in our Soho, NYC office 3 days per week

 

Please note that we are unable to sponsor applicants for work visas.

Unfortunately, we cannot consider applicants from these states: Alaska, California, Colorado, Montana, Hawaii, New Mexico and Puerto Rico.

jobs.title: Fluids Analyst II, Combustion Devices
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Propulsion team at Relativity is focused on developing and delivering highly performant and manufacturable engines for Terran R. Engineers are responsible for the entire lifecycle of their parts, from initial design through production to qualification and flight. The team fosters a culture of bottoms-up decision-making, free from technical gatekeeping, where ownership and accountability are key at all levels. But designing engines with a quarter million pounds of thrust is just the beginning. As the flight configuration enters qualification, the team is now exploring modifications for future engines, including thrust upgrades, new cycles, and design for mass production.

About the role:

• Contribute to design and qualification of combustion devices hardware (injectors, thrust chamber, heat exchangers, igniters) through Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis

• Review test and flight data as necessary to evaluate and anchor models

• Interface with hardware designers and utilize thermofluid expertise to influence design decisions

• Develop and recommend analysis approaches that may decrease design iteration time

• A strong commitment to accountability, collaboration, and execution

About you:

• Bachelor's degree in a science or engineering field

• 2+ years of experience in performing computation fluid dynamics analyses (employment, internships, project experience)

• Familiar with typical analysis steps including pre/post-processing, meshing, boundary conditions, etc.

• Experience with basic engineering scripting in Python, MATLAB, or similar

• Strong background in fluid mechanics and heat transfer

Nice to haves, but not required:

• We believe varied perspectives & backgrounds strengthen our team. Prior experience in aerospace is not required

• Graduate degree in a science or engineering field

• Experience in Siemens STAR-CCM+

• Working knowledge of rocket engine subsystems, such as combustion devices

jobs.title: Northeast Field Service Technician - Water Technologies

The ideal candidate possesses strong mechanical and electrical aptitude, excellent troubleshooting skills, and a passion for delivering exceptional customer service. This individual will work independently while collaborating closely with Technical Support, Sales, Customer Service, and internal operations to ensure customers receive timely, professional, and high-quality service.

jobs.title: Senior Construction Bridge Engineer
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend Heery is seeking a Senior Construction Bridge Engineer to join our team. The Senior Bridge Engineer provides senior-level engineering leadership, technical oversight, and construction support for complex bridge, guideway, and structural infrastructure associated with major transportation and railroad programs, including the California High-Speed Rail (CAHSR) Project.

The Senior Bridge Engineer is responsible for leading the review and resolution of complex structural engineering issues, evaluating bridge design and construction documents, providing technical direction to project teams, and ensuring that construction activities comply with contract requirements, applicable design standards, and regulatory requirements.

This position serves as a senior technical resource and liaison among design consultants, construction management, contractors, engineers, regulatory agencies, and project stakeholders to support the safe, efficient, and successful delivery of complex bridge infrastructure.

Responsibilities

• Provide senior-level engineering oversight for the design, construction, inspection, testing, and acceptance of bridges, guideways, retaining structures, culverts, foundations, and other transportation-related structural systems
• Lead the technical review of bridge design plans, specifications, structural calculations, shop drawings, working drawings, Requests for Information (RFIs), submittals, construction work plans, and design modifications for compliance with contract requirements and applicable engineering standards
• Perform and/or oversee complex structural engineering analyses involving reinforced concrete, prestressed and post-tensioned concrete, structural steel, foundations, seismic systems, bearings, expansion joints, and other bridge components
• Provide technical direction and engineering recommendations for complex field conditions, constructability issues, design discrepancies, non-conforming work, and proposed design changes
• Evaluate contractor proposals, value engineering proposals, change requests, design revisions, and field modifications, including assessment of technical feasibility, structural adequacy, constructability, cost, schedule, and risk

• Lead or participate in constructability reviews, design reviews, interdisciplinary coordination meetings, risk assessments, value engineering workshops, and technical working groups
• Review and provide technical oversight of structural concrete placement, reinforcing steel, post-tensioning, structural steel fabrication and erection, bearings, expansion joints, falsework, shoring, temporary works, erection engineering, and construction staging
• Review and evaluate temporary works and construction engineering to verify that proposed construction methods maintain structural stability, public safety, worker safety, and compliance with approved project requirements
• Perform independent engineering evaluations and calculations to support field decisions related to structural integrity, construction sequencing, temporary conditions, design deviations, and changes to approved construction methods
• Provide senior technical guidance to engineers and construction personnel and mentor less-experienced staff in bridge engineering, construction practices, technical documentation, and engineering problem-solving
• Review inspection reports, material testing results, non-conformance reports (NCRs), corrective action plans, quality records, and other construction documentation to ensure timely and technically appropriate resolution of quality issues

• Support project risk management by identifying structural, design, construction, and interface risks and recommending appropriate mitigation measures
• Coordinate with regulatory agencies and stakeholders, as applicable, on structural engineering, design compliance, construction, and safety matters
• Support compliance with Federal Railroad Administration (FRA), California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC), California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), applicable environmental requirements, and Authority safety and quality requirements
• Perform other senior-level bridge engineering duties as assigned in support of the project and overall transportation infrastructure program

• Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline and a minimum of eight (15) years of progressively responsible bridge, structural, transportation, or construction engineering experience; or, in lieu of a degree, eighteen (18) years of progressively responsible bridge or structural engineering experience

• Demonstrated experience with the design, construction, inspection, or technical oversight of bridges or other complex transportation structures
• Advanced knowledge of reinforced concrete, prestressed and post-tensioned concrete, structural steel, foundation systems, seismic design principles, structural analysis, and bridge construction methods
• Strong knowledge and demonstrated ability to interpret engineering plans, specifications, structural calculations, contract documents, construction drawings, and technical reports
• Demonstrated ability to independently analyze complex engineering problems, develop technically sound solutions, and exercise professional engineering judgment
• Experience reviewing contractor submittals, RFIs, design changes, construction work plans, temporary works, and other technical documentation
• Strong understanding of construction quality assurance, inspection, testing, non-conformance resolution, and construction documentation processes
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present technical recommendations to project management, contractors, consultants, and other stakeholders
• Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary technical coordination and work effectively with engineers, construction personnel, contractors, consultants, and regulatory agencies
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and engineering, structural analysis, design, and construction management software
• Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple technical assignments, and make sound engineering recommendations in a complex construction environment

• Preferred Qualifications/ Certifications/ Licensures
• Current California Structural Engineer (SE) license.
• Master's degree in Structural Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a related engineering discipline
• Ten (10) or more years of progressively responsible experience in bridge design, bridge construction, structural engineering, or major transportation infrastructure programs.
• Experience providing senior-level engineering oversight on railroad, high-speed rail, commuter rail, freight rail, highway, transit, or other major transportation infrastructure projects.
• Experience supporting California High-Speed Rail, Caltrans, major commuter rail, freight rail, or other large-scale public infrastructure programs.
• Advanced knowledge of AREMA, AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications, Caltrans Bridge Design and Construction Manuals, California Building Code (CBC), and other applicable transportation and structural engineering standards.
• Experience with seismic design and evaluation of bridges and transportation structures in accordance with applicable California and national standards.

Experience leading technical teams, mentoring engineers, and coordinating multidisciplinary engineering activities on complex infrastructure projects

Job Title: Project Engineer-Travelling

Company: Loenbro, LLC
Business Unit/Department: Operations
Location: Western US
Reports to:  Project Manager
Employment Type: Full-Time
FLSA Classification: Exempt

About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Project Engineer supports the Project Manager and field teams in the coordination and execution of construction projects. This role is responsible for assisting with project documentation, scheduling, procurement, and communication to ensure projects are delivered efficiently, safely, and in alignment with contract requirements. The Project Engineer plays a key role in maintaining organization, tracking project progress, and supporting successful project outcomes.

Essential Job Responsibilities

• Assist in managing project execution by supporting day-to-day activities, monitoring scope, schedule, budget, and contract requirements, and helping identify and address potential project impacts.

• Maintain and coordinate project documentation, including RFIs, submittals, change orders, drawings, specifications, permits, project correspondence, and contract-related records.

• Support project planning and controls through schedule updates, cost tracking, invoice review, forecasting assistance, and maintenance of project budgets and performance metrics.

• Coordinate procurement and subcontractor activities, including material and equipment purchases, delivery tracking, subcontractor onboarding, contract administration, and compliance monitoring.

• Collaborate with Project Managers, Superintendents, Foremen, subcontractors, vendors, and clients to facilitate communication, resolve project challenges, and support successful project execution.

• Promote safety, quality, and regulatory compliance by ensuring adherence to company policies, project specifications, applicable codes, and contractual requirements.

• Assist with field operations and project closeout activities, helping ensure completed work meets quality standards, client expectations, and overall project objectives.

Other duties may be assigned as needed to support business operations.

Minimum Qualifications

Required:

• Associate degree or Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and construction experience.

• Construction, project engineering, or related field experience.

• Basic understanding of construction means and methods, project documentation, contracts, scheduling, and procurement processes.

• Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, contracts, RFIs, and submittals.

• Strong organizational, problem-solving, and time-management skills.

• Effective written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work collaboratively across project teams.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to safety, quality, and project success.

Preferred:

• Field experience supporting civil, mechanical, industrial, commercial, or construction projects.

• Experience with commercial, industrial, federal, energy, manufacturing, or infrastructure projects.

• Experience using Procore, Bluebeam, Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or similar construction management software.

• Exposure to project scheduling, cost tracking, procurement, and contract administration processes.

• Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification or pursuit of professional licensure is a plus.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

• Indoor office environments involving project planning, coordination, documentation, and reporting activities.

• Outdoor construction and industrial sites with exposure to varying weather conditions, noise, dust, chemicals, uneven terrain, and construction-related hazards.

• Fabrication shops and operational facilities with exposure to noise, dust, machinery, and other environmental factors.

• Frequent visits to active project sites to monitor progress, support field operations, and coordinate project execution.

• Travel requirements: up to 90% of time.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Benefits

Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) retirement plan with company match

• Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay

• Life and disability insurance

• Professional development and training opportunities

• Employee assistance program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.

Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

• Living with Integrity

• Exceeding Expectations

• Acting with Urgency

• Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.

Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.description:
We’re looking for Auto Painters with a minimum of 5 years of professional automotive painting experience to join us at Carvana - the fastest-growing used automotive retailer in U.S. history and one of the four fastest companies to make the Fortune 500.

As an Experienced Painter, you’ll be expected to be highly skilled in painting (base coats, tri-coats, solid, metallic, and clear coats), blending adjacent panels, and paint correcting vehicles.

At Carvana, you’ll receive a competitive wage and amazing perks – including a 401(k) with Carvana match and even a vehicle purchase discount – all while using state of the art tools in one of our high-tech Inspection Centers (click here to learn more). If you’re joining us in an entry-level position, we offer training programs to make sure your skills and pay progress along with the company.

Other perks of the Job

• 100% company-paid healthcare premiums

• Generous paid-time off and your birthday is a holiday!

• ASE and tool reimbursement programs

• Tuition reimbursement and student loan repayment

Schedule:

We do everything we can to deliver an exceptional customer experience, and that includes delivering great vehicles when expected. If we're in a pinch, mandatory overtime is one way in which we can follow-through on this commitment to our customers. We're looking for team players who are all in on our mission and are able to work mandatory overtime based on our business needs.

How To Get Started
Join the Carvana team by applying on this page, or call one of our recruiters by phone at (888) 690-7853, Monday through Friday, between 6 AM and 4 PM PT (9AM to 7PM ET).

Not a match for this role?
We have a variety of paint roles available, depending on your experience - look below to see other roles available to help us get our low-mileage, late-model cars ready for our customers:

• Paint Prepper (min 6 months professional experience): prepare vehicles for cosmetic paintwork, including sanding, masking, taping, bagging, unbagging/tear down, and buffing

• Entry-Level Painter (min 1 year professional experience): prime vehicles and perform final sanding before the vehicle is painted, along with buffing, touch-up, paint mixing, and airbrush.

• Mid-Level Painter (min 3 years professional experience): match/mix paint color and use water-based paint to paint the vehicle inside our paint booths

• Experienced Painter (min 5 years professional experience): painting (base coats, tri-coats, solid, metallic, and clear coats), blending adjacent panels, and paint correcting vehicles.

We also have a variety of other automotive roles available in one of our 18 locations across the country – take a look at our Careers site to apply for one of the following roles:

• Auto Body roles: Paint, Prep/Body work, Wheel Repair, Airbrush, Interior Repair, Glass Repair, and PDR (Paintless Dent Repair) roles

• Auto Technician/Mechanic roles: Lube and Oil, Inspection, Brake and Tire, Mechanical Repair / Build, and Master Technician roles

• Entry-Level roles: Detailing, Inventory Associate (Car Porters), Photo, Parts Associate, Inspection, and Coordinator/Administrator roles

General qualifications and requirements

• Ability to physically operate vehicle equipment and tools - must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently

• Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Some positions may be subject to an Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check

• An ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-changing production environment while sometimes being exposed to excessive weather conditions (heat/cold)

• Use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment

About Carvana
At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period.

To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website.

Think you’ve got what it takes to join our team? Apply today!

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Must be able to read, write, speak and understand English.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures, along with many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values — Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle — shape how we work and grow as a team.



About the Team

Decagon’s APM team turns enterprise commitments into durable customer outcomes. We own deployment execution, steady-state operations, and the operating system that lets delivery quality and velocity scale as our customer base and deal complexity grow.

Within the APM team, the Technical Program Manager (TPM) function helps drive end-to-end delivery of Decagon's most complex customer implementations — design partnerships, strategic deals, and enterprise go-lives — alongside the internal cross-functional programs that underpin enterprise readiness. We work across the company to ensure every deployment ships on time and at high quality. Most importantly, the TPM function builds the operational strategy and foundation that scales as Decagon grows.

This is a fully in-office role based in our New York office.


About the Role

As a Technical Program Manager at Decagon, you will own delivery of our most complex customer deployments and drive the internal cross-functional programs that enable enterprise readiness. You will work across APM, Engineering, Product, Research, Security, Legal, and Go-to-Market to translate requirements into executable programs, manage dependencies across parallel workstreams, and surface issues before they become blockers. As Decagon grows, you will be responsible for continuously improving our operational and internal functional excellence so we can scale seamlessly.



In this role, you will:

 - Partner with a forward-deployed working team to drive operational excellence and program management for complex customer implementations end-to-end — aligning on scope, sequencing dependencies, managing risk, and ensuring no one is caught off-guard at handoffs or milestones; this includes design partnerships and strategic accounts where requirements are still taking shape

 - Translate customer requirements and feedback into structured program plans — working with GTM and Product to prioritize the highest-impact asks, map them to delivery roadmaps, and track execution against committed timelines

 - Drive internal cross-functional programs — model lifecycle management, security and compliance buildouts, external certifications — from kickoff through completion, aligning stakeholders and holding workstreams accountable without direct authority over executing teams



Your background looks something like this

 - 4-6+ years of experience as a technical program manager or in product/engineering operations, with direct ownership of either complex enterprise deployments or large-scale internal cross-functional initiatives

 - Track record running high-stakes customer implementations or feature builds at the design-partner or strategic-deal tier, where scope is ambiguous, requirements evolve mid-build, and the customer's success is tied directly to yours

 - Demonstrated ability to drive programs without authority — an outcome-oriented but collaborative approach that unites teams around shared milestones and holds the work accountable end-to-end with influence

 - Structured, rigorous approach to ambiguity — able to define program scope, sequence dependencies, surface blockers early, and keep multiple concurrent workstreams moving without losing resolution

 - Enough technical fluency to engage credibly with engineering teams — able to ask the right questions, pressure-test tradeoffs, and translate between technical and business contexts without going deep on implementation

 - Exceptional written and verbal communicator — able to calibrate depth, format, and framing for customers, engineering leads, executive sponsors, and external partners alike



Even better if you have

 - Hands-on experience with LLMs or conversational AI — you've shipped something with these systems, whether in a professional or personal context

 - A track record of moving programs through legal, security, engineering, and customer approval gates — able to anticipate friction points and keep timelines intact



Benefits

We proudly offer the following benefits for our full-time employees:

 - Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits for you and your family

 - Life Insurance and Disability Benefits

 - Retirement Plan (e.g., 401K, pension)

 - Parental Leave

 - Fertility and family building benefits through Carrot

 - Monthly stipend to support your wellness, lifestyle, and work-life balance

 - Daily lunches and snacks in the office to keep you at your best

 - Take what you need vacation policy (subject to local requirements; UK employees receive 25 days of statutory leave)

These benefits are described in more detail in Decagon’s policies, may vary by location, and can change at any time according to applicable compensation and benefits plans.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Content & Operations, Global Customer Advocacy
jobs.description:
Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) accelerates digital transformation so customers can be more agile, efficient, resilient, and secure. The Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange platform protects thousands of customers from cyberattacks and data loss by securely connecting users, devices, and applications in any location. Distributed across 200+ public data centers globally and thousands of private sites at the edge, the SASE-based Zero Trust Exchange is the world’s largest in-line cloud security platform.

We believe the future of work is Human + AI and are building an AI-native enterprise where human potential is amplified by machine intelligence to solve the world’s hardest security challenges. Driven by deep customer obsession, we are committed to the mission, outcome, and to each other. We bring these commitments to life through three core behaviors: ownership and collaboration, trust through outcomes and impact, and a challenge culture with ongoing feedback. Ready to make an impact at the company pioneering security transformation in the AI era? Join us at Zscaler.

Role

We are looking for a Senior Manager, Content & Operations, Global Customer Advocacy to join our team. This is a Remote (Americas) role, reporting to the Senior Director, Global Customer Advocacy.  The Senior Manager, Content & Operations will drive the scale and impact of Global Customer Advocacy through AI-powered innovation, strategic content development, and third-party customer validation. This role will lead the adoption and optimization of AI-driven solutions, amplify customer proof points across cross-functional workflows, and strengthen Zscaler’s market credibility through customer reviews and analyst engagement. By connecting customer advocacy to key business priorities, this individual will accelerate operational efficiency, influence buyer decisions, and maximize the business impact of customer storytelling.

What you’ll do (Role Expectations)

• Drive AI-powered customer advocacy by leading the adoption, integration, and continuous optimization of the Customer Story Agent, embedding customer proof points into cross-functional workflows to increase accessibility, utilization, and operational efficiency

• Accelerate AI adoption and measure business impact by executing global enablement initiatives, establishing an AI impact measurement framework, and tracking productivity gains and business outcomes

• Develop strategic customer content aligned with core solution priorities, partnering with cross-functional marketing teams to fuel integrated campaigns and amplify high-impact customer success stories

• Strengthen third-party customer validation by leading the Gartner Peer Insights strategy, establishing an always-on review recruitment program, and integrating customer feedback into marketing content to support competitive positioning and AI-driven search visibility

• Support strategic analyst engagement by partnering with Analyst Relations and regional advocacy teams to fulfill customer reference requests for major industry evaluations and facilitate customer participation in key industry events

Who You Are (Success Profile)

• You are driven by innovation, bringing curiosity and technological fluency to solve complex challenges and uncover scalable, AI-powered solutions.

• You act like an owner with a bias for action, taking full accountability for outcomes and navigating seamlessly between high-level advocacy strategy and hands-on operational execution.

• You are data-driven, relying on rigorous analytics and measurable evidence to make sound decisions, optimize workflows, and demonstrate tangible business value.

• You are a high-trust collaborator who communicates with clarity and respect, embracing feedback and partnering across cross-functional teams to achieve shared organizational goals.

• You think at scale, connecting daily operational efforts to overarching business objectives and designing durable processes built to support global growth.

What We’re Looking for (Minimum Qualifications)

• Demonstrated curiosity and active exploration of AI tools, with a proven history of integrating new technologies to enhance daily workflows and augment problem-solving

• 7+ years of experience in customer marketing/advocacy, content strategy, product marketing, marketing operations, or related disciplines within a B2B technology environment

• Strong strategic content development experience, with the ability to translate complex technology solutions and customer outcomes into compelling, data-driven content that supports integrated marketing campaigns

• Proven cross-functional program management skills, with experience leading global initiatives, influencing stakeholders, and driving measurable outcomes across Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success

• Strong analytical and operational expertise, including developing performance measurement frameworks, establishing scalable processes, and leveraging data to optimize program effectiveness

What Will Make You Stand Out (Preferred Qualifications)

• Demonstrate a proven ability to leverage AI technologies and workflows to drive measurable operational efficiency

• Hands-on experience with Upland RO, including managing customer advocacy content, maintaining data integrity, and optimizing platform workflows

• Background in customer advocacy or customer marketing, with experience managing Gartner Peer Insights programs, supporting analyst relations and customer reference requests, and developing compelling customer content

• Proven track record deploying and operationalizing AI agents, securing cross-functional stakeholder buy-in, driving internal adoption, and managing ongoing content ingestion, maintenance, and optimization to ensure long-term effectiveness

jobs.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

• Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.

• What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.

• It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS*

• Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options

• Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave

• Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees

• And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays

• Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.

*Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

We are seeking a detail-oriented Software QA Engineer to join our growing team. This role is ideal for someone early in their QA career who is passionate about ensuring product quality within the software lifecycle, learning automation tooling and collaborating with developers in a fast pace industry.

This is a 3 month temporary employment engagement. There is potential to convert to regular employment based on performance and business need.

RESPONSIBILITIES

• Execute manual and automated test cases against a full stack software

• Document and report software defects within the software lifecycle in Jira

• Participate in an agile team sprint planning/stand ups

• Collaborate with developers and product teams to clarify requirements and reproduce issues

• Assist in maintaining a growing test repository of manual and automated scripts within Playwright framework

• Continuous contribution to QA standards and testing processes

QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelors degree in computer science or related field/equivalent education

• 0-2 years experience in software qa/testing (internships included)

• General understanding of software development lifecycle, testing methodologies and Agile processes

• Basic understanding of coding languages (preferred java script)

• Familiarity with Jira ticketing and Git

• Strong attention to detail and problem solving

• Strong communication skills

• U.S. Citizen and eligible for DoD Secret or TS/SCI clearance

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

• Exposure to automation tooling (playwright/cypress/selenium)

• Experience with API tooling

• Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (github actions/ jenkins, etc.)

• Motivated to learn and grow within QA industry

• Team player with a proactive, problem-solving mindset

• Ability to manage time and tasks effectively in a fast paced environment

• Flexible mindset

COMPENSATION

• Base Salary: Denver: $70,000; Long Beach: $80,000

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

• Work Location—this role will be onsite at either our Centennial, CO or Long Beach, CA location, with travel to other sites as needed.

• Work environment—the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person's working conditions while performing the job.

• Physical demands—the physical demands of the job, including bending, sitting, lifting and driving.

This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below.

jobs.title: Engineer III, Global Technology - Identity and Access Management
jobs.description:
Why This Role Matters

This Engineer III designs, implements, and maintains identity and access management solutions that support secure access across the organization. This role contributes to IAM modernization efforts while improving authentication, authorization, automated provisioning, access governance, and compliance.

As an experienced individual contributor, you will help shape technical decisions, deliver high-quality solutions, and continuously improve the IAM program by evaluating emerging identity threats, technologies, and best practices.

Team and Technology

You will work across SailPoint IdentityIQ, SailPoint Identity Security Cloud, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID, Java, REST APIs, GraphQL, SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP, and Active Directory. You will partner with application, infrastructure, security, audit, and business teams to define and implement access requirements. The role supports complex applications, data integrations, automated provisioning processes, and compliance with organizational policies and frameworks such as SOX, TISAX, GDPR, and CMMC.

What Success Looks Like

• Serve as a lead engineer contributor for identity and access management modernization efforts.
• Lead design sessions for the team.
• Identify, manage, and resolve incidents for applications owned by the team while developing long-term technical solutions.
• Become established as a mentor for other engineers.
• Continuously improve the IAM program through emerging technologies and best practices.

Key Areas of Impact

Technical Depth and Delivery

• Design, implement, maintain, and support identity and access management solutions while automating identity-management processes using PowerShell, APIs, Java, AI, and other development tools.
• Develop, configure, and support SSO, MFA, conditional access, passwordless authentication, provisioning, federation, and directory services while contributing to operational excellence, incident response, and continuous improvement.

Architectural Scale

• Develop role-based and attribute-based access controls, integrate enterprise applications with IAM platforms, and evaluate system dependencies, operational impacts, and design tradeoffs.
• Design and implement scalable IAM solutions using SailPoint IIQ, SailPoint ISC, Auth0, Microsoft Entra ID, REST APIs, GraphQL, SAML, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SCIM, LDAP, and Active Directory.

Team Collaboration Scale

• Partner with application, infrastructure, security, audit, and business teams to define and implement access requirements while supporting planning, coordination, and alignment across initiatives.
• Collaborate across engineering teams, provide technical feedback, support the growth of less experienced engineers, and contribute to a culture of knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

Influence and Advocacy

• Lead design sessions, share technical recommendations, communicate risks and tradeoffs, and advocate for solutions that improve security, delivery, quality, and customer outcomes.
• Evaluate emerging identity threats, technologies, and best practices to continuously improve the IAM program and strengthen access governance capabilities.

Scope of Vision

• Contribute to IAM modernization efforts by translating business and technical priorities into actionable plans and technology solutions with a near- to mid-term planning horizon.

Scale of Business Understanding

• Support compliance with organizational policies and frameworks, including SOX, TISAX, GDPR, and CMMC, while balancing technical quality, operational effectiveness, and business needs.
• Conduct access certifications, entitlement reviews, and privileged-access assessments to strengthen security controls and improve customer and business outcomes.

This position is on-site and will reside in the greater Seattle, WA. area at one of the following locations depending on availability. Candidates must be local or willing to relocate. Relocation assistance is not offered for this position.

• Downtown Seattle
• Federal Way
• Lynnwood
• Bellevue (Factoria)

Qualifications for Success

Required

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Business, or a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience in identity management, information security, systems engineering, application development, or infrastructure architecture.
• Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, supporting, and administering enterprise IAM solutions such as SailPoint IIQ, SailPoint ISC, Auth0, and Entra ID.
• Five or more years of professional experience in a technical, IAM engineering position.
• Experience creating complex applications, data integrations, and automated provisioning processes.
• Working knowledge of security and compliance principles, including least privilege, separation of duties, and access governance.
• Experience contributing to technical design discussions and solution architecture decisions.
• Experience supporting production systems and participating in operational support activities.
• Experience collaborating across teams to deliver technology solutions and business outcomes.
• Experience working with agile delivery practices, source control, testing methodologies, and modern engineering workflows.
• Experience with Agentic AI development processes and practices.

Preferred

• Experience building applications and APIs.
• Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, Azure Security Engineer Associate, SailPoint certification, CISSP, or CISM.

Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not transfer or sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (such as an H-1B visa) for this opportunity.

No need to be an expert in every tool or service from day one. A willingness to learn, take ownership, and grow with the team is what matters most.

Apply now and take the next step in your career as a Client Account Manager

Our clinics are designed with pets and people in mind: warm, friendly, and highly sniffable. We balance this design with a strong focus on technology, all built in-house, which means we can easily innovate our systems to improve the veterinary team, pet, and client experience.

In July 2026, Bond Vet and Small Door Veterinary merged  to build a more connected, accessible, and compassionate veterinary care experience across routine, primary, and urgent care. The combined organization will span more than 55 clinics across major Northeast, Mid-Atlantic, and Midwest markets, serving over half a million pets.

This role will play an important part in shaping the next chapter of our combined organization and advancing our shared mission to transform veterinary care.

This role will play an important part in shaping the next chapter of our combined organization and advancing our shared mission to transform veterinary care.

Overview
Mission: Every nurse at every Small Door practice works to one standard, and every nurse, from assistant to leader, has a clear, skills-verified path to grow with us.

The Director of Nursing does three things:

• Sets and holds the nursing standard: protocols, skill benchmarks for every level, quality audits, and the accountability loop with Practice Managers and regional leadership.

• Builds and leads the Clinical Nurse Trainer program: onboarding, practice openings, integrations, and support for practices below standard.

• Owns the nursing career ladder and talent pipeline: one path from assistant to credentialed nurse to Managing Nurse and Clinical Nurse Trainer, plus the externship and credentialing pathways that feed it, in partnership with Talent and People.

This is a senior leadership role. Practice Managers manage nursing teams; you lead through the standard, the trainer program, and the ladder.
