jobs.location: Albuquerque, NM or Oak Ridge, TN
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables.

Job Summary

The Manufacturing Equipment Technician's primary responsibility is troubleshooting, repairing, and maintaining manufacturing equipment and ensuring Preventative Maintenance (PM) is completed. The technician also maintains related maintenance documentation and supports equipment commissioning and coordination with internal teams and external service providers.

Responsibilities

• Coordinate the receipt of newly procured equipment and machining centers.

• Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair all electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, and pneumatic components of various types of machine tools, including CNC and conventional machines, part washers, air benches, welders, recyclers and other production equipment.

• Ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations, and follow company protocols for lockout/tagout (LOTO) and hazardous materials handling.

• Maintain and update maintenance logs and documentation for all active manufacturing machinery, including troubleshooting findings, completed PM actions, any failures, or repairs that occur.

• Perform critical lifts and rigging operations in accordance with applicable safety requirements and procedures.

• Support spare parts inventory management by identifying critical spares and ensuring adequate stock levels.

• Use machine tool manuals, technical documents, and internal and vendor resources to research machine issues.

• Identify and replace parts as necessary.

• Perform testing and commissioning as needed.

• Coordinate with external suppliers and maintenance companies to ensure timely and accurate completion of work.

• Partner with internal Kairos Power teams (Facilities, Construction, EHS, etc.) to support building improvement projects that directly impact manufacturing operations.

• In conjunction with the production team, will support continuous improvement of PM instructions and schedules to help prevent equipment failures.

• Perform manufacturing operations using 3- & 5-Axis CNC Milling, CNC lathe work, welding equipment, and hand tools.

• Support large assembly projects in collaboration with other team members.

• Support general facilities maintenance related to manufacturing areas and equipment.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

• High school diploma or general education degree (GED) and five years of experience and/or training in industrial equipment maintenance, machine tool repair, manufacturing equipment maintenance, or a related field; or equivalent combination of education and experience

• Experience operating and/or programming manual, semi-automated, or automated tools and machines (lathes, mills, grinders etc.)

• Experience with CNC controls and PLC troubleshooting and repairs

• Demonstrated proficiency in industrial mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic and electrical aptitude and repair

• Experience in production/manufacturing environment desirable

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Ability to read parts manuals, electrical and mechanical schematics, assembly instructions and troubleshooting guides

• Expert in rigging and critical lifts

• Ability to write routine reports and correspondence

• Mechanically inclined, able to work with a large variety of hand tools and power tools, operate a Forklift

• Advanced knowledge of CNC machine systems and operation

• Advanced knowledge of and experience with electrical test equipment, electrical, hydraulic and mechanical systems

• Advanced knowledge of industrial electrical systems and experience using electrical test equipment to troubleshoot and diagnose manufacturing equipment.

Physical Demands

• Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods

• Moving about to accomplish tasks or moving from one worksite to another

• Moving self in different positions to accomplish tasks in various environments including tight and confined spaces

• Ascending or descending ladders, stairs, scaffolding, ramps, scissor lifts, articulated boom lifts and the like

• Setting up and transferring temporary structures (e.g. scaffolding, ladders)

• Adjusting, moving, transporting, installing, positioning, or removing objects up to 25 pounds in all directions

• Communicating with others to exchange information

• Operating motor vehicles, heavy equipment or machinery

• Use hand tools

• Repetitive assembly operations of manufacturing test fixtures and test setups in collaboration with engineering and manufacturing teams

Environmental Conditions

• Low Temperatures

• High Temperatures

• Odors or fumes from chemicals or chemical reactions

• Assessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned

• High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced

• Elevated heights

Safety and PPE

• Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs

• Manipulating, cleaning and disposal of hazardous materials

• Reporting issues with equipment or unsafe conditions

• Color identification: detecting, distinguishing, recognizing and identifying colors

• Wearing proper personal protective equipment (PPE), which may include respiratory protection, face protection, gloves, safety footwear, and other PPE as required

Travel

Certification

• Ability to obtain and maintain forklift and boom lift certifications

Additional Requirements

• Regularly requires overtime

• Regularly requires working weekends

• Regularly requires schedule flexibility

• Occasionally requires non-standard work-week hours

• Occasionally requires working 2nd shift, beginning at 4:30pm local time

• Occasionally requires extended hours to support launch and critical project timelines

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Payroll Platform
jobs.description:
Please Note: This is a remote position available in the state listed on this job. Additionally, employment with BambooHR is contingent on passing both a background and credit check.

AI at BambooHR

At BambooHR, we're all about setting people free to do great work, and we believe AI is a powerful partner in that mission. We're leaning into intelligent tools to streamline our workflows, giving us more time for high-impact innovation. We look for curious, forward-thinking people who are ready to explore how AI can elevate their work and help us reimagine the future of HR.

Essential Job Duties

We're looking for a Sr. Product Manager to own the systems payroll runs on: data sync, calculation, payment operations tools, and the data model underneath them. You'll make sure payroll builds on BambooHR's shared platform services: canonical data entities, a permission service, an event bus, and an observability stack. You hold payroll to the contracts those services publish.

On a typical day you might sequence a migration step so no client's payday is ever the test case, agree on the direction of the payroll data model with payroll engineering leadership, or work out what it costs to keep an old system alive one more quarter. A new platform is still maturing while the old system carries production load.

You will:

• Own payroll platform modernization: decide what moves from old operational tools to their replacement, and when, and sequence each step so payroll is never at risk.

• Price the cost of keeping old systems running, including support escalations, manual fixes, and the risk of a missed pay date.

• Own the product half of the payroll data-model redesign, weighing event-driven streaming against the current full-resync approach, jointly with payroll engineering leadership. Validate it against the company's canonical entity models using real client examples.

• Own access and audit discipline on payroll systems: permission granularity, audit posture, least-privilege carve-outs, deny-by-default rollouts, and feature-flag discipline. Coordinate with the security organization and build on the platform's existing ways of recording who did what.

• Own compliance and retention for payroll: data retention positions, regulatory changes that affect payroll systems, and the audit interface with governance, risk, and compliance, documented as decisions rather than tribal knowledge.

• Test long-held assumptions about what payroll systems can and cannot do, publish the real limits and latency curves, and write them up so leadership can act on them.

• Run a payroll roadmap review cadence: a quarterly plan with dates, a weekly written status for leadership, and coordination with payroll services on operational readiness.

Success in the First 180 Days

• Deliver a dated plan for retiring the old systems with the cost of keeping each one priced, and retire at least one without a payroll incident.

• Land the payroll data-model direction as a written decision agreed with engineering.

• Make payroll's permission and audit setup the reference example other internal tools copy.

• Complete canonical-model validation for each payroll domain so payroll builds against platform contracts by default.

What You Need to Get the Job Done

• You feel aligned with the BambooHR values.

• 5+ years of product management experience. HCM, payroll, or payroll-adjacent platform experience is strongly preferred.

• You have coordinated with downstream consumers at scale: dozens of teams reading one system's contracts.

• Rollout discipline is a reflex for you: parallel runs, instant rollback, user acceptance testing, and release trains.

• You're technical enough to discuss database schemas, APIs, and migration mechanics with engineers as a peer.

• You're comfortable in regulated, sensitive-data domains and treat compliance counterparts as partners.

• You hold evidence standards in a domain full of inherited assumptions: you measure before you assert, and you write decisions down.

• You flag risks before deadlines.

What Will Make Us REALLY Love You

• Experience stewarding a legacy enterprise platform through a successor migration.

• Payments, money-movement, or banking-file operational experience.

• Familiarity with event-driven data architectures that replace batch and resync patterns.

• A developer background.

What You'll Love About Us

• A Great Company Culture that has been recognized by multiple organizations like Inc, and Salt Lake Tribune

• Comprehensive health, life, and disability insurance

• Generous leave policies that include 4 weeks of vacation, 12 company holidays, parental leave, and volunteer time off so you can enjoy quality of life

• 401k plans with up to 6% company match

• $2000 Paid-Paid Vacation bonus

• EAP through Headspace

• Check out all our benefits that benefit you

About Us

At BambooHR, we're building something different: we're building a people intelligence platform that transforms HR and sets people free to do great work! We're a proven market leader driving innovation while building lasting success through thoughtful, sustainable growth. Here, you'll find a place that champions growth: both professional and personal, both individual and collective.

We invest in potential, giving you the space to stretch your capabilities and turn good ideas into reality while providing the safety net of a supportive, values-driven culture. Our approach combines meaningful work with meaningful lives, offering competitive benefits, professional development, and the flexibility to thrive both in and outside the office.

What sets us apart isn't just what we do, but how we do it: with openness, integrity, and a shared commitment to doing the right thing. Join us in creating HR software that makes work better for everyone, while we make work better for you.

BambooHR is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals and will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process.  If you would like to request accommodations, please let your recruiter know.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Replication
jobs.description:
MongoDB’s Replication Team builds the infrastructure that enables high availability, fault tolerance, automatic failover, and tunable consistency. As a Senior Engineer on the team, you will design and implement distributed-systems features that protect data and keep applications available under demanding operating conditions.

You will work primarily in C++ on core database code, partner with engineers across MongoDB, and shape features central to major MongoDB releases. This is an opportunity to apply distributed-systems fundamentals to problems in data consistency, recovery time, replication performance, and operability.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based near one of our MongoDB office for our hybrid working model.

What you will do

• Design and implement production features across the replicated data lifecycle

• Improve restore and recovery workflows with attention to recovery time objectives

• Improve replication lag, throughput, and flow control; measure performance and prevent or resolve regressions

• Write production-quality C++ and the unit, integration, and system tests needed to demonstrate its correctness

• Use JavaScript and Python where appropriate to extend test coverage and validate end-to-end behavior

• Collaborate with partner engineering teams and stakeholders on large, cross-functional initiatives

• Investigate distributed-systems issues raised by customers and Technical Support, communicate findings clearly, and deliver durable fixes

• Participate in code reviews, design reviews, and technical discussions that improve the quality of the team’s work

• Interview candidates and mentor junior engineers and interns

What you bring

Required

• At least five years of experience programming, debugging, and performance-tuning distributed or highly concurrent software systems

• Strong systems fundamentals, including multithreaded programming, concurrency, debugging, and performance profiling

• Practical experience with distributed-systems concepts such as replication, data consistency and durability, recovery, fault tolerance, or consensus protocols

• Experience working with complex production codebases and diagnosing problems that cross system boundaries

• Strong written and verbal technical communication skills

• A collaborative approach and the ability to make realistic assessments of project complexity and delivery risk

Preferred

jobs.title: Field Test Operator- Excavator
jobs.description:
Position: Field Test Operator - Excavator

Location: Open

Travel: 100%

About Blue River

We’re Blue River, a team of innovators driven to create intelligent machinery that solves monumental problems for our customers. We empower our customers-farmers, construction crews, and foresters - to implement safer and more sustainable solutions, driving increased profitability and reducing reliance on scarce labor. We believe that focusing on the small stuff,  pixel-by-pixel and task-by-task  leads to big gains. With our partners at John Deere, we have the ability to bring innovative computer vision, machine learning, robotics, and product management solutions to scale production, maximizing their potential impact.

Our people are at the heart of what we do. Through cross-discipline collaboration, this mission-driven and daring team is eager to define the new frontier of mobile robotics. We are always asking hard questions, rapidly iterating, and getting our boots in the field and on-site to figure it out. We won’t give up until we’ve made a tangible and positive impact on the planet.

Summary

We’re developing the next generation of smart construction equipment, and we want the people who know excavators best helping us get it right. As our Field Test Operator, you’ll run a John Deere excavator outfitted with cameras and sensors at a test site, working alongside our field and engineering teams to test new machine technology in real digging conditions.

This isn’t a typical production seat. The goal isn’t to move the most dirt. It’s to do each task safely, smoothly, and consistently, and to tell our engineers what you’re seeing and why you run the machine the way you do. Your experience and feedback will directly shape how this equipment is designed, and you’ll get in early on the technology side of the industry. You don’t need a tech background. You need to know excavators inside and out, put safety first every day, communicate clearly, and be curious about where the industry is headed.

Other responsibilities could include serving as the in-cab safety operator during early technology testing, helping prep the test site and move machines, mentoring new operators as the team grows, and giving feedback on controls, attachments, and tooling. If the work calls for it, we’ll support you in earning additional certifications, such as an FAA Part 107 drone license.

The Field Test Operator reports to a Field Operations Manager or Field Test Site Manager, and takes day-to-day direction from the excavator program lead and engineering team during testing. The contract term is 12 months, with the possibility of extending or transitioning to full time. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Job Responsibilities

• Run a John Deere excavator through planned tasks from startup to shutdown, including digging, swinging, dumping, loading, trenching, and grading, following the data collection plan for each session

• Repeat the same task smoothly and consistently, run after run, so the data we collect is clean and reliable

• Talk through your work as you operate: what you see, what you plan to do next, and why you chose a certain bucket angle, approach, swing path, dig depth, or machine position

• Follow session procedures, including run naming, data logging steps, stop criteria, and incident reporting

• Write short notes after each session on what happened, what changed, and what you recommend next

• Perform daily walkarounds, routine preventive maintenance, and basic troubleshooting on the machine, including a check before each session that cameras and sensors are clean and recording

• Help engineers sort out whether a problem came from the machine, the site conditions, the plan, the sensors, or the test setup

Required Experience and Skills

• 3+ years of hands-on production experience operating excavators on real job sites

• Skills beyond truck loading, including trenching, bulk excavation, benching, grading, slope work, spoil placement, and working around utilities and obstacles in different soils

• A strong safety record and mature jobsite judgment around machine stability, blind spots, people on the ground, utilities, and changing ground conditions, with no risky shortcuts

• Mechanical aptitude, including a working understanding of hydraulics and machine limits, and comfort working around sensors, cameras, wiring, and computers mounted on the machine

• Comfortable using a tablet or laptop for checklists, digital work instructions, and simple data entry

• Clear communicator and steady teammate who can explain what you’re doing and why, out loud and in short written notes, and who carries themselves professionally on our site and customer sites

• Valid driver’s license, and willing to work outdoors and adjust your schedule when testing calls for it

• Willing to show your skills in a hands-on operating evaluation and to provide references who can speak to your safety record, such as a superintendent, foreman, safety lead, or project manager

Nice-to-Have Experience and Skills

• 5+ years of production excavator experience across a range of job types and site conditions

• Experience across multiple excavator brands and sizes, such as Deere, Caterpillar, Komatsu, Volvo, or Hitachi

• Experience on other earthmoving equipment, such as dozers, wheel loaders, rollers, or skid steers

• GPS/GNSS grade control systems, such as Trimble, Topcon, or Leica

• Time as a foreman, trainer, union instructor, equipment evaluator, or new-hire mentor

• NCCER Heavy Equipment Operator credentials, IUOE journeyman status, or equivalent documented training

• Experience with remote operation, machine automation features, prototype equipment, or field R&D testing

• Additional safety training, such as OSHA-30 or heavy-civil safety programs

Tools, equipment, and PPE are provided by the employer, and employer reimburses for all job required travel-related expenses. If you don’t already have an OSHA-10 card, we’ll provide the training after hire.

Compensation is hourly: $46.00 - $68.00 per hour, depending on experience

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to communicate verbally, including listening and speaking. This position requires sitting in an equipment cab for extended periods, along with standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, crouching, crawling, and climbing on and off equipment, often outdoors in cold and hot weather with dust, noise, and vibration. The employee must frequently lift and/or move items over 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move items over 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus. We are committed to building a diverse team and encourage applications from people of all backgrounds.

jobs.title: Business Development Representative
jobs.description:
TL;DR: Our Business Development team is growing to help fuel Listen Labs’ next phase of growth. This is not a traditional “dial-for-dollars” BD role. You’ll be building your own lead lists, showing up at conferences and events, developing real relationships, and helping shape how Listen Labs is viewed by the market.

If you’re hungry, extroverted, resilient, and excited to grind in a highly visible role at an early-stage startup- this is for you. Top performers will have a clear path to an Emerging AE or other Growth roles.



Background

Listen Labs is the world's fastest AI research platform, built so every company can understand what their customers want, why, and what to do about it. Our AI conducts in-depth interviews, analyzes conversations, and delivers executive-ready insights in hours, not weeks. Born out of a Harvard research project, Listen is trusted by teams at leading brands like Google, Microsoft, Anthropic, Perplexity, Sweetgreen, Replit, and Nestlé to bring real customer voices into their biggest product, marketing, and growth decisions.



Company highlights — entirely product-led:

Over 30% of our team are former founders, and multiple are competitive programming medalists.

 - Hypergrowth: Since launching, Listen has grown annualized revenue 15x and completed over 2 million interviews — backed by $100M in total funding led by Ribbit Capital, with Sequoia, Conviction, and Pear VC participating.

 - Traction: Already serving 15% of Fortune 100s. Enterprise wins and expansions across Anthropic, Microsoft, Nestlé, Perplexity, Sweetgreen, and more — with teams telling us research that used to take six to eight weeks now happens in days.



What You’ll Do

Lead Generation & Prospecting

 - Build and own your own prospect lists - identifying target companies, personas, and buying signals

 - Proactively source leads via outbound email, LinkedIn, cold calls, referrals, and creative channels

 - Research accounts deeply to personalize outreach and create thoughtful first touches

Events, Conferences & Relationship Building

 - Attend conferences, industry events, dinners, and meetups to represent Listen Labs

 - Network aggressively - spark conversations, build relationships, and follow up to turn interest into pipeline

 - Act as a brand ambassador: be “on,” be curious, and make people excited to talk to Listen

Qualification & Early Sales Motion

 - Run initial discovery calls to qualify inbound and outbound leads

 - Clearly articulate Listen’s value and identify strong handoffs to AEs / leadership

 - Procurement

DOSS is trusted by fast-growing operators to run critical operations with speed, control, and confidence.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Doss's Forward Deployed Services (FDS) team is the core engine of DOSS and the success of our customers. The Portfolio Manager sits at the intersection of product, data, operations, implementation, and customer partnership — leading a team of Forward Deployed Product Manager (FDPM) ICs while staying deeply hands-on yourself.

You'll own a portfolio of Doss's most complex, high-value client relationships and lead your team through the full post-sales lifecycle:

 - Discovery: partnering with cross-functional client leadership to analyze operational and financial workflows (flow of goods, information, and money)

 - Product Design: data model, workflows, and integrations

 - Build/Configure on the DOSS platform

 - UAT and Go-live

You'll manage a team of Forward Deployed Product Managers, setting the standard for quality and pace while staying in the weeds alongside your team. This is a player-coach role - you're not just directing, you're doing.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Lead a team of FDPMs across a portfolio of upper mid-market and enterprise clients — you're accountable for team output, client outcomes, and individual development

 - Stay hands-on across the end-to-end post-sales lifecycle: discovery, design, implementation, and go-live — this is a player-coach role and you'll be in the work, not above it

 - Own the success of Doss's most complex client relationships; your portfolio is a direct reflection of your team's execution

 - Conduct and lead cross-functional deep dives across customer organizations to map end-to-end business processes and workflows

 - Drive and contribute to new product capabilities that support Doss's push to upper mid-market and enterprise

 - Set the standard for best-in-class practices and processes across the team — build what doesn't exist, improve what does

 - Translate process flows into product design and configuration within the DOSS platform

 - Partner with technical teams on integrations and data migrations

 - Lead the portfolio through UAT, training, and go-live support across your portfolio; build relationships that drive retention and expansion

 - Coach your FDPM on client management, problem-solving frameworks, and delivery quality — and create the feedback loops that accelerate their growth

 - Drive automation and AI-forward improvements to Doss's product and customer lifecycle processes — we're an AI-native company and team




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years of experience in engineering, consulting, finance, operations, product operations, or technical program management, including time as a people manager with direct reports

 - ERP Implementation Leadership. You’ve managed a team through an ERP implementation (scoping, configuration, data migration, go-live). Strongly preferred, though we’ll also consider people who’ve led implementations of other complex B2B software or run professional services delivery teams.

 - Systems Thinker. Everything in our business is highly interconnected across people, process, and technology. You can traverse it, untangle it, and put it back together, and you can teach others to do the same.

 - Player-Coach Mentality. You lead by doing. You’re not the person who delegates everything and manages from a distance: you roll up your sleeves, model the work, and hold the bar.

 - High-Intensity. You’ve thrived in high-pressure environments (startups, consulting, finance), and that’s a real preference, not a stated one.

 - Technical from First Principles. You can grok hard engineering and logic problems from intuition, not memorization, and you can break them down for your team.

 - Intellectual Firepower. You cut through noise, synthesize fast, and make good calls under ambiguity.

 - Strong analytical mindset; SQL experience is a plus (not required)

jobs.title: Support Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RUNLAYER 


AI is transforming how every company operates, but most enterprises are stuck. They want to move fast with AI Agents, tools, and workflows, but they can't do it safely. We're fixing that.

 

Our team built AI Actions for OpenAI, shipped Zapier Agents to millions of users, and launched the first remote MCP server with Anthropic. We helped establish the protocol, and now we're building the platform enterprises need to actually put AI to work.

 

Runlayer is one platform for MCPs, Skills, and Agents: purpose-built security, fine-grained governance, and complete observability so organizations can go all-in on AI across the entire company without the risk. We just raised a $30M Series A led by Felicis, with participation from Khosla Ventures, bringing our total raised to $42M. Already trusted by Gusto, Instacart, Opendoor, dbt Labs, and Decagon.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As the founding Support Engineer at Runlayer, you'll be the technical frontline for enterprise customers deploying Runlayer across their engineering orgs. You'll work directly with customers in Pylon, Slack, and Teams to triage and resolve issues across the control plane, connectors, OAuth flows, deployment configs, and AI client integrations, and you'll build the support playbook from scratch as the bridge between customers and engineering.




WHY YOU'LL THRIVE HERE

 - Impact: Be the first support hire and the face of Runlayer to every enterprise customer in production.

 - Excellence: Work closely with the engineers who built the platform, and use AI tooling daily to do the job.

 - Ownership: Own the support function end to end, from triage and runbooks to the fixes that kill recurring tickets.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Work directly with customers in Pylon, Slack, and Teams to triage and resolve technical issues and bugs across the control plane, MCP connectors, OAuth, and deployments.

 - Use AI and MCP tooling to triage faster: diagnostic agents, log query templates, and reproduction workflows.

 - Guide enterprise teams through onboarding: first setup, SSO and SCIM, connector activation, and policy configuration.

 - Build the knowledge base from zero: runbooks, troubleshooting guides, and customer-facing docs for common deployment patterns (EKS, ECS, Helm, Terraform).

 - Manage escalations: debug what you can, and pull in Platform, SRE, or Identity engineers with clear reproduction steps when you can't.

 - Close the loop with product and engineering: turn recurring tickets into doc fixes, product fixes, and self-serve flows.

 - Learn and share new features as they ship each week, both to customers and across the team.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3-5 years in technical support, solutions engineering, or customer-facing engineering at SaaS or developer-tools companies.

 - An infrastructure support background, or strong technical depth in enterprise infra and AI systems like agents and identity.

 - Debugging fluency across the stack: you read Python/TypeScript, query PostgreSQL, trace HTTP requests, and interpret Kubernetes pod logs.

 - Familiarity with enterprise identity (SSO, SCIM, OAuth) and cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred: EKS/ECS, CloudWatch, VPCs).

 - Experience running support in Pylon and over Slack or Teams.

 - AI-native workflow: you use MCPs and AI tools daily to do real work

 - A drive to put customer satisfaction first and go above and beyond.

 - Excellent written communication: clear, concise explanations for both engineers and IT admins.

 - Zero-to-one mindset: comfortable defining your own SLAs, triage workflows, and escalation paths.




BONUS QUALIFICATIONS

 - Hands-on experience with MCP and how agents call tools in production.

 - Experience supporting security-critical or compliance-driven enterprise deployments.

 - Built support tooling or self-serve flows that measurably reduced ticket volume.




WHAT WE OFFER

We provide a competitive package designed to attract and retain top talent who can work effectively with enterprise customers.

 - Competitive salary and equity — compensation that reflects your expertise and customer-facing responsibilities.

 - Paid time off — paid vacation, paid sick leave, and paid parental leave.

 - Professional development — budget for conferences, courses, and certifications in AI, enterprise software, and customer success.

 - Top-tier equipment — your choice of laptop and accessories to create your ideal work environment.

 - Health benefits — comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.

 - Customer interaction opportunities — work directly with innovative companies and see the immediate impact of your work.



Not quite the right fit? Reach out to careers@runlayer.com careers@anysource.com with details about your experience and interests.

jobs.title: Manager – Welding & Process Improvement
jobs.description:
About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps expand the reach of the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Manager – Welding & Process Improvement is responsible for advancing welding technology, manufacturing processes, equipment standardization, automation, and continuous improvement across Loenbro's Fabrication & Manufacturing operations.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing, this position plays a key role in executing Loenbro's strategic plan by establishing and implementing standardized best practices across the fabrication network while continuously improving safety, quality, productivity, throughput, cost, and manufacturing capability. The Manager will assess existing fabrication practices, welding and cutting technologies, equipment, facility workflows, and manufacturing methods; develop practical, fit-for-purpose standards; and provide technical leadership for capital planning and equipment selection.

The successful candidate will combine deep welding and fabrication knowledge with manufacturing, automation, operational-excellence, and continuous-improvement expertise. The objective is to position Loenbro as a best-in-class manufacturing platform capable of safely and efficiently producing high-quality fabricated and manufactured products at scale.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Welding & Fabrication Process Standardization

• Assess welding, cutting, fitting, assembly, material-handling, and fabrication practices across Loenbro facilities and identify opportunities for standardization and improvement.

• Develop and implement company-wide fabrication and manufacturing best practices that are scalable across multiple facilities and appropriate for individual products, markets, and operating requirements.

• Establish standardized processes, methods, equipment recommendations, workstation concepts, tooling, production practices, standard work, and technical guidance, defining what good looks like across the network.

• Ensure processes are fit for purpose and aligned with applicable codes, specifications, customer requirements, and quality programs, supporting a manufacturing culture centered on safety, quality, and continuous improvement.

Welding Technology & Technical Leadership

• Serve as a technical resource for welding processes and fabrication methodologies across Loenbro's manufacturing network.

• Evaluate processes and technologies based on material type, wall thickness, joint configuration, production volume, quality requirements, labor availability, and total cost.

• Partner with Quality and Welding Engineering regarding WPS/PQR requirements, welder qualifications, code compliance, inspection requirements, and weld quality.

• Analyze weld productivity, repair rates, deposition efficiency, arc-on time, and rework to identify opportunities to reduce labor and non-value-added work, and evaluate emerging welding technologies for practical advantage.

Cutting, Preparation & Material Processing

• Assess and optimize cutting, beveling, coping, drilling, forming, preparation, and material-processing methods.

• Evaluate CNC plasma, oxy-fuel, laser cutting, saw systems, automated pipe profiling, robotic cutting, beveling systems, and other applicable fabrication equipment.

• Develop standardized approaches that improve dimensional accuracy, throughput, fit-up quality, material utilization, and downstream welding productivity.

• Identify opportunities to integrate digital fabrication data with cutting and manufacturing equipment to reduce manual inputs and errors.

Automation & Advanced Manufacturing

• Identify and evaluate welding automation, robotics, mechanized welding, automated cutting, positioning, material-handling, and other advanced manufacturing opportunities.

• Evaluate robotic and collaborative welding, orbital welding, automated pipe welding, CNC systems, positioners, manipulators, turning rolls, and related technologies.

• Develop business cases based on production demand, labor savings, throughput, quality, safety, utilization, payback, maintainability, and scalability, ensuring technology selections are supported by sustainable production demand.

• Work with Engineering & Productization to optimize products and assemblies for automated manufacturing and repeatable production.

Capital Expenditure & Equipment Strategy

• Lead or support technical evaluation of Fabrication & Manufacturing capital expenditures, developing standardized evaluation criteria covering capability, capacity, reliability, productivity, safety, quality, and total cost of ownership.

• Prepare capital business cases, recommendations, and a multi-year equipment roadmap aligned with strategic priorities and anticipated market demand.

• Identify opportunities to standardize platforms across facilities to improve training, maintenance, spare parts, consumables, purchasing leverage, and workforce flexibility.

• Participate in trials, vendor demonstrations, factory acceptance testing, commissioning, and performance validation, and develop productive relationships with leading equipment suppliers.

Manufacturing Process Improvement

• Lead improvement initiatives focused on safety, quality, productivity, throughput, cost, schedule, and capacity.

• Assess workflows from material receipt through cutting, preparation, fit-up, welding, inspection, coating, assembly, storage, and shipment, identifying bottlenecks, excessive movement, waiting, rework, and other waste.

• Apply Lean manufacturing, 5S, value-stream mapping, standard work, visual management, and root-cause analysis where appropriate, recommending improvements to shop layout, production cells, and material flow.

• Partner with Operations to implement improvements, validate benefits, and sustain results.

Productivity & Performance Measurement

• Establish meaningful, standardized productivity metrics for welding and fabrication operations.

• Track and analyze direct labor hours per unit, weld/diameter inches, arc-on time, deposition rates, repair and rejection rates, fit-up productivity, machine utilization, uptime, cycle time, rework, and scrap.

• Benchmark performance among facilities and against relevant industry practices, using operational data to prioritize improvement opportunities and validate results.

Shop Assessments & Manufacturing Excellence

• Participate in formal facility assessments in support of the Manufacturing strategic plan and Tiger Team workstreams.

• Evaluate facilities against standards for welding, cutting, equipment, layout, material flow, productivity, automation, quality, safety, and manufacturing maturity.

• Develop prioritized facility improvement roadmaps and facilitate adoption of proven internal best practices across the network.

• Support decisions on where capabilities should be consolidated, expanded, automated, or strategically developed, and assist in defining future-state concepts for new or expanded facilities.

Engineering & Productization Collaboration

• Work closely with the Director of Engineering & Productization to incorporate Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) principles into repeatable products and assemblies.

• Provide manufacturing input during development to improve manufacturability, reduce labor, simplify welding and assembly, and enable automation.

• Standardize materials, connections, joint configurations, components, and fabrication methods where beneficial.

• Participate in design reviews, prototypes, pilot production, first-article builds, and production-readiness assessments, and help transition successful prototypes into scalable production processes.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

• Partner with Quality and Safety leadership to ensure improvements maintain or enhance compliance with applicable codes, specifications, procedures, and customer requirements.

• Promote practices that reduce ergonomic exposure, manual handling, fumes, heat exposure, repetitive work, and other fabrication-related risks.

• Ensure equipment recommendations address guarding, ventilation, ergonomics, training, maintenance, and safe operation.

• Participate in root-cause investigations involving significant welding, fabrication, equipment, or process failures, and support continuous reduction of defects, repairs, rework, and quality escapes.

Training & Workforce Development

• Identify training needs associated with standardized processes, new equipment, automation, and manufacturing technologies.

• Partner with Operations, Quality, Safety, and Training personnel to develop practical training programs and operator competency expectations.

• Develop welding and fabrication subject-matter experts and facilitate knowledge sharing among facilities.

Key Performance Indicators

• Fabrication labor productivity and throughput improvement.

• Reduction in weld repair/rejection rates, rework, and cost per unit.

• Improvement in arc-on time, deposition efficiency, equipment utilization, and uptime.

• Reduction in production cycle time and improvement in material flow.

• Percentage of facilities operating to standardized manufacturing practices.

• Capital-project ROI and achievement of planned benefits.

• Automation utilization and verified productivity improvement.

• Number of standardized processes deployed across multiple facilities.

• Successful implementation of new technologies and equipment.

• Improvement in manufacturing safety and ergonomic exposure.

Key Qualifications

• 8+ years of progressive experience in welding, fabrication, manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, process improvement, or related industrial operations.

• Extensive practical knowledge of industrial welding and fabrication processes, equipment, cutting systems, material preparation, fit-up, positioning, and workflow.

• Experience evaluating or implementing manufacturing equipment and capital projects.

• Demonstrated success improving fabrication productivity, quality, throughput, or manufacturing processes.

• Ability to interpret engineering and fabrication drawings, welding symbols, specifications, and applicable requirements.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving capability with the ability to turn shop-floor observations and production data into practical improvements.

• Ability to collaborate effectively with craft personnel, supervision, engineering, quality, safety, vendors, and executive leadership.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills and willingness to travel regularly among Loenbro facilities.

• Bachelor's degree in Welding Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Welding Technology, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent extensive industry experience considered.

• Certified Welding Inspector (CWI), Certified Welding Engineer (CWEng), or other relevant AWS credential preferred.

• Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or similar continuous-improvement certification preferred.

• Experience with robotic, mechanized, orbital, or automated pipe welding; CNC/laser/plasma cutting; automated material handling; or other advanced manufacturing technologies preferred.

• Experience with ASME, AWS, API, or other applicable fabrication codes and standards preferred.

• Experience supporting mission critical/data centers, power generation, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, energy, mining, water/wastewater, or related industrial markets preferred.

• Experience in both project-based fabrication and high-volume or repeatable manufacturing environments preferred.

• Experience developing equipment ROI analyses and multi-year capital-investment plans preferred.

Core Competencies: Manufacturing Excellence | Welding Technology | Fabrication Operations | Continuous Improvement | Lean Manufacturing | Automation | Capital Equipment Evaluation | Process Standardization | Productivity Improvement | Technical Problem Solving | Manufacturing Engineering | DfMA | Change Management | Cross-Functional Leadership

Education

Physical Demands and Work Environment

jobs.title: Oncology Care Manager Lead - Full Time - Wolf River
jobs.description:
Job Title: Oncology Care Manager Lead

About Us

At West Cancer Center, we are committed to providing exceptional, patient-centered cancer care through collaboration, compassion, and clinical excellence. Our team works together to coordinate comprehensive care, improve patient outcomes, and support patients and their families throughout their cancer treatment journey.

Position Overview

The Oncology Care Manager Lead serves as the department representative for Value-Based Care Committee meetings and is responsible for reporting and data collection related to the Value-Based Care Manager role. This position oversees the Value-Based Care Manager team, provides training for new team members, and serves as a resource for staff.

The Oncology Care Manager Lead is also responsible for the healthcare management of oncology patients participating in value-based care programs. This includes matching patient needs with appropriate services, maintaining and updating patient records, reviewing clinical diagnoses and treatments, and ensuring compliance with required practice redesign elements. This position models appropriate behavior as exemplified in the Mission, Vision, and Values of West Cancer Center.

Key Responsibilities

• Attend Value-Based Care meetings and provide updates regarding Value-Based Care Manager processes, patient enrollment volumes, and program-related issues

• Collaborate with data teams to review metrics related to program progress

• Review reports for accuracy and work with EMR and data teams to correct reporting issues

• Assign patients to the Value-Based Care Manager team

• Serve as a resource and trainer for Value-Based Care Managers regarding patient interactions, patient management and interventions, documentation, and patient referrals

• Collaborate with clinic leadership to integrate the Value-Based Care Manager role into clinic operations and ensure cohesive workflows with nursing and clinic staff

• Provide feedback regarding the job performance of Value-Based Care Management staff

• Serve as a central point of contact to effectively manage patients at high risk for complications while eliminating redundant services

• Utilize a collaborative process of assessment, planning, facilitation, care coordination, evaluation, and advocacy to meet individual healthcare needs and promote quality, cost-effective outcomes

• Collaborate with the patient's primary care team, particularly the nurse navigator, to ensure coordinated care without overlap or redundancy

• Identify and decrease healthcare barriers by assessing the needs of patients, families, and caregivers and providing anticipatory guidance and education

• Provide appropriate clinical interventions within the scope of nursing practice and clinical training

• Educate patients regarding general preventive care practices and reinforce individualized care plans to prevent unnecessary admissions, readmissions, and overutilization of resources

• Track patient progress and outcomes, adjusting care plans as needed in collaboration with the oncologist

• Coordinate patient appointments, communicate with physicians and specialists, contact outside agencies and organizations, and arrange additional services to support patient care and well-being

• Assist patients in managing their health conditions, prioritizing healthcare needs, preventing complications through standardized care protocols, and navigating the healthcare system

• Assist with transitions of care following hospital discharge, ensuring a seamless return to the outpatient setting, management of discharge medications, and scheduling of follow-up appointments

• Collaborate with provider clinic staff to ensure accurate documentation of staging, oncology/hematology diagnoses, other medical conditions, and pertinent clinical information

• Supervise the Value-Based Care Manager team

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Required:

• Bachelor's degree in Nursing (BSN)

• At least three (3) years of nursing experience, including one (1) year of Case Management experience

Preferred:

• Master's degree

• Oncology Case Management experience

Credential/Licensure

Required:

• Current Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state where work is performed or a compact nursing license

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• Knowledge of healthcare management resources to match patient needs with appropriate services

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, strong problem-solving abilities, and effective conflict resolution skills

• Proficiency in Microsoft applications, including Word and Excel, and knowledge of security measures and legislation regarding patient privacy

• Ability to communicate effectively with associates at all levels, physicians, patients, and families

• Ability to work without close supervision and exercise independent judgment

• Ability to organize multiple tasks and projects and maintain control of workflow

Work Environment & Physical Demands

• Physical activities may include climbing, pushing, standing, hearing, walking, reaching, grasping, kneeling, stooping, and repetitive motion

• Must have good balance and coordination

• Medium work requiring exertion of up to 50 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 25 pounds of force frequently

• Close visual acuity, including color, depth perception, and field of vision, is required for activities such as assessing patients, preparing and analyzing data and figures, transcribing, viewing a computer terminal, and extensive reading

• Frequent invasive and non-invasive patient contact

• Exposure to patient body fluids as well as hazardous or poisonous materials

• Ability to react quickly to emergency situations

Why West Cancer Center is a Great Place to Work

• Meaningful Impact: Play a direct role in supporting patients through one of the most challenging times of their lives.

• Collaborative Culture: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of dedicated professionals committed to improving cancer care.

• Professional Development: Benefit from ongoing training, educational resources, and growth opportunities.

• Mission-Driven Environment: Be part of an organization guided by compassion, integrity, and innovation.

No nights, weekends, or holidays. Comprehensive benefits package.

Join Us

If you are an experienced Registered Nurse with a passion for oncology care management, strong leadership skills, and a commitment to improving patient outcomes, we encourage you to apply for the Oncology Care Manager Lead position at West Cancer Center. Join our team and help lead initiatives that enhance care coordination, support patients throughout their cancer journey, and promote quality, patient-centered care.

jobs.title: Growth Lead
jobs.description:
THE ROLE

You'll be the first senior growth hire at Numeric and establish the demand generation engine that unlocks the next level of scale.



Numeric recently launched the Financial Data Platform, an ERP replacement that’s a fundamentally new take https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PTJcGupdBJg&xstg=CAMSEBUJ_b-oH-PhF0yjBgb_zzE%3D on a centuries old way of doing accounting. This isn’t an incremental product that’s 15% better than what’s existed before. This is a totally new way of doing the work.



The year ahead will be a big one for the company - the FDP is getting attention - it’s your role to convert that attention into pipeline and drive awareness to help attract best fit customers.



It’s a fairly unique spot to be in. You’ll get the testing & building from scratch that typically comes with a Seed / Series A company role for the newer product. But you’ll also inherit working demand gen motions, hundreds of happy customers, and a content and product marketing team to support your work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

This role will report into Numeric’s Head of Marketing. In the position, you will:

 - Act as a player coach to start with 2-3 direct reports and overtime expand the growth function.

 - Map campaigns and channels to pipeline growth across products, partnering closely with a working BDR motion.

 - Build an enterprise ABM motion to penetrate top target accounts.

 - Own paid channels (with agency support) as our chief experimenter.

 - Partner with product marketing and content leadership to create strong feedback loops and share growth learnings.

 - Set the quality bar for growth at Numeric: world-class editing, feedback, and coaching along with leading by example with your own strong deliverables.

 - Form a clear point of view on what growth should be as AI reshapes the discipline and help ensure Numeric remains on the edge of what’s possible.
   
   

Few hires have the potential to shape a company’s trajectory like this one. There’s a ton of whitespace to run at and a supportive founding team who understands the value of marketing.




WHO YOU ARE



 - 7+ years of experience, with 5+ years in growth marketing.

 - You've owned growth end-to-end —you've defined what to work on, not just executed against someone else's plan.

 - You dive in. It’s clear to your teammates that you care about your work, the company, and the people around you. You raise your hand in the classroom of life - you ask questions, you bring ideas, and you are invested.

 - You’re a blend of scientist and creative. You love a spreadsheet just as much as a sticky note. (See here https://www.numeric.io/blog/cash-cab and here https://heyzine.com/flip-book/cb26d7b0ad.html for a few examples of Numeric marketing creativity in action!)

 - You're a strong editor and coach who raises the quality of everyone around you.

 - You've marketed a technical B2B product (not purely consumer).

 - You’re serious about excellent work - but not serious about yourself. You view a great team as one that both laughs together and creates magic together.




NICE TO HAVE

 - You’ve worked in both smaller start-up settings (Series A / Seed) and seen scale firsthand (Series C+).

 - Experience in accounting, finance, or fintech.

 - A background (or exposure to) events marketing.




ABOUT NUMERIC

Backed by IVP, Menlo, and Founders Fund most recently in a $81M Series B, Numeric's tackling one of the most technically challenging (and durable!) arenas of tech today. 

The TL;DR: Accounting runs on a data model that's centuries old. While Salesforce reinvented the customer database and Rippling the employee record, the financial database has remained constrained by the journal entry. The output is a sprawl of tools, Excel files acting as a databases, and AI that's hand-cuffed by lack of context.

Until Numeric. 

Numeric's vision is to make the system of record the system of decision. A world where every role at every company can make better, real-time decisions with their financial data. Instead of seeing accounting work as spreadsheet driven, we believes in a world where 'finance engineers' are architecting a system that looks more like a modern data platform than today's ERPs. 

The market is massive. The timing is right for reinvention. And we've assembled an invested and talented (often silly) team to make the magic happen. If you're serious about your work and not too serious about yourself, you'll love working here :)

jobs.title: Engineering & Productization Manager – Fabrication & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps expand the reach of the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Engineering & Productization Manager is responsible for converting market demand and project opportunities into standardized, repeatable, and commercially viable fabricated and manufactured solutions that advance Loenbro's transformation from project-specific fabrication toward a scalable manufacturing platform.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing, this role leads the technical development and productization of fully integrated modular solutions for Loenbro's targeted end markets. The Manager will establish strategic working relationships with engineering and packaging firms, developers, owners, general contractors, EPCs, OEMs, technology providers, and internal Loenbro operating groups to identify recurring needs, shape basis-of-design requirements, and create solutions optimized for off-site manufacturing and field installation.

The position will be the technical integrator for Loenbro's hub-and-spoke manufacturing model, with repeatable products and modules engineered for final assembly, integration, testing, and shipment through designated manufacturing hubs, while components and subassemblies are allocated to spoke facilities wherever capability, capacity, quality, logistics, and economics support the work. The successful candidate will combine engineering leadership, design management, product-development discipline, manufacturing knowledge, commercial judgment, and strong external relationship skills — moving concepts through design, validation, pilot production, standard release, configuration control, and continuous improvement.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Productization Strategy & Portfolio Development

• Develop and execute an engineering and productization roadmap aligned with Loenbro's Fabrication & Manufacturing strategic plan, growth priorities, available capabilities, and targeted end markets.

• Identify recurring customer needs, project scopes, assemblies, and system configurations suitable for standardization, modularization, cataloging, and repeatable production.

• Prioritize product-development investments using market demand, strategic customer pull, addressable volume, margin, capacity utilization, technical feasibility, capital needs, and speed to market.

• Maintain a stage-gate portfolio from opportunity and concept through business case, engineering, prototype, validation, commercialization, standard release, and lifecycle management.

Strategic Partnerships & Early Market Engagement

• Develop strategic relationships with engineering and packaging firms, developers, owners, hyperscalers, general contractors, EPCs, OEMs, technology providers, and other partners capable of accelerating standardized modular solutions.

• Lead technical engagement in design-assist, early contractor involvement, basis-of-design development, constructability workshops, and product-definition sessions.

• Establish clear partnership models addressing responsibilities, intellectual property, design ownership, licensing, exclusivity, confidentiality, engineering liability, and continuous improvement.

• Represent Loenbro's technical and productization capabilities in customer presentations, industry forums, conferences, and strategic partner meetings, translating partner and customer insight into actionable product requirements.

Integrated Modular Solution Development

• Lead development of fully integrated modular systems combining mechanical, piping, structural, electrical, controls, equipment, insulation, testing, and other disciplines as applicable.

• Create repeatable solutions including electrical prefabrication assemblies, electrical and mechanical skids, cooling and liquid-cooling assemblies, modular piping systems, pipe racks, utility modules, power packages, and process modules.

• Define module boundaries, battery limits, interfaces, connection strategies, transportation envelopes, lifting concepts, installation sequencing, commissioning approach, and turnover requirements.

• Coordinate multidisciplinary design reviews and resolve interface risks before release to procurement and manufacturing, ensuring solutions address total installed cost and lifecycle value.

Hub-and-Spoke Manufacturing Integration

• Develop engineering and work-allocation strategies that enable final integration and testing at designated hubs while distributing components and subassemblies to capable spoke facilities.

• Partner with Operations and project leadership to map facility capabilities, capacity, labor, equipment, certifications, geography, logistics, and cost to product work breakdown structures.

• Design products with clear manufacturing breakdown structures, standardized interfaces, controlled tolerances, kitting requirements, quality hold points, and assembly instructions that support multi-facility execution.

• Recommend make/buy and hub/spoke allocation decisions and develop repeatable handoff, packaging, shipping, and traceability requirements for work moving between facilities.

Engineering Management & Design Governance

• Plan, lead, and coordinate internal and external engineering resources, including discipline engineers, designers, BIM/VDC personnel, consultants, and specialty partners.

• Establish design criteria, engineering execution plans, deliverable registers, schedules, budgets, reviews, approval workflows, and responsibility matrices.

• Ensure designs comply with applicable codes, standards, contractual requirements, professional-practice obligations, customer specifications, and Loenbro quality systems.

• Manage outsourced engineering performance, scope, schedule, cost, and quality, and ensure appropriate professional review, stamping, and jurisdictional compliance through qualified engineering entities.

Design for Manufacturing & Assembly

• Embed Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA) principles in products to simplify fabrication, reduce part count and labor, improve repeatability, enable automation, and minimize field work.

• Standardize materials, components, connections, joint configurations, dimensional schemes, equipment selections, controls interfaces, and fabrication processes where beneficial.

• Partner with the Welding & Process Improvement Manager, Quality, Supply Chain, shop leadership, and craft subject-matter experts to ensure designs match production capabilities and improvement roadmaps.

• Facilitate design-to-cost, value-engineering, constructability, and production-readiness reviews before design release, using production and field feedback to continually improve standard designs.

Prototype, Validation & Production Readiness

• Plan and lead prototypes, mockups, pilot builds, first-article production, factory acceptance testing, and product validation activities.

• Define measurable acceptance criteria for performance, quality, safety, manufacturability, cost, cycle time, installation, commissioning, and repeatability.

• Document lessons learned, resolve design and process issues, and complete formal production-readiness reviews before scalable release.

• Establish controlled work instructions, inspection and test plans, tooling requirements, training materials, and quality records with Operations and Quality, confirming that capacity, supply chain, and skills support forecast demand.

Configuration, Intellectual Property & Lifecycle Management

Commercialization & Cross-Functional Execution

Target End-Market Development

Leadership, Systems & Continuous Improvement

A Day in the Life

Customer Sales & Profit

General Information

Team & Development

Retail Operations/ Visual & Commercial Execution

Who You Are
