jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager - Seller Experience (Remote)
jobs.description:
Who is Trace3?

Trace3 is a leading Transformative IT Authority, providing unique technology solutions and consulting services to our clients. Equipped with elite engineering and dynamic innovation, we empower IT executives and their organizations to achieve competitive advantage through a process of Integrate, Automate, Innovate.

Our culture at Trace3 embodies the spirit of a startup with the advantage of a scalable business. Employees can grow their career and have fun while doing it!

Trace3 is headquartered in Irvine, California. We employ more than 1,200 people all over the United States. Our major field office locations include Denver, Indianapolis, Grand Rapids, Lexington, Los Angeles, Louisville, Texas, San Francisco.

Ready to discover the possibilities that live in technology?

Come Join Us!

Street-Smart - Thriving in Dynamic Times

We are flexible and resilient in a fast-changing environment. We continuously innovate and drive constructive change while keeping a focus on the “big picture.” We exercise sound business judgment in making high-quality decisions in a timely and cost-effective manner. We are highly creative and can dig deep within ourselves to find positive solutions to different problems.

Juice - The “Stuff” it takes to be a Needle Mover

We get things done and drive results. We lead without a title, empowering others through a can-do attitude. We look forward to the goal, mentally mapping out every checkpoint on the pathway to success, and visualizing what the final destination looks and feels like.

Teamwork - Humble, Hungry and Smart

We are humble individuals who understand how our job impacts the company's mission. We treat others with respect, admit mistakes, give credit where it’s due and demonstrate transparency. We “bring the weather” by exhibiting positive leadership and solution-focused thinking. We hug people in their trials, struggles, and failures – not just their success. We appreciate the individuality of the people around us.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

The Sr. Program Manager, Seller Experience, owns the end-to-end experience of Trace3's sellers and leads the systematic removal of friction across the sales process. This role is responsible for building and managing a seller listening program that identifies productivity barriers, translating insights into prioritized process and technology improvements, and driving those initiatives from analysis and design through documentation, training, adoption, and measurable business impact.

Sellers are the customers of this function. Through direct observation, feedback, and data analysis, this leader will develop productivity benchmarks, establish operational health metrics, and oversee the intake process for seller-related tools, systems, and process enhancement requests across Revenue Operations.

In partnership with HR, IT, and Revenue leaders, this role will also own new seller ramp acceleration, change management, and adoption strategies for all Revenue Operations initiatives. Success is measured not only by what is delivered, but by seller adoption, productivity gains, and improvements in sales performance. Adoption is how we define done.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

Seller Listening Program

• Build and lead seller advisory board, nominated by regional sales leaders, and serve as the voice of the field within Revenue Operations.

• Gather and analyze seller feedback, workflow observations, and productivity data to identify barriers to selling effectiveness.

• Measure and monitor seller satisfaction and experience across regions, segments, and roles.

• Maintain a prioritized backlog of seller productivity opportunities and improvement initiatives.

Process Improvement, Documentation, and Adoption

• Lead continuous improvement initiatives that streamline sales processes, reduce administrative burden, and improve seller productivity.

• Evaluate current-state processes, identify inefficiencies, and design scalable solutions that drive measurable business outcomes.

• Establish and maintain process documentation, standards, and governance practices across Revenue Operations.

• Drive successful rollout, training, and adoption of new processes, tools, and capabilities.

• Manage intake, prioritization, and roadmap planning for seller-facing process and technology improvements.

Measurement and Baselines

• Define and maintain key performance indicators related to seller productivity, adoption, effectiveness, and experience.

• Develop reporting and performance benchmarks to track the impact of Revenue Operations initiatives.

• Measure and communicate realized business value, including productivity gains, process efficiencies, and adoption outcomes.

• Partner with leadership to identify trends, risks, and opportunities that improve sales execution.

Onboarding, Ramp, and Certification

• Partner with POH, Sales Leadership, and IT to continuously improve the new seller onboarding and ramp experience.

• Develop frameworks, measurements, and programs that accelerate time-to-productivity for new sellers.

• Support role-based enablement, certification, and readiness programs aligned with sales motions and business objectives.

• Monitor ramp effectiveness and recommend enhancements based on performance data and seller feedback.

Change Management

• Lead change management efforts for Revenue Operations initiatives, ensuring successful adoption and sustained behavioral change.

• Develop communication, training, and reinforcement strategies that maximize seller engagement and utilization.

• Serve as a seller advocate in cross-functional decision making, ensuring seller productivity and experience are considered in prioritization and trade-off discussions.

• Establish adoption measures and accountability mechanisms to validate success and business impact.

Cross-Functional Leadership

• Partner closely with Sales Leadership, HR, Marketing, IT, Finance, Customer Experience, and Transformation teams to deliver seller-focused solutions.

• Build alignment across stakeholder groups and influence outcomes without direct authority.

• Lead through collaboration, data-driven decision making, and a customer-first mindset with sellers as the primary customer.

QUALIFICATIONS & INTERESTS:

• Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.

• 7+ years of experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Business Operations, Process Improvement, Sales Enablement, or a related function, including at least 3 years leading enterprise programs from strategy through execution.

• Demonstrated expertise in process improvement methodologies, with Lean, Six Sigma (Yellow Belt or higher), or comparable training and experience strongly preferred.

• Experience building and operating customer, employee, or seller experience programs, including structured feedback and listening mechanisms.

• Proven track record leading process improvement initiatives from discovery and analysis through implementation, documentation, training, change management, and measurable adoption.

• Experience designing and managing structured feedback programs such as advisory boards, seller councils, surveys, voice-of-the-customer programs, workflow observations, or similar mechanisms.

• Strong analytical and quantitative skills, including the ability to establish performance baselines, define success metrics, and communicate insights to executive stakeholders.

• Experience working with CRM, ERP, sales enablement, and related business systems, with a strong understanding of seller workflows and revenue processes.

• Experience partnering cross-functionally with Sales, People Operations, IT, Marketing, Finance, and other business functions to drive organizational change.

• Experience supporting onboarding, training, certification, adoption, or enablement programs that improve employee productivity and performance.

• Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and drive alignment across organizations without direct authority.

• Strong executive presence and exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, including experience presenting recommendations and results to senior leadership.

• Highly organized with the ability to manage multiple priorities and drive results in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Actual salary will be based on a variety of factors, including location, experience, skill set, performance, licensure and certification, and business needs. The range for this position in other geographic locations may differ. Certain positions may also be eligible for variable incentive compensation, such as bonuses or commissions, that is not included in the base salary.

Estimated Pay Range

$160,000—$175,000 USD

The Perks

• Comprehensive medical, dental and vision plans for you and your dependents

• 401(k) Retirement Plan with Employer Match, 529 College Savings Plan, Health Savings Account, Life Insurance, and Long-Term Disability

• Competitive Compensation

• Training and development programs

• Major offices stocked with snacks and beverages

• Collaborative and cool culture

• Work-life balance and generous paid time off

Our Commitment

At the core of Trace3's DNA is our people. We are a diverse group of talented individuals who understand the importance of teamwork and demonstrating leadership, character, and passion in all that we do.

We’re committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to grow. We recognize that embracing diversity drives innovation, improves outcomes, fosters collaboration, boosts teammate satisfaction, and builds a more inclusive culture.

As an equal opportunity employer, Trace3 bases all employment decisions based on individual qualifications, merit, and business requirements. We do not engage in discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

Any demographic information provided is strictly voluntary, kept confidential in accordance with Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) regulations, and will not be used in employment decisions, including hiring, promotions, or mentorship programs. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all.

If you require a reasonable accommodation to complete the application process or participate in an interview, please email recruiting@trace3.com.

jobs.description:

Who we are

CloudKitchens helps restaurateurs around the world succeed in online food delivery - our goal is to make food more affordable, higher quality, and convenient for everyone.

We take underutilized properties and transform them into smart kitchens so they can better serve restaurateurs, customers, and the neighborhoods they’re in. Every time we launch a new facility, we create jobs in that neighborhood, and we’re proud to provide a wide range of cuisines and options for healthy food at an affordable price.

We're changing the game for restaurateurs, whether they’re entrepreneurs opening their first restaurant, all the way through to your favorite global quick-service restaurant chains.

This isn’t a typical HVAC job chasing random service calls.

• Work on modern, standardized commercial kitchen facilities

• Predictable environments → faster diagnostics, less guesswork

• Mix of hands-on repair + system troubleshooting + facility support

• Opportunity to grow into Facilities or Regional leadership roles

• Be part of a rapidly growing operation in a $100B+ industry

HVAC/R & Facilities Maintenance

Facility Operations Support

System Performance & Troubleshooting

• Use Building Management Systems (BMS) to monitor performance and diagnose issues

New Site Support

• Assist with new facility openings by verifying installation and system functionality

• Identify issues early and coordinate corrective actions

What Your Week Looks Like

• 70% hands-on HVAC/R maintenance & repair

• 20% troubleshooting & diagnostics (onsite + remote)

• 10% inspections, reporting, and system verification

What we’re looking for

Required

• 5+ years of commercial HVAC/R experience

• Experience working with rooftop units, ventilation systems, or refrigeration(Walk-Ins)

• Strong troubleshooting and diagnostic skills

• Valid driver’s license and ability to travel between sites locally

Preferred

• HVAC Universal certification (EPA, trade school, or equivalent)

Work Environment & Schedule

• Field-based role across the Greater DMV Area

• Local travel between sites (home daily)

• Monday–Friday schedule with on-call rotation and overtime opportunities

Why join us

• Demand for online food delivery is growing really fast! In the last 5 years, just in the US, the overall market has expanded 10X from $10B to $100B, and could expand to $500B- $1T by 2030.

• Changing the restaurant industry: You’ll be part of a team that helps restaurants succeed in online food delivery.

Compensation & Benefits

• 401(k)

• Paid time off

• Life insurance

• Company-provided device (laptop/tablet)

Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.

About this role

We are seeking an experienced Executive Recruiter with 10+ years of progressive recruiting experience, specializing in the identification, engagement, and placement of top-tier VP and SVP level talent. This role is responsible for managing the entire executive search lifecycle and partnering closely with senior leadership to execute effective talent acquisition strategies for mission-critical leadership roles.

This will be an opportunity to contribute to building a leadership team that reflects our values and diverse perspectives, while also helping to define a world-class executive recruiting experience.

What you’ll do

• Lead and manage full-lifecycle executive search processes for VP and SVP level positions, both in the US and abroad, including sourcing, assessment, interviewing, offer negotiation, and onboarding readiness.

• Partner with C-level executives and senior stakeholders to develop position specifications and create targeted recruitment strategies aligned with business objectives.

• Advise hiring managers and interview panels on best practices for executive recruitment, interview techniques, and selection criteria.

• Maintain up-to-date knowledge of market trends, compensation benchmarking, and competitive intelligence for executive talent.

• Ensure compliance with all relevant employment laws and company policies.

What you’ll bring

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

• 10+ years of progressive experience in executive recruiting, with a focus on VP and SVP level placements. Technology-industry experience is strongly preferred.

• Demonstrated expertise in managing full-cycle executive search processes within a dynamic environment that values adaptability and balance.

• Strong collaborative communication skills, with the ability to build trust across diverse teams.

• Proven ability to build relationships with senior leaders and influence decision-making.

• Deep knowledge of executive search methodologies, assessment tools, and talent mapping.

• A process-oriented mindset that leverages data to develop pipeline and funnel metrics that enable data-driven decision making and reporting.

• A high degree of professionalism, discretion, and confidentiality.

• An enthusiasm for building new processes creating a world-class candidate experience.

• Experience leveraging ATS and CRM systems for executive recruiting.

• 401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions

jobs.title: Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer
jobs.description:
Renesas is seeking a Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer to join our team developing complex power management SoCs. These products integrate digital control, telemetry, fault management, communication interfaces, configurable peripherals, and advanced power-control functions for AI, datacenter, enterprise computing, networking, and high-performance power delivery applications.

You will independently own verification of significant blocks and features from planning through closure. The role combines hands-on UVM development, coverage-driven verification, complex debug, and close collaboration with architecture, RTL design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Responsibilities

• Own verification of complex digital blocks or major SoC features from requirements analysis through coverage closure.

• Develop feature-based verification plans from product, architecture, and microarchitecture specifications; identify gaps, ambiguities, corner cases, and risks.

• Build and extend reusable SystemVerilog/UVM environments, including sequences, monitors, scoreboards, checkers, assertions, and coverage models.

• Develop constrained random and targeted tests for normal operation, error handling, recovery, and system-level interactions.

• Drive functional, code, toggle, FSM, and assertion coverage closure using regression and coverage data.

• Debug RTL, testbench, assertion, integration, and regression failures; collaborate with design and firmware teams to isolate issues and verify fixes.

• Automate regression, triage, reporting, and analysis workflows using scripting and modern engineering tools.

• Communicate status, risks, dependencies, and closure evidence clearly; provide technical guidance to less-experienced engineers.

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

• 4 or more years of relevant digital design verification experience, or equivalent directly applicable experience.

• Demonstrated ownership of a complex block, subsystem, or major feature from verification planning through closure.

• Strong proficiency in SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained random verification, functional coverage, and SystemVerilog Assertions.

• Experience translating specifications into test plans, test scenarios, checkers, scoreboards, assertions, coverage models, and closure criteria.

• Hands-on experience developing and debugging reusable UVM environments and analyzing complex regression failures.

• Strong RTL and testbench debug skills, with the ability to distinguish design, environment, test, firmware, and specification issues.

• Working knowledge of digital design fundamentals, including state machines, clocks and resets, interrupts, register interfaces, memories, and clock-domain crossings.

• Proficiency in Linux and at least one scripting language such as Python, Bash, Perl, or Tcl.

• Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across architecture, design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience verifying complex SoCs, power management ICs, voltage regulators, digital controllers, or mixed-signal products.

• Experience verifying RTL interfaces to embedded processors, memory-mapped peripherals, and firmware-controlled hardware features.

• Familiarity with PMBus, AVSBus, SVID or SVI3, I2C, SPI, or similar control and communication protocols.

• Understanding of telemetry, fault and alert handling, power sequencing, multiphase regulation, or digital control loops.

• Experience with Cadence Xcelium, SimVision, vManager, JasperGold, Synopsys VCS, Verdi, or comparable tools.

• Experience with formal verification, gate-level simulation, silicon bring-up, or pre-silicon-to-silicon correlation.

• Experience improving regression infrastructure, coverage analytics, failure triage, or verification automation.

What You Bring

• Strong technical ownership and a disciplined approach to verification completeness.

• Ability to reason beyond directed requirements and identify meaningful corner cases and feature interactions.

• Clear communication of technical risk, progress, and signoff evidence.

• A collaborative mindset and interest in improving verification methodology and productivity.

jobs.title: Finance Director – Fabrication & Manufacturing
jobs.description:
About Loenbro

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.

At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps expand the reach of the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.

Job Summary

The Finance Director – Fabrication & Manufacturing is the senior financial business partner to the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing and is responsible for establishing the financial foundation, operating discipline, and decision-support structure required to operate Loenbro Fabrication & Manufacturing (F&M) as a centralized, stand-alone profit and loss business.

A primary initial responsibility will be to work across Manufacturing, Operations, Corporate Finance, Accounting, Project Controls, Estimating, Supply Chain, and other key stakeholders to carve out the current fabrication and manufacturing cost structure from the broader operating businesses. The Director will establish transparent and repeatable methods for revenue recognition, direct and indirect cost assignment, overhead allocation and absorption, intercompany/interdivision charging, facility economics, project and product profitability, forecasting, and management reporting.

This role extends beyond traditional finance and reporting. The Finance Director will be a strategic partner in executing Loenbro's manufacturing transformation and growth strategy, providing financial analysis for capacity expansion, capital deployment, productization, external-market growth, facility rationalization, strategic partnerships, acquisitions, and other investments. The position will create the KPI framework and financial visibility necessary to understand utilization, margin, cash generation, return on invested capital, and the true economics of Loenbro's manufacturing network.

As Loenbro develops additional centralized or new business lines within Operations, this position is expected to have the potential to expand beyond Fabrication & Manufacturing and provide financial leadership, governance, and business-building support for those emerging operations. The successful candidate will therefore combine strong FP&A and accounting fundamentals with operational finance, commercial judgment, manufacturing and project-costing knowledge, capital allocation discipline, and a builder mentality.

Essential Job Responsibilities

Stand-Alone P&L Development & Financial Structure

• Partner with the SVP of Manufacturing, Corporate Finance, Accounting, Operations, and other stakeholders to establish Fabrication & Manufacturing as a centralized, stand-alone P&L business.

• Lead the financial carve-out and baseline assessment of existing F&M operations, including revenue, direct labor, materials, equipment, facilities, supervision, shared services, and indirect costs.

• Establish consistent methodologies for cost allocation, intercompany/interdivision charges, transfer pricing, overhead recovery, shared-service allocations, and treatment of idle capacity and unabsorbed overhead.

• Develop cost-center, profit-center, project, facility, customer, and product-level structures that provide clear visibility into performance across the manufacturing network.

• Create appropriate financial separation and reporting for internal Loenbro work and external third-party revenue while preserving transparency into enterprise value creation.

• Partner with Accounting to ensure the F&M financial model complies with corporate policies, internal controls, revenue-recognition requirements, and period-close standards.

• Build a scalable financial structure capable of supporting future facilities, products, acquisitions, and new operating business lines.

Financial Planning, Analysis & Forecasting

• Own budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, and financial analysis for Fabrication & Manufacturing.

• Develop integrated financial models linking backlog, probability-weighted pipeline, shop loading, labor requirements, facility capacity, revenue, margin, overhead absorption, cash flow, and capital needs.

• Implement rolling forecasts and scenario models that allow leadership to anticipate underutilization, capacity constraints, margin risk, and investment requirements.

• Provide timely variance analysis and executive-level insights explaining performance versus budget, forecast, estimate, and strategic plan.

• Develop business cases for new products, customers, markets, facilities, technologies, and manufacturing initiatives.

• Support multi-year strategic planning and quantify the financial implications of Loenbro's transition from project-specific fabrication toward scalable manufacturing.

Cost Transparency & Operational Finance

• Establish a clear understanding of the true cost to operate each fabrication and manufacturing facility and major production capability.

• Develop standardized costing methodologies across mechanical/pipe fabrication, electrical prefab, modular assembly, and future manufactured product lines.

• Provide visibility into labor productivity, burden rates, material performance, equipment costs, freight and logistics, facility costs, rework, scrap, quality costs, and other major cost drivers.

• Partner with Operations and Project Controls to improve project-level cost forecasting, estimate-at-completion accuracy, change management, and margin protection.

• Create estimate-to-actual feedback loops that improve future estimating, pricing, production planning, and execution.

• Identify margin leakage, structural inefficiencies, underutilized assets, and opportunities to improve cost competitiveness across the network.

• Support make-versus-buy, internal-versus-external sourcing, hub-versus-spoke allocation, and capacity decisions using fact-based financial analysis.

KPI Development & Performance Management

• Develop and maintain an integrated F&M scorecard combining financial and operational KPIs that support accountability and timely decision-making.

• Establish measures for revenue, gross margin, EBITDA contribution, backlog, pipeline conversion, facility utilization, labor utilization, shop loading, direct versus indirect labor, productivity, overhead absorption, and unabsorbed overhead.

• Track revenue and margin per direct labor hour, estimate versus actual performance, project margin erosion, material variance, rework/cost of poor quality, working capital, cash conversion, and return on invested capital.

• Develop visibility into internal versus external revenue mix, customer and market concentration, product/program profitability, facility economics, and capital productivity.

• Lead recurring financial and business-performance reviews with F&M leadership and provide concise actions, trends, risks, and opportunities rather than historical reporting alone.

• Ensure KPI definitions and data sources are standardized across facilities so performance can be compared consistently across the enterprise network.

Capital Planning & Investment Analysis

• Lead financial analysis and business-case development for capital expenditures across the F&M network.

• Establish consistent CAPEX evaluation criteria including ROI, payback, NPV, capacity impact, labor savings, margin improvement, strategic value, and execution risk.

• Evaluate investments in facilities, automation, equipment, technology, tooling, material handling, testing capabilities, and manufacturing systems.

• Support facility expansion, consolidation, rationalization, greenfield development, and major capacity decisions.

• Develop post-investment reviews to measure actual performance against the approved business case and improve future capital-allocation decisions.

• Partner with leadership to prioritize capital across competing growth, productivity, maintenance, and strategic requirements.

Strategic Acquisitions, Partnerships & Growth

• Partner with the SVP of Manufacturing, Corporate Development, executive leadership, and ownership in evaluating acquisitions that support the F&M strategy.

• Assess historical financial performance, quality of earnings, backlog, customer concentration, margins, assets, working capital, CAPEX requirements, capacity, and growth potential of acquisition targets.

• Evaluate strategic fit, synergies, geographic expansion, customer access, workforce capability, manufacturing capacity, and integration requirements.

• Develop valuation models, investment cases, return scenarios, sensitivity analyses, and downside cases to support acquisition decisions.

• Support financial due diligence, transaction planning, integration, and post-close performance tracking against the original investment thesis.

• Evaluate strategic partnerships, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, alliances, and other inorganic growth opportunities from a financial and value-creation perspective.

Commercial, Pricing & Productization Support

• Partner with Business Development, Estimating, Operations, and Manufacturing leadership on pricing strategy and commercial decision-making.

• Develop financial frameworks for internal transfer pricing and external market pricing that preserve appropriate manufacturing margins and clearly communicate enterprise economics.

• Evaluate major bids, customer programs, framework agreements, long-term manufacturing commitments, and programmatic opportunities.

• Support productization by developing product-level cost models, target margins, pricing frameworks, investment cases, and volume/breakeven analyses.

• Provide financial analysis supporting growth in mission critical/data centers, power, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, water/wastewater, energy transition, and other strategic markets.

• Evaluate the economics of standardized mechanical, electrical, skid, modular, and integrated M&E solutions, including the value of field-labor displacement and total-installed-cost improvement.

• Help establish hurdle rates and financial criteria for new products, markets, facilities, customers, and strategic initiatives.

Systems, Data & Financial Governance

• Partner with Operations, IT, Project Controls, Supply Chain, and Corporate Finance to establish the systems and data architecture required to operate a scalable manufacturing business.

• Support development and integration of ERP/MRP, project controls, shop-loading, forecasting, inventory, procurement, and management-reporting capabilities.

• Establish common financial master data, coding structures, definitions, and reporting standards across facilities.

• Drive automation of dashboards, forecasting, management reporting, and recurring financial analysis wherever practical.

• Ensure leadership has timely, reliable, decision-oriented information and clear ownership of source data and financial controls.

Leadership & Business Partnership

• Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the SVP of Manufacturing and the F&M leadership team, translating financial results into clear operational and strategic actions.

• Participate actively in strategic planning, operating reviews, commercial decisions, investment reviews, acquisition assessments, and business-performance discussions.

• Constructively challenge assumptions and ensure major operating, pricing, growth, and investment decisions are supported by disciplined analysis.

• Build financial acumen and ownership throughout the F&M leadership organization so operational leaders understand the financial consequences of their decisions.

• Develop and lead finance, FP&A, project-controls, or analytical resources as the business scales.

• Maintain strong functional alignment with Corporate Finance while providing the speed, transparency, and business-partner orientation required by a growing stand-alone operation.

Future Operations Finance Scope

• Support the establishment of financial frameworks and stand-alone P&Ls for additional centralized or emerging Operations business lines as assigned.

• Apply the F&M financial operating model to new businesses, including cost structure, reporting, KPI governance, forecasting, capital planning, and performance management.

• Support incubation, commercialization, acquisition, and integration of new service lines and operating platforms.

• Help build a scalable Operations finance organization capable of supporting multiple growth businesses while maintaining appropriate corporate governance and controls.

Key Performance Indicators

• Accuracy and timeliness of stand-alone F&M P&L reporting and forecasting.

• Visibility and consistency of facility, project, customer, and product-level profitability.

• Gross margin, EBITDA contribution, cash generation, and working-capital performance.

• Forecast accuracy tied to backlog, pipeline, shop loading, and capacity.

• Facility and labor utilization; overhead absorption and unabsorbed overhead.

• Estimate-to-actual performance and reduction in margin leakage.

• Revenue and margin per direct labor hour and other productivity economics.

• Internal versus external revenue mix and profitable external-market growth.

• CAPEX performance versus approved ROI, payback, and strategic objectives.

• Acquisition and investment performance versus approved business case.

• Quality, consistency, and adoption of F&M financial dashboards and KPI reporting.

• Timeliness and quality of decision support provided to Manufacturing and executive leadership.

• Financial readiness and scalability of new products, facilities, acquisitions, and future Operations business lines.

Key Qualifications

Required

• 10+ years of progressive experience in finance, FP&A, operational finance, project controls, accounting, or related business-finance leadership roles.

• Demonstrated experience supporting manufacturing, fabrication, construction, industrial services, EPC, or another project-based operating environment.

• Experience establishing, managing, or materially supporting business-unit P&Ls and developing cost structures in complex operating environments.

• Strong understanding of job costing, manufacturing costing, overhead allocation and absorption, utilization, burden rates, margin analysis, and project financial controls.

• Demonstrated capability in budgeting, rolling forecasts, long-range planning, scenario analysis, and executive financial modeling.

• Experience developing CAPEX business cases and evaluating ROI, payback, NPV, and investment tradeoffs.

• Strong commercial and analytical judgment with the ability to connect operational decisions to margin, cash flow, capital efficiency, and enterprise value.

• Experience with ERP, project controls, business intelligence, and financial reporting systems; advanced spreadsheet and financial-modeling capability.

• Ability to operate effectively in an evolving environment where processes, systems, reporting structures, and organizational boundaries are being established and standardized.

• Strong executive communication, cross-functional leadership, and stakeholder-management skills.

• Ability and willingness to travel to Loenbro manufacturing and operating locations as required.

Preferred

• MBA, CPA, CMA, or other relevant advanced degree or professional credential.

• M&A, quality-of-earnings, due-diligence, valuation, acquisition integration, or corporate-development experience.

• Experience in private-equity-backed, high-growth, or transformation environments.

• Experience building finance capabilities for a new business unit, carve-out, centralized shared operation, or stand-alone P&L.

• Knowledge of fabrication, modular construction, electrical prefab, manufacturing operations, shop loading, inventory, supply chain, and capacity planning.

• Experience with product costing, standard costing, configure-to-order or engineer-to-order manufacturing, and product-line profitability.

• Experience developing executive dashboards and operational-finance KPI frameworks using business-intelligence tools.

• Experience supporting multi-site operations, facility rationalization, greenfield expansion, or manufacturing-network optimization.

Education

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline required.

Core Competencies: Strategic Finance | Operational Finance | FP&A | P&L Leadership | Manufacturing Costing | Project Controls | KPI Development | Financial Modeling | Capital Allocation | M&A Analysis | Commercial Finance | Pricing & Margin Management | Business Transformation | Data & Systems | Executive Decision Support | Cross-Functional Leadership

Leadership Expectations

The Finance Director is expected to operate as a business leader first and a financial steward second. This individual must understand how work is estimated, sold, engineered, procured, fabricated, manufactured, shipped, and installed, and must translate those operating realities into financial structures that drive accountability and better decisions.

The Director must be willing to build where structures do not yet exist. Success will require creating transparency without unnecessary bureaucracy, challenging legacy cost assumptions, establishing consistent financial disciplines across multiple facilities, and partnering closely with operational leaders to improve margin, utilization, cash generation, and return on capital.

This leader will play a central role in Loenbro's manufacturing transformation. Success means providing the SVP of Manufacturing and executive leadership with a reliable financial foundation for scaling F&M as a stand-alone business, allocating capital intelligently, evaluating acquisitions and growth opportunities, and ultimately applying the same discipline to additional new business lines within Operations.

Working Relationships

This role collaborates extensively with the Senior Vice President of Manufacturing, Chief Operating Officer, CFO and Corporate Finance, Accounting, Corporate Development, Fabrication & Manufacturing leadership, shop and operations leaders, Business Development, Estimating, Project Controls, Procurement/Supply Chain, Engineering & Productization, Quality, Safety, HR, IT, Legal/Contracts, Loenbro operating divisions, executive leadership, ownership, external advisors, acquisition targets, strategic partners, customers, and suppliers.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Work Environment:

• Combination of office/remote work and regular travel to manufacturing facilities and operating locations; travel of approximately 20–30%, based on business needs.

• Potential visits to fabrication facilities, industrial job sites, and manufacturing shop floors to gather cost, utilization, and operational data.

• Potential exposure to typical industrial and manufacturing environment factors while touring facilities.

• Regular engagement with executive leadership, ownership, and external advisors, which may require regional and national travel by air and ground transportation.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health

jobs.description:

Unlock Your Potential

• While this role will be focused on one client over the next few years, this role offers a unique opportunity to join a team delivering some of the most prestigious museum projects in the country.

• Excellent analytical, organizational, problem solving, presentation, interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills

What You’ll Be Doing

Why Work With Us?

jobs.title: Biologist Central Coast (on-call)
jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a highly motivated part time Authorized Special Status Species Field Biologist for immediate employment in Central California, including San Cruz, Monterey, Paso Robles, Morro Bay, San Luis Obispo, Pismo Beach and Maria Maria.  This is a field-based, fully remote, on-call position requiring the ability to be local on field assignments for extended periods.

The responsibilities of this position could include a subset of those listed below based on relevant experience:

• Biological compliance monitoring during active construction projects.

• Lead protocol and pre-construction surveys for special-status wildlife and nesting birds.

• Preparation of technical reports to document findings from surveys and monitoring.

• Preparation of other biological technical reports or permit application packages as needed.

• Manage and maintain strong relationships with AECOM, client, and construction personnel.

• Organization of project files, and tracking of project schedules.

• Promote safety culture and adherence to Safe Work Plans.

About AECOM’s Environment Business Line

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it.  We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.

AECOM is known for our award-winning technical excellence, leading-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide-ranging environmental problems.

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in related field (biology, ecology, etc.)
• 4+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education with biological surveys and monitoring in central California.
• A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy
• Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Strong knowledge of California wildlife, including special-status and protected species, with experience conducting surveys, monitoring, handling, relocation/translocation, and compliance support for species occurring throughout Central and Central Coast California.
• Specialized expertise and/or permits for targeted species such as Quino checkerspot butterfly, Stephens’ kangaroo rat, western spadefoot, and Crotch’s bumble bee, including protocol surveys, monitoring, trapping, handling, exclusion fencing, and translocation activities.
• Central Coast California plant identification skills and familiarity with aquatic resource delineations, California Coastal Commission permitting/ESHA analysis, and transportation projects (preferred).
• Working knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations and permitting requirements, including ESA, CESA, NEPA, CEQA, and the Clean Water Act.
• Excellent technical writing, verbal communication, organization, and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, maintain attention to detail, and adapt in a fast-paced environment.

• Sponsorship will not be provided now or in the future.
• THIS POSTING IS FOR A CURRENT VACANCY, AND AECOM INTENDS TO FILL THIS POSITION BY JANUARY 21, 2027.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.title: Senior Recruiter, Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a key member of Anduril's Talent Acquisition team, you will be responsible for the company's talent management as we continue to rapidly scale and grow. Your work will be hands-on and involve collaborating with Manufacturing leaders to define the hiring needs, influence process improvements and efficiencies, and set a high bar of talent and performance. To achieve this, you will be given the autonomy and tools to execute, build, and develop Anduril's world class team. We are looking for someone who can handle every aspect of recruiting and talent mapping, excited to be part of lean and nimble team on one mission together, where no task is too big or too small.

This role will be hybrid in Morrisville, NC. This is a 6 month contract with the ability to extend up to 18 months. Opportunity to be converted to a full-time employee based on performance, impact, and business need.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Act as a subject matter expert in prospecting techniques and tools used for information retrieval, data extraction, web-scraping, continuous process improvement, process automation, and candidate management

• Own and drive hiring strategy full-cycle, providing effective, clear communication and reporting

• Conduct a high volume of interviews, demonstrating ability to anticipate and influence hiring manager preferences through successful interview-to-offer conversion ratios

• Engage and source passive candidates using LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean strings, referrals and SOBO campaigns

• Build talent maps to generate market insights to inform your engagement strategy

• Drive diverse talent into the organization ensuring a positive candidate experience at every touchpoint

• Represent the company's brand and recruiting team internally and externally at the highest caliber

• Leverage internal resources, team mates, and cross functional partners to build strategy around selling our value proposition and impacting hiring practices

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• 6+ years of high-volume talent acquisition experience evaluating and hiring top tier talent

• 3+ years of experience working with senior level leaders and stakeholders, reporting on progress, creating and advising on talent strategies

• Experience recruiting at an agency and fast-paced startup, hiring exempt roles for Production, Manufacturing Engineering, and/or Manufacturing Operations.

• Ability to be onsite/hybrid at Morrisville, NC office

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Knowledge of ITAR policies around hiring practices

• Experience acting in a consultative manner where your guidance has led to improved outcomes and positive candidate experiences

• Clear and effective communication with candidates to understand motivation, drivers, and fit within the organization

• Experience managing various high-volume pipelines of candidates and keeping track of their progress throughout the recruitment process

• Highly autonomous, collaborative, and adaptable

US Hourly Range

$50—$70 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Account Director
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE

We are in search of senior sales and customer business development professionals with the drive to build strong, value-driven relationships with market leaders that support our growth objectives.

This role reports to the Director of Sales and calls for an experienced strategic enterprise seller — someone with a substantial track record in high-level, strategic sales roles at manufacturing companies who embraces the value of planning, process, and execution against company and customer goals. This person is naturally driven to develop value-based relationships with customer executives, to build and execute co-developed strategic growth plans, and to work cross-functionally with both internal teams and customer stakeholders to deliver against those plans.

Hadrian has strong access to stakeholders at Space and Defense primes, and a clear path to turn proof-of-concept manufacturing at the business-unit level into transformation programs at the corporate executive level. We start with executives who champion strategic supply-chain change, then work throughout the organization to define value, co-develop strategic growth plans, and execute.

Success in this role depends on fluency in how Aerospace and Defense suppliers are qualified and onboarded. The right candidate understands the requirements and cadence behind AS9100 certification, quality audits, and business assessments; the handling and compliance demands of ITAR; and the qualification gates that govern new work, including First Article Inspections (FAIs) and Production Part Approval Processes (PPAPs). They are comfortable navigating multi-year commitments and the contractual flowdowns that accompany defense programs, and they can speak credibly to these topics with both customers and internal teams.





WHAT HADRIAN OFFERS

 - Greenfield opportunity with customers that currently spend $100M–$3B annually at existing vendors we are disrupting

 - Ability to sell two “products” where we have fundamental speed and cost advantages over legacy competitors

jobs.title: Technology Warehouse Associate
jobs.description:
Build the Future with Us — EquipmentShare is Hiring a Technology Warehouse Associate

At EquipmentShare, we’re not just filling a role — we’re assembling the best team on the planet to build something that’s never been built before. We’re on a mission to transform an industry that’s been stuck in the past by empowering contractors and communities through innovative technology, real-time support, and a team that truly cares.

We’re hiring a Technology Warehouse Associate at our Telematics Warehouse in Overland Park, KS and we’re looking for someone who’s ready to grow with us, bring energy and drive to their work, and help us build the future of construction.

The Technology Warehouse Associate is responsible for supporting all aspects of warehouse operations related to technology hardware, including receiving, inventory management, device provisioning, kitting, quality inspection, order fulfillment, and shipping. This role ensures that all products and devices are accurately received, properly configured, carefully assembled, and shipped in a “field-ready” condition to meet customer and company standards.

Primary Responsibilities

Inventory & Receiving

• Receive and inspect inbound shipments for accuracy, damage, and completeness.

• Verify product quantities and serial numbers; scan and record devices in the inventory management system.

• Generate and apply product identification, tracking, and shipping labels.

• Direct incoming products to the appropriate location (quality inspection, provisioning, storage, etc.).

• Support purchase order entry, invoice tracking, and inventory reconciliation as needed.

• Maintain accurate inventory records and assist with cycle counts and audits.

Device Readiness & Configuration

• Power up, provision, assemble, and configure telematics and electronic devices according to current specifications.

• Perform firmware updates and configuration changes via OTA, USB, serial connection, or command-line tools.

• Conduct quality inspections on inbound devices and wiring harnesses.

• Troubleshoot and triage device issues during provisioning and readiness processes.

• Collaborate with quality, development, and support teams to ensure compliance with versioning and configuration requirements.

• Ensure all devices are “field ready” prior to shipment.

Kitting & Assembly

• Review and interpret work orders and pick lists to assemble kits and subassemblies.

• Accurately count, assemble, and package components according to customer specifications.

• Operate warehouse equipment including scan guns, label printers, shrink wrappers, and other packaging tools.

• Maintain a high standard of quality control during kit assembly and preparation.

Order Fulfillment & Shipping

• Perform final quality checks against pick lists to ensure 100% order accuracy.

• Pack orders to prevent damage and optimize shipping efficiency.

• Generate packing slips and apply appropriate carrier, regulatory, and lithium battery labels.

• Prepare small package and LTL shipments for carrier pickup.

• Support domestic and international shipping processes, including customs documentation when required.

• Load outbound packages and freight safely and efficiently.

Safety & Continuous Improvement

• Follow all safety standards and warehouse best practices.

• Maintain a clean and organized work environment.

• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives to increase quality, efficiency, and accuracy.

• Perform other duties as assigned to support warehouse and operations functions.

Why EquipmentShare?

Because we do things differently — and we think you’ll feel it from day one. We’re a people-first company powered by cutting-edge technology. That means our proprietary T3 platform doesn’t just run our business — it also makes your job easier, safer, and more connected. Whether you’re behind the wheel, under the hood, leading a branch, or closing deals — tech supports you, and you drive us forward.

We’re a team of problem-solvers, go-getters, and builders. And we’re looking for teammates who take pride in doing meaningful work and want to be part of building something special.

Perks & Benefits

• Competitive compensation

• Full medical, dental, and vision coverage for full-time employees

• Generous PTO + paid holidays

• 401(k) + company match

• Gym membership stipend + wellness programs (earn PTO and prizes!)

• Company events, food truck nights

• 16 hours of paid volunteer time per year — give back to the community you call home

• Career advancement, leadership training, and professional development opportunities

About You

You want to be part of a team that’s not just changing an industry for the sake of change — we’re transforming it to make it safer, more secure, and more productive. You bring grit, heart, and humility to your work, and you’re excited about the opportunity to grow within a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.

We’re looking for people who:

• See challenges as opportunities

• Embrace change and continuous improvement

• Bring energy, effort, and optimism every day

Skills & Qualifications

• Familiarity with telematics or consumer electronics devices preferred.

• Ability to read and interpret work orders, schematics, wiring diagrams, and shipping documentation.

• Experience using tools such as wire cutters, crimpers, volt meters, and related equipment preferred.

• Proficiency with PCs and standard software applications; familiarity with command-line tools is a plus.

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

• Excellent organizational and communication skills.

• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

Education and Experience

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• At least 1 year of experience in a warehouse, manufacturing, or technology fulfillment environment required.

• Experience with inventory management systems required.

• Previous experience in shipping, receiving, kitting, or device provisioning preferred.

• Experience with UPS WorldShip, LTL freight, small package shipping, and Customs processes is a plus.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to lift up to 70 pounds on occasion.

• Ability to stand and/or walk for 8–10 hours per shift (with breaks).

• Ability to frequently push, pull, squat, bend, reach, and use ladders and material handling equipment.

• Ability to safely handle electronic equipment, including devices containing batteries.

A Workplace For All

At EquipmentShare, we believe the best solutions come from a team that reflects the world around us. Our initiative — A Workplace For All — is rooted in the belief that we must work together to solve some of the toughest problems in construction. That means attracting, developing, and retaining great people from all walks of life.

We value different backgrounds, talents, and perspectives. We want you to feel like you belong here — because you do.

EquipmentShare is an EOE M/F/D/V.

Employment is contingent on passing a background check. Additionally, some roles require passing a drug test, depending on the job responsibilities.

jobs.title: Lifecycle Marketing Technologist
jobs.description:
Why Housecall Pro?

Help us build solutions that build better lives. At Housecall Pro, we show up to work every day to make a difference for real people: the home service professionals that support America’s 100 million homes. We’re all about the Pro, and dedicate our days to helping them streamline operations, scale their businesses, and—ultimately—save time so they can be with their families and live well.

While our headquarters are based in Denver, Colorado, our team spans the globe, with teammates across Brazil, Poland, the Philippines, Mexico, and beyond. We care deeply about our customers and foster a culture where our company, people and Pros grow and succeed together—no matter where they’re based. Leadership is as focused on growing team members’ careers as they expect their teams to be on creating solutions for Pros.

We also offer:

• A generous benefits program that supports the whole you with medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and 401(k)

• Paid holidays and flexible, take-it-as-you-need-it paid time off

• Equity in a rapidly growing startup backed by top-tier VCs

• Monthly tech reimbursements

• A culture built on innovation that values big ideas, no matter where they come from

Role Overview

As the Lead, Lifecycle Marketing, you manage the full spectrum of lifecycle campaigns, including email, SMS, and in-app messaging, focusing on enhancing customer engagement and driving conversions. You oversee campaign strategy, execution, and analysis across multiple channels, collaborating closely with content, design, and analytics teams to ensure seamless integration with overall marketing strategies. Your role requires analyzing performance metrics, optimizing campaigns, and continuously evolving strategies to meet business goals. You ensure campaigns are personalized, timely, and compliant with relevant regulations, providing a cohesive experience across all customer touchpoints.

Our team is passionate, empathetic, hard-working, and above all else focused on improving the lives of our service professionals (our Pros). Our success is their success.

What you do each day:

• Build dynamic, personalized content with Liquid and Mustache logic, including conditionals, loops, fallbacks, and data-driven content blocks

• Collaborate with content and design teams to create engaging and relevant campaigns tailored to customer segments

Qualifications:

• Strong JavaScript skills for landing pages, forms, custom tracking, and data manipulation

• Proven experience writing Liquid and/or Mustache templates for advanced personalization and conditional content

What will help you succeed:

• Attention to detail and creative problem-solving abilities

• A proactive mindset focused on continuous improvement

• Enthusiasm for learning and staying current with industry trends

• Strong ability to Multi-task to ensure communication and deployments happen on-time

Location Dependent Information

This role is open to candidates and the expected salary range for this role is $83,600-$104,000 + equity. The specific salary for the successful candidate will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location. This role is also eligible to participate in Housecall Pro’s equity plan and the following benefits: health care insurance (medical, dental, vision, disability), employee assistance program, 401(K), flexible time off, paid parental leave, tech reimbursement, and other company benefits. Housecall Pro is growing fast and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth.

Founded in 2013, Housecall Pro helps home service professionals (Pros) streamline every aspect of their business. With easy-to-use tools for scheduling, dispatching, payments, and more, Housecall Pro enables Pros to save time, grow profitably, and provide best-in-class service.

Housecall Pro’s brand portfolio includes Business Coaching by Housecall Pro, a business coaching solution for home services businesses. Our brands are united by a singular mission to champion our Pros to success.

We support more than 50,000 businesses and have over 2,000 ambitious, mission-driven, genuinely fun-loving teammates across the globe. If you want to do work that impacts real people, supported by a team that will invest in you every step of the way, we’d love to hear from you.

Housecall Pro celebrates diversity and we are committed to creating an inclusive environment. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of gender, race, religion, national origin, ethnicity, disability, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other category protected under the law.   #LI-Remote

All final hiring and engagement decisions are made by human representatives, not AI tools.

jobs.title: People Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
Collections today works like an emergency room. The doctors carry too many patients, everyone arrives at their worst moment, and nobody has their chart. We're making it primary care. January personalizes interactions and optimizes decisions across every stage of consumer credit. We started in the hardest, most broken stage, because if it works there it works anywhere.



Most consumers want to pay what they owe. They want a way out, not a break. We've serviced over $20 billion in debt across more than 20 million consumers. We see more people with charged-off loans each year than all but the top five US banks. Those consumers rate us about 50% higher than the banks that lent them the money. Creditors net over 30% more because we collect more and charge less.



Most AI strips the human out of the work. We use it to make someone's hardest financial moment more human. The more human we make it, the more people recover. Now we're moving upstream, catching people before they default and building across every stage of the consumer credit lifecycle. The consumer in collections today is the consumer who gets approved tomorrow.

As our People Strategy & Operations Lead, you’ll build the systems, programs, and infrastructure that enable January to scale without compromising the employee experience. You’ll own the operating foundation of our people function, from core HR operations to the programs and analytics that help us continuously improve how we work. Your mission is to make the employee experience seamless, thoughtful, and scalable so our people can focus on doing their best work as the company grows.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll own the employee lifecycle end to end, from the moment someone accepts an offer through the day, if it comes, that they leave. You'll support the semi-annual performance cycle and the annual comp cycle, manage leaves and accommodations, and be the continuous link between outside counsel and any employee working through a visa case — work that exists because we go after exceptional talent regardless of where it comes from.



This role covers three broad areas:

 - Designing and executing the key moments in the employee lifecycle, from onboarding to exit, treating each one as a repeatable program with clear owners, timelines, and success metrics designing new hire onboarding start to finish with Recruiting and hiring managers, operating the performance and comp cycles as cross-functional programs with defined milestones and stakeholder alignment, executing offboarding and advising managers through involuntary terminations, and creating the systems that answer the team's pay, benefits, and policy questions.

 - Owning HR’s operational core and building the infrastructure to scale: running HR operations with the rigor of a program owner, including compliance, benefits and Open Enrollment, immigration and visa casework, leave and accommodations, biweekly payroll, HR technology and vendor relationships, and investing in automation and self-service systems that reduce manual work and scale with the company.

 - Owning people data and analytics to continuously improve the employee experience: building trusted reporting and actionable insights across HRIS, payroll, and employee data; defining success metrics for key people programs; and using trends and outcomes to identify opportunities, inform decisions, and continuously improve how employees experience the company.

This is a role for someone who treats process as the product — who builds the documentation and systems that let this function scale with headcount instead of straining under it, and who gets the technical details exactly right, every time. You are a force multiplier: you identify the highest-leverage problems across the company’s people systems, scope them, sequence them, and drive them to measurable outcomes.




WHAT WE NEED

 - You read a messy, high-stakes situation and reach the right call without a clean rule to point to — and you update your read when new facts come in instead of defending your first conclusion

 - You think in systems and tradeoffs: given an ambiguous, cross-functional problem, you scope it, prioritize it against everything else competing for attention, and drive it to a shipped outcome

 - You shift registers fluidly: the warm first contact on someone's first day, the steady presence in a hard conversation, the plain-English translator between an anxious employee and a lawyer's fine print — sometimes in the same afternoon

 - You know the difference between a call that's yours to make and one that needs to go up or across — and you escalate deliberately, through the right channel, not reflexively

 - You get the technical details exactly right on work with real legal exposure — a visa classification, a leave calculation, a filing deadline — because you know a small error here doesn't stay small

 - You pick up work nobody owns and carry it to a real outcome, not a status update, and you leave behind a process your successor can run without you

 - You build collaborative working relationships with Legal, IT, Finance, and outside counsel, and know exactly where HR's call ends and someone else's begins

 - You’re data-fluent: you define the metrics, build the dashboards, and turn HRIS and payroll data into recommendations leadership can act on

 - You surface a gap before anyone asks — a missed filing, a stalled case, a ticket sitting with the wrong owner

 - You hear what someone actually needs underneath what they're asking for, and you fix the system, not just the one instance in front of you

 - 3+ years of experience in HR/People Operations

 - Nice-to-have: experience with Rippling, Sequoia
   
   


HOW WE WORK

 - Decentralization beats control. The best calls get made by the people closest to them, not routed up a chain. You'll set the standards that let the team decide without you in the room.

 - Speed beats perfection. You run tight loops, act at 70% on reversible calls and adjust as you learn. Fast loops beat slow ones.

 - Candor beats comfort. You'd rather hear a hard truth early than a polite sidestep that wastes everyone's time.

 - Writing beats the average meeting. Clarity scales.

 - AI runs through everything here. We built our own code reviewer that beats the alternatives. Our voice AI handles most inbound calls with zero hallucinated payments. Engineers ship 3-4x the PRs they used to. You'll push it further into the work than almost any company you've worked at.

 - We operate at every altitude. No one here lives only on Mount Olympus, not even the leaders. We get into the trenches to learn the ground truth, then refine our information flows so ground truth climbs as fast as direction comes down.

 - We build in person, at least three days a week in our office in Nolita, with a growing group coming in every day. Random run-ins cross-pollinate ideas. Face time builds trust no thread can. Building alongside people makes work far more fun.




As a New York City-based company, we are dedicated to transparent, fair, and equitable compensation practices that reflect our commitment to fostering an environment where all team members are valued and supported. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply.




We are an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion in the workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, age, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

This position is open to candidates in the Seattle, WA area. You will have a hybrid remote/in-office schedule where you will work from our casual, pet-friendly office at least 3 days a week.

Responsibilities:

Primary Support Function

Partner with the business to effectively and accurately implement large-scale organizational transformations.
