Please visit careers.quora.com/eligible-countries http://careers.quora.com/eligible-countries for details regarding employment eligibility by country.]




ABOUT QUORA:

Quora’s mission is to grow the world's collective intelligence. To do so, we have two platforms:

 - Quora http://quora.com: a global knowledge sharing platform with millions of monthly unique visitors, bringing people together to share insights on various topics and providing a unique platform to learn and connect with others.

 - Poe https://poe.com/: a cloud workspace where millions of users run multiple AI agents on shared context and tools. One subscription, every frontier model, and the collaboration layer that makes them work together.

Behind these products are passionate, collaborative, and high-performing global teams. We have a culture rooted in transparency, idea-sharing, and experimentation that allows us to celebrate success and grow together through meaningful work. Join us on this journey to create a positive impact and make a significant change in the world.

This role will be working on our Quora product.




ABOUT THE TEAM AND ROLE:

At Quora, machine learning drives nearly every aspect of our product, and our lean, high-velocity engineering team tackles complex, high-impact challenges daily. We thrive in a remote-first culture built on absolute autonomy, continuous learning, and bold experimentation.

We are looking for a Staff Machine Learning Engineer to define the technical future of Quora’s recommendation ecosystem. In this role, you will own the technical direction for feed ranking and retrieval, lead our highest-impact modeling bets, and pioneer the integration of LLMs and generative models to redefine how we understand and rank content. Beyond the home feed, you will also scale recommendation surfaces like notifications and digest emails, while architecting the underlying tools and abstractions that empower our entire engineering organization.

This is a high-leverage, hands-on IC role with organization-wide scope. You will write production code, mentor rising talent, and actively shape how our team leverages AI-assisted development to accelerate our shipping velocity.




RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Set the technical direction for Quora’s home feed recommendation systems

 - Lead the highest-impact projects across the recommender stack, from candidate generation and retrieval to ranking, re-ranking, and multi-objective optimization

 - Drive measurable improvements in user engagement and content quality through well-designed online experiments

 - Take end-to-end ownership of ML systems, including data pipelines, candidate extraction, feature engineering, model training, and production integration

 - Identify new opportunities to apply machine learning to different parts of the Quora product

 - Partner with product, data science, and infrastructure teams to align on priorities and tradeoffs

 - Mentor engineers and lead by example, raising the bar for code quality, modeling rigor and AI assisted dev velocity




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

 - Availability for meetings and impromptu communication during Quora's “coordination hours https://quora.com/coordination_hours" (Mon-Fri: 9am-3pm Pacific Time)

 - 6+ years of professional software development experience in machine learning

 - 4+ years of professional experience building and optimizing Home Feed recommendation systems for social media and user-generated content platforms.

 - Deep knowledge of the full recommender stack: candidate generation, retrieval, ranking, re-ranking, embeddings, and multi-objective optimization.

 - Deep understanding of mathematical foundations of machine learning algorithms

 - Experience leading large-scale ML projects end-to-end with measurable outcome

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills

 - BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science




PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS:

 - 6+ years of experience writing Python or C++ code

 - Hands-on experience deploying and running generative models at scale

 - Background in notifications, email/digest recommendations, or growth and lifecycle modeling

 - Flexible and positive team player

 - Publications at venues like RecSys, KDD, NeurIPS, or ICML.

 - Passion for Quora's mission and goals

We encourage all candidates who share a passion for growing the world’s knowledge, even those who may not strictly meet all the preferred requirements, to apply, as we know that a diverse range of perspectives can have a significant impact on our products and our culture.

About Lucid

At Lucid, we are creating exceptional mobility experiences through innovation to drive the world forward. Built on Lucid’s proprietary technology and software-defined vehicle architecture, our award-winning vehicles bring our “Compromise Nothing™” approach to the global automotive market. That means refusing to choose between performance and sustainability, design and engineering, ambition and integrity. In Lucid Air and Lucid Gravity, we have designed and built vehicles that have redefined their segments, combining exceptional range, performance, design, and expansive space in a single experience.

We achieve this through deep vertical integration, with design, engineering, and production happening in-house across our global offices and manufacturing facilities. Our teams come from industries around the world, united by a shared commitment to excellence. By refusing to settle, you can help redefine what’s possible and shape the future of mobility.

As a Studio Manager within a Lucid studio, your primary responsibility will be to directly manage, coach, develop and support a team with the successful articulation and delivery of the Lucid brand and ownership experience.  This role will report directly to the Market Leader to lead the studio team and processes that enable the studio to achieve their targets.

They will be naturally organized with strong leadership skills and a focus on efficient and effective operations management.

Studio Managers must be agile and driven with an inclination for coordinating and developing all team members to consistently deliver exceptional customer experiences through education and enjoyable interactions. This role will be pivotal in providing organization, support and counsel to all members of the Studio team to ensure a seamless experience for all guests and members of the Lucid community.

BUSINESS HEALTH

• Coach and motivate the team to meet test drives, delivery, and productivity goals

• Demonstrate leadership by role-playing and having an active presence in customer-facing locations

• Train and develop team on Lucid products and delivery processes

• Analyze data to determine optimal business strategies

• Set individual goals for your team, ensuring processes and routines are conducive to building pipeline and creating owners in order to reach studio goals

• Ensure the team is fluent in all aspects of Lucid product knowledge and relevant automotive industry offerings, and competitive landscape

• Drive for excellence in all areas of business focused on reaching expectations for the respective location

CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

• Leads, values, and inspires their team to prioritize customer service and deliver the Lucid experience to all customers.

• Responsible for ensuring all employees provide best-in-class experience in every interaction on the studio floor, in test drives, and through actively following up on leads

• Also acts as a Senior Studio Associate, handling high-potential customers

• Clientele management for VIP customers

• Your hands-on leadership will assist in coaching and training your team to deliver an exceptional experience that touches both the heart and mind of the customer.

EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT

• Provide targeted coaching, skill development for Studio Associates to excel in performance metrics with weekly one-on one meetings

• Recruitment, training and development of a high performing and customer focused team, ensuring all positions are filled in a timely manner

• Provide leadership, direction and coach all members of the team to ensure a seamless experience for customers and all members of the Lucid community.

• Develop inclusive, diverse, and high performing teams through defining efficient processes and developing the team through teaching moments.

• Sets goals, timelines, and target lists for Studio Associates and tracks results to ensure timely execution on lead generation and/or market Initiatives.

• Demonstrates a confidence in operations and planning all aspects of the business including developing monthly attainment plans and communication of results to team.

• Manages leads, appointments, reservations and motivates a team to deliver results by communicating company initiatives and engaging team through effective coaching, performance management and training.

STUDIO OPERATIONS

• Own the operations within the studio to ensure the customer journey is frictionless and seamless from reservation through to delivery.

• Supervise merchandising product inventory and display

• Manage and coordinate studio team scheduling.

• Partner with Retail Operations and coordinate with vendors and service providers as needed

• Ensure facility maintenance and showroom presentation adhere to the brand standards

• Thrives in a fast-paced environment where innovation is inevitable, and change is expected.

• Assist with daily operations as needed

Qualifications

• 4-8 years of related professional experience.

• A Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in business, marketing or related discipline.

• Curiosity and passion about electric vehicles and the premium vehicle market and competitive landscape

• Excellent communication, leadership and organizational skills.

• Penchant for nurturing and leading exceptional customer-oriented teams.

• Willingness to be hands-on with all Studio operations.

jobs.title: Staff Technical Change Manager
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

JOB PURPOSE:

The Technical Program Governance team enables complex technical initiatives across PlayStation engineering organizations by creating clarity, alignment, and disciplined execution across organizational boundaries.

As a Staff Technical Change Manager, you will lead the people, adoption, and organizational dimensions of complex technical change across engineering and technology organizations. You will work alongside technical leaders, architects, program managers, and delivery teams to understand what is changing, who is affected, what will be required of them, and how to move from awareness to sustained adoption.

This is a technical change role. Success requires more than familiarity with software-development terminology or experience working near engineering teams. You must be able to understand systems, platforms, architecture, integrations, engineering delivery models, and technical dependencies well enough to identify meaningful change impacts, ask informed questions, and translate technical decisions into practical organizational action.

This role offers the opportunity to build and shape change capability from the ground up. You’ll help define how change is led, scaled, and embedded across a growing technical organization, creating practical approaches that can evolve with the business rather than inheriting a fixed playbook.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

Essential

• Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional organizational change within technology, engineering, digital, or technical environments.

• Strong technical fluency across modern software and technology environments. Able to understand systems, platforms, architecture, integrations, engineering workflows, and technical dependencies well enough to assess organizational impact and engage credibly with technical leaders.\

• Proven ability to translate complex technical concepts and decisions into clear stakeholder impacts, adoption needs, communications, enablement plans, and practical actions.

• Deep practical knowledge of organizational change methods and tools, combined with the judgment to adapt, combine, simplify, or move beyond a methodology when the situation requires it.

• Experience developing end-to-end change strategies, including stakeholder analysis, impact assessment, readiness, communications, engagement, learning or enablement, adoption measurement, and reinforcement.

• Strong independent judgment and problem-solving skills, with a record of operating effectively in ambiguous environments where the change strategy, operating model, or path forward is still being created.

• Ability to influence senior technical and business leaders, facilitate difficult conversations, build alignment across competing priorities, and move decisions forward without direct authority.

• Experience using qualitative and quantitative signals to assess adoption, identify resistance or friction, test assumptions, and adjust strategy based on evidence rather than process compliance.

• Demonstrated ability to create reusable frameworks, playbooks, tools, and guidance and to coach others so change capability scales beyond the individual.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to produce concise executive narratives while retaining enough technical substance for engineering audiences.

Desirable

• Consulting or transformation advisory experience, particularly in environments requiring rapid context building, executive influence, and practical recommendations across multiple clients, organizations, or business units.

• Experience building or materially evolving a change capability in an organization where practices, roles, standards, and expectations were not already mature or consistently established.\

• Experience supporting platform, infrastructure, cloud, architecture, developer tooling, enterprise systems, or other technically complex transformation work.

• Experience working directly with engineers, architects, technical program managers, product leaders, and senior technology executives.

• Background in the games, interactive entertainment, or large-scale technology industry.

• Formal change-management certification.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE FOR DECISION MAKING:

Technical Change Strategy and Delivery

• Lead change strategy and execution for complex technical initiatives spanning multiple teams, organizations, technologies, or geographies.

• Build a clear understanding of the technical change itself, including affected systems, dependencies, operating models, workflows, roles, and decision points, before determining the appropriate change approach.

• Translate technical implementation plans into stakeholder impacts, readiness needs, adoption risks, engagement strategies, and measurable change outcomes.

• Embed organizational readiness into the design and delivery of major initiatives, helping ensure change is considered from the beginning and translated into sustained adoption, stronger execution, and measurable business impact.

• Identify adoption barriers early, frame the underlying problem, and drive practical interventions that address behavior, capability, process, structure, or incentives as appropriate.

• Define meaningful measures of readiness, adoption, and sustained use, and adjust strategy when evidence shows the current approach is not working.

Technical Partnership and Organizational Judgment

• Partner closely with engineers, architects, technical program managers, product leaders, and subject-matter experts to understand technical decisions and their organizational consequences.

• Ask informed technical questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and surface dependencies or downstream impacts that may otherwise be missed in change planning.

• Operate as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, bringing clear recommendations, rationale, risks, tradeoffs, and expected outcomes rather than relying on escalation or waiting for direction.

• Demonstrate strong judgment about where and how change leadership can add value. Read the room, adapt to the audience and organizational context, and apply the right level of structure to accelerate outcomes without introducing unnecessary process.

• Use organizational context, stakeholder insight, and data to determine where leadership attention is required and where teams can move independently.

• Connect technical transformation to business and organizational outcomes so leaders understand not only what is changing, but why it matters and what successful adoption looks like.

Capability Building and Scale

• Help build a practical, scalable technical change-management capability, including reusable frameworks, playbooks, templates, decision guides, and operating practices.

• Create lightweight approaches that can be used by program and technical leaders directly, reserving specialist change support for the work where it creates the most value.

• Coach leaders, TPMs, and cross-functional partners on stakeholder engagement, readiness, adoption planning, resistance, and reinforcement so change knowledge spreads through the organization.

• Use strong facilitation and organizational judgment to bring the right people together, navigate competing perspectives, and turn complex conversations into clear decisions, alignment, and action.

• Capture lessons learned and patterns across initiatives and use them to improve future change strategies, tools, and organizational practices.

• Leave teams more capable than you found them by building knowledge, confidence, and repeatable practices that continue beyond an individual initiative.

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

·       Sustained adoption and organizational readiness for complex technical changes, demonstrated through measurable use, behavior change, or operating outcomes.

·       Quality and timeliness of change-impact identification, stakeholder strategy, risk management, and interventions across multiple initiatives.

·       Demonstrated technical credibility and effectiveness partnering with engineering, architecture, program, and senior leadership audiences.

·       Evidence that change approaches are adapted based on context, feedback, and data rather than applied mechanically.

·       Measurable growth in organizational change capability through reusable tools, coaching, knowledge sharing, and increased self-sufficiency of partner teams.

·       Senior stakeholder confidence in the clarity, practicality, and strategic value of change recommendations and execution.

The individual will be measured on:

• Successful adoption and sustained impact of complex technical and organizational changes, with clear evidence that intended outcomes are understood, adopted, and embedded.

• Ability to identify where change leadership will have the greatest impact, applying sound judgment and the appropriate level of structure based on the audience, environment, risk, and desired outcome.

• Quality of strategic partnership with technical and business leaders, including the ability to build trust, navigate organizational dynamics, challenge constructively, and influence decisions.

• Effectiveness in translating complex technical change into meaningful organizational action, connecting technical direction with what teams need to understand, do differently, and sustain.

• Measurable improvements in organizational readiness and adoption, using meaningful indicators and feedback to identify barriers, adjust strategy, and improve outcomes.

• Growth of scalable change capability across the organization, including practices, approaches, and knowledge that enable leaders and teams to manage change more effectively without continued direct support.

• Ability to strengthen and evolve the organization’s approach to change, identifying opportunities to improve how change is led and building practical capabilities that can scale as the organization matures.

• Effectiveness operating independently in complex and ambiguous environments, bringing recommendations, exercising strong judgment, and driving work forward without requiring a predefined playbook.

jobs.title: Practicing Clinicians: Paid Interview on Outpatient Care Workflows
jobs.description:
WHAT WE'RE RESEARCHING

We are running a paid study on clinical workflows within outpatient and community-based healthcare settings. Our goal is to map the realities of patient care delivery outside of traditional hospital environments. This research directly informs how modern clinical tools can better support day-to-day medical practice.


HOW IT WORKS

You will participate in a remote voice and video interview moderated by our AI platform. During the session, you will describe your typical patient care routines and outline the steps you take to manage outpatient workflows. We will ask you to react to hypothetical clinical scenarios and share the operational hurdles you face most often. Your feedback will be collected through guided conversational prompts to capture a realistic picture of your practice.


WHO THIS IS FOR

We are looking for practicing clinicians who currently work in outpatient or community-based medical settings. We welcome primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and specialist clinicians managing community clinics. You should have direct experience coordinating patient care workflows outside of a large inpatient hospital system.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Describe your daily clinical workflow in an outpatient setting

 - Walk us through how you manage routine patient care delivery

 - Identify operational challenges or bottlenecks in your current practice

 - Respond to AI-guided questions about community-based care scenarios


WHO SHOULD APPLY

 - Currently practicing as a clinician in an outpatient or community clinic

 - Direct experience managing patient care delivery workflows

 - Comfortable discussing the operational realities of your medical practice

 - Ability to join a remote video call from a quiet environment

jobs.title: Vice President of Strategy
jobs.location: Remote; Washington, D.C. or Los Angeles preferred
jobs.description:
Thank you for considering Oklo. We are hiring a Vice President of Strategy to build and lead our corporate Strategy function.

Position Description

Oklo is seeking a Vice President of Strategy to serve as the senior leader of the company’s corporate strategy function. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, you will shape Oklo’s enterprise strategy, lead the Strategy team, and help the company make and execute its most consequential decisions.

The function is designed to be proactive and high leverage: identifying emerging opportunities and risks, developing independent points of view, and deploying a focused team against the company’s highest-priority questions and initiatives. You will set the function’s agenda and standards, determine where Strategy resources can have the greatest impact, and lead work from early thesis development through executive decision, execution, and handoff.

You will work directly with the founders, CFO, and business-unit leaders, bringing forward original recommendations, constructively challenging assumptions, and leading the Strategy function’s contribution to executive and Board decisions. You will be accountable for the quality of company-level strategy, the effectiveness of the Strategy function, and the impact of the initiatives it leads.

Specific responsibilities include:

• Build and lead the corporate strategy function. Design the function's operating model; hire, develop, and manage talent; allocate resources; and own the standards, quality, and results of the team.

• Own enterprise strategy. Lead the development and refinement of Oklo's long-range strategy, including portfolio choices, priority markets, business models, growth platforms, and the allocation of leadership attention and company resources.

• Set a proactive strategic agenda. Identify important opportunities, risks, and unanswered questions before they are formally assigned. Sponsor the right analysis and recommend what the company should pursue, defer, reshape, or decline.

• Lead strategic planning and performance reviews. Own the Strategy team's delivery of annual and multi-year planning, objectives and key results, scorecards, and initiative reviews.

• Shape major corporate choices. Support the strategic evaluation of partnerships, creative capital initiatives, acquisitions, new ventures, international opportunities, and structural options in collaboration with the relevant business units and functional owners.

• Own the strategic-initiative portfolio. Establish objectives, accountable leaders, milestones, decision points, and review mechanisms. Recommend when to advance, resource, redirect, stop, or hand off work.

• Advise executive leadership and the Board. Bring independent, evidence-based recommendations; challenge assumptions constructively; frame alternatives and tradeoffs; and lead consequential strategic discussions.

• Personally lead selected high-stakes initiatives. Take direct responsibility for a small number of the company's most important initiatives through decision, launch, transaction, or a clear operational handoff.

• Integrate strategy across the company. Partner with Finance, Corporate Development, Strategic Partnerships, Legal, Government Affairs, international teams, technical and regulatory leaders, and business units so company-level choices remain coherent through execution.

• Build company-wide strategy capability. Establish rigorous methods for business cases, decision memos, portfolio reviews, and strategic planning, and coach colleagues to improve the quality and speed of decision-making.

Minimum Qualifications

• Senior leadership experience. Substantial experience leading corporate strategy, general management, business building, or a comparable enterprise mandate, with a record of shaping company direction and driving implementation.

• Functional and people leadership. Demonstrated success building high-performing teams, setting an agenda, developing talent, managing performance, and delivering results through others.

• Executive and Board judgment. Experience advising founders, senior executives, or Boards on consequential choices and creating alignment around difficult decisions.

• Commercial and financial depth. Strong judgment across business models, partnerships, capital requirements, growth opportunities, portfolio choices, and resource tradeoffs.

• Cross-functional execution. A record of leading complex initiatives across functions and business units without relying solely on direct reporting authority.

• Exceptional communication. Excellent writing, synthesis, and executive communication, with the credibility to challenge assumptions and represent the company with senior counterparties.

Bonus Qualifications

• Experience building a Strategy function or leading strategy across multiple businesses in a growing, capital-intensive, or regulated company.

• Experience with industrial or technology partnerships, capital formation, international initiatives, acquisitions, or new ventures.

• Experience leading executive and Board strategy work and establishing effective company planning and accountability processes.

Competencies

• Takes ownership of the function's agenda, people, standards, and results.

• Brings independent judgment and imagination, grounded in evidence and commercial discipline.

• Develops strong teams, builds alignment, and makes difficult tradeoffs explicit.

• Welcomes constructive disagreement and combines senior leadership with hands-on work.

Who you are

You want to own a meaningful part of a company's direction and build the team that makes it actionable. You bring an agenda, not just an answer to someone else's question. You can challenge an executive, align business leaders, develop talented colleagues, and take responsibility for what happens next.

About Oklo travel requirements

Significant travel for executive working sessions, team collaboration, and selected engagements may be required. Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters in Santa Clara, California, twice per quarter based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara.

About Oklo compensation:

Salary: $250,000-$280,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, bonuses, competitive pay, 401(k), health insurance (with employer contribution), HSA, FSA, flexible work hours, wellness credits, and other benefits.

This position may involve access to information subject to U.S. export control laws. Only applicants who meet the definition of a U.S. person under applicable laws may be eligible.

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

FULL-TIME JOB VACANCY
Director, FP&A and Grant Management
Operations Department
Multiple Locations Considered
Application Deadline: November 12, 2026

The Director of Financial Planning & Analysis and Grant Management (“FP&A”) reports into the Chief Financial Officer and serves as a strategic partner to the CFO and senior leadership team. The Director leads HRW’s strategic financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, financial analysis, and grant financial management functions, ensuring leadership has the information, financial insights and tools needed to support sound decision-making, organizational sustainability, and effective stewardship of donor resources.

The Director oversees annual organizational budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, grant budgeting and financial reporting, revenue projections, and a team of seven FP&A and grants management professionals. This role will preferably be based in New York or Washington DC, and will be expected to work from the office two days per week. Candidate in other cities with HRW offices that have working hours with considerable overlap with eastern time will also be considered.

Responsibilities:

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting
• Lead HRW’s annual organizational budget process, including planning, coordination, consolidation and analysis.
• Develop financial models, scenarios, analyses and management reporting to support the CFO, Executive leadership, Finance & Investment Committee and other Board stakeholders in strategic decision making.
• Lead organizational forecasting and multi-year financial planning, ensuring projections reflect organizational priorities, operating plans, revenue expectations, and emerging risks and opportunities.
• Monitor and report on financial performance through monthly and quarterly management reporting, including budget versus actuals, forecasts, cash flow projections, and key financial and organizational indicators.
• Perform other tasks as may be required.

Grant Financial Management
• Partner with Development and Programs to develop donor proposal and grant budgets, monitor grant financial performance, and ensure timely and accurate donor financial reporting through the grant cycle.
• Develop and maintain indirect cost recovery approaches to ensure that full costs are presented and covered.

Systems, Reporting and Process Improvement
• Strengthen financial systems, reporting tools, dashboards, and data-driven decision making in collaboration with Technology, Accounting and Development, and other functions.
• Identify and implement improvements to financial processes, systems, and reporting capabilities to enhance efficiency, accuracy, integration, and decision making.

Leadership and Partnership
• Lead and develop a high-performing FP&A and Grants Management team through a culture of mentorship, collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement and customer service.
• Build cross-functional partnerships across Operations, Development, and Programs promoting financial understanding, helping leaders understand financial implications, tradeoffs and opportunities.

Qualifications:
Education: A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field is required. A CPA, ACCA, CIMA, MBA, or equivalent advanced degree/certification preferred.

Experience: A minimum of ten years of experience overseeing financial and budgetary activities, and a minimum of five years of managerial experience, are required.

Related Skills and Knowledge:

1. Demonstrated experience leading organizational budgeting, forecasting, multi-year financial planning, financial modeling, and management reporting in a complex multinational and/or non-profit organization – ideally both.
2. Significant experience managing donor-funded grants and restricted funding, including proposal budgeting, financial forecasting, expenditure monitoring, and donor financial reporting.
3. Experience partnering and advising senior executives, boards, and complex international operations is required; a demonstrated ability to influence without specific authority and to build financial literacy in non-financial leadership is desirable.
4. Strong financial modeling, analytical, and leadership skills are required.
5. Strong written and verbal communication skills in English are required; fluency in additional languages (particularly French) is advantageous.
6. Experience with ERP systems, business intelligence tools, and multi-currency environments are required, experience with NetSuite, Salesforce and Concur are preferred.
7. Proven ability to translate complex financial information into actionable recommendations for non-financial stakeholders.
8. Strong managerial skills, and the demonstrated ability to closely partner with other operational functions is required.

jobs.description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo’s Technical Program Managers and Program Managers are accountable for Waymo’s roadmap execution by providing thoughtful cross-functional planning, clarity, and proactive risk management. In the face of complex technical and operational challenges with no established playbooks to follow, we act with thoughtful urgency, driving conversations, discussions, and outcomes. Our team partners closely with every function of Waymo to structure, own and drive work towards real-world deployments of the Waymo Driver across platforms and geographies.

You will:

• Lead cross-functional technical programs to integrate Waymo's autonomous service with third-party platforms.

• Own the technical delivery of external integrations end-to-end, from creating the cross-functional execution plan to defining the process for ensuring continued quality post-launch.

• Serve as the primary execution counterpart for external teams, translating an ambiguous set of work into clearly defined deliverables, owners, and schedule.

• Drive technical trade-off decisions across scope, schedule, scalability, and user experience.

• Proactively identify, prioritize, and mitigate risks and dependencies across multiple concurrent partner programs, and represent them to executive leadership.

• Build the scalable frameworks, processes, and tooling that let Waymo onboard and operate many partner integrations without a linear increase in effort.

You have:

• 7+ years of experience leading highly complex, cross-functional technical programs with a holistic understanding of business-wide functions (e.g. Product, Engineering, Business Development, Operations).

• A track record of shipping consumer-facing software products and features, with demonstrated ownership of the execution from kickoff through launch and post-launch operations.

• Experience running programs where critical dependencies sit with teams outside your direct influence, and a track record of getting them to deliver.

• Strong technical depth: you can read a system design, hold your own in architecture and API discussions with engineers, and tease out the scope, schedule, and risk implications of each option to drive the decision.

• Deep care for the end user, with the ability to keep rider experience and quality at the center of technically complex, multi-party programs.

• Exceptional communication and leadership skills, with demonstrated ability to align diverse internal teams and external partners and influence executive stakeholders.

jobs.title: Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst
jobs.description:
Thanks for your interest in Oklo!  We are searching for an Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst to join our environmental compliance team.

Position Description

The Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst is responsible for analyzing the resource areas included in a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) report. This includes performing research and technical analyses for resource areas such as, but not limited to, land use, water resources, air resources, and socioeconomics. The Analyst position is responsible for documentation of each of the resource areas in environmental deliverables to the lead agency performing the NEPA analysis. This position also supports providing technical work for State and local compliance requirements as needed.

Specific responsibilities may include:

• Research, analyze, and interpret Federal environmental laws, regulations, and guidance

• Evaluate the policy implications of proposed legislation, regulations, and agency actions

• Draft and revise Environmental Reports for NEPA and briefing materials

• Support development of internal environmental technical processes and compliance frameworks

• Track regulatory changes and assess risk, compliance gaps, and operational impacts

• Assist with environmental permitting processes (air, water, waste, land use, etc.)

• Support compliance with NEPA, NHPA, Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and the Endangered Species Act

• Interface with regulatory agencies (e.g., NRC, DOE) to clarify requirements and respond to inquiries

• Review technical studies and consultant reports for accuracy and policy alignment

• Incorporate technical studies into NEPA documentation

• Prepare materials and lead meetings with regulators

• Maintain organized records of regulatory correspondence

• Monitor emerging trends in environmental policy

• Support audits, inspections, and internal reviews as needed

Experience Level:

• Intermediate (2-5yr) or Experienced (5-10yr)

Minimum Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s, Master’s or Ph.D in Environmental Policy, Environmental Science, Environmental Studies, Natural Resources, Public Policy, Sustainability, or a closely related field or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience

Bonus Qualifications:

• Experience in NEPA compliance with the NRC or DOE

• Experience in Ohio, Tennessee, Idaho, Alaska

Competencies

We are looking for an Environmental Policy & Compliance Analyst that:

• Has a working knowledge of environmental laws and regulations (Federal, State, and local)

• Is able to interpret statutes, rules, permits, and guidance documents and assess complex regulatory requirements

• Is able to evaluate likelihood and severity of different regulatory strategies

• Understands NRC and DOE regulatory processes and agency roles

• Aware of how policy changes affect compliance obligations and operations

• Familiar with NEPA documentation

• Is able to analyze environmental and compliance data

• Is able to review and evaluate technical studies and consultant reports

• Is able to write clear, accurate technical and regulatory documents

• Communicate effectively with regulators, consultants, and internal stakeholders

• Is able to manage multiple priorities

• Detail oriented and able to spot inconsistencies or errors in compliance materials

• Motivated to stay current on evolving regulations and policy trends

• Open to feedback and skill development

• Passionate about clean energy

• An optimist at heart

• Passionate about making advanced fission a reality

• Willing and able to learn quickly

• Willing to think differently and do things in new ways

• Comfortable in a fast-paced, highly iterative startup environment

• Excited to think creatively, critically, and reflectively about the problems they are solving while not leaning only on what has been done before

• Willing to propose novel and creative solutions to technical problems

• An excellent writer who can write in a modern active voice, so make your cover letter compelling and write it well!

• Able to communicate technical content and results verbally

Who you are:

A startup person: You aren't driven by titles or hierarchy, and prefer efficiency to excess process. You don't need or expect to have a lot of guidance but you enjoy working in a fast-paced team. If you prefer the culture and feel of a large organization, that is great, but you likely won’t enjoy working with us! There is plenty of important work and plenty of good opportunities with organizations like that.

Motivated: You are self-motivated. You bring an enthusiasm to the team, and imbue a sense of passion that goes beyond clocking in and clocking out. This isn’t about a fake or arbitrary “pieces of flair” mentality or lack of work-life balance! It is about being a part of the vision and feeling a part of reaching team goals.

A team-player: Oklo genuinely is a team. We aren’t about taking credit for ourselves, and we aren’t about pushing blame to others. We do incredible things because we work as a team.

An excellent communicator: We need a person who is not only technically competent but also a clear and upbeat communicator.

Creative: Being creative means that when things fall outside clear scopes or processes or problems arise without clear solutions, you are able to identify it as well as invent ways to solve a problem or fill a need without micromanagement. The successful person in this job will not only be creative, but also enjoy being creative and solving open-ended problems which may change day-by-day.

Detail-oriented: This focus is a big part of excellence, consistency, and quality. Excellent grammar and spelling matter for both good communication as well as the image of the company that we put forward.

About Oklo travel requirements:

Oklo requires remote employees to travel to headquarters (Santa Clara, CA) twice a quarter annually, based on business or team needs, including attendance at team meetings, off-sites, and other company events or gatherings. For the first two weeks of onboarding, employees are required to be in person at headquarters in Santa Clara, CA.

About Oklo compensation: $100,000-$150,000

Oklo offers flexible time off, equity, competitive pay, 401k, health insurance, FSA, flexible work hours, and other benefits.

We are looking to fill this position immediately!

About Oklo Inc.: Oklo Inc. is developing fast fission power plants to deliver clean, reliable, and affordable energy at scale; establishing a domestic supply chain for critical radioisotopes; and advancing nuclear fuel recycling to convert nuclear waste into clean energy. Oklo was the first to receive a site use permit from the U.S. Department of Energy for a commercial advanced fission plant, was awarded fuel material from Idaho National Laboratory, and submitted the first custom combined license application for an advanced reactor to the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Oklo is also developing advanced fuel recycling technologies in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy and U.S. National Laboratories.

#CHOP: Oklo’s Values
Collaboration: We go further, together. We bring diverse perspectives, listen actively, and build trust through transparency and respect. We work across disciplines, sharing ownership to turn complex challenges into shared successes.
Humility: We are team players who act for the good of the company and for the world. We are focused on our mission, not personal recognition.
Ownership: We take pride in what we do and how we do it. We are proactive in finding solutions and see tasks through  to completion. We are committed to delivering on our promises to provide clean, reliable, and affordable energy.
Pathfinding: We chart new ground where no path exists by approaching challenges with curiosity, courage, and creativity while navigating ambiguity.

Candidates should be aware that employment may be contingent upon successful completion of a drug screening, and employees may be subject to drug testing at any time in accordance with company policy and applicable laws.

Recruitment Fraud Disclaimer

Oklo is aware of recent recruitment fraud attempts targeting job seekers. Please be cautious of anyone claiming to represent Oklo who does not contact you from an official Oklo email address.

All legitimate communications from our recruiting team— including application updates, interview requests, and job offers — will come exclusively from an @oklo.com email. Oklo will never ask for sensitive personal information, payments, or account credentials during the hiring process.

If you receive suspicious outreach or have concerns about the authenticity of any communication claiming to be from Oklo, please contact us through the official channels listed on our website.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

As an AM Supervisor - Heat Treat, EDM, Bandsaw, Media Blast, you will lead a team of highly trained technicians operating a growing fleet of Monolith LPBF additive manufacturing systems. jobs.title: Partner 20, Social Media Lead, Frontier
jobs.description:
Founded in Silicon Valley in 2009 by Marc Andreessen and Ben Horowitz, Andreessen Horowitz (aka a16z) is a venture capital firm that backs bold entrepreneurs building the future through technology. We are stage agnostic. We invest in seed to venture to growth-stage technology companies, across AI, bio + healthcare, consumer, enterprise, fintech, frontier, games, and companies building toward American dynamism. a16z has $100B+ under management across multiple funds.

We’ve established a team that is defined by respect for the entrepreneur and the company-building process; we know what it’s like to be in the founder’s shoes. Our team is at the forefront of new technology, helping founders and their companies impact and change the world.

a16z Frontier is a venture capital fund from Andreessen Horowitz that invests in emerging technologies across AI, biology, crypto, hardware, and more. We’re drawn to the outer planets, the outliers and edge cases that don’t fit neatly into preset categories. This has been our approach for years: backing founders building a future no one else sees yet, long before it becomes mainstream. Some projects start out looking absurd or unserious — more like toys, experiments, or weekend hobbies — but go on to change lives.

The Frontier marketing team supports portfolio companies through R&D; engineering, security, and best practices; legal and regulatory, designed to guide founders and policymakers in traditionally unregulated or tough regulatory environments; go-to-market expertise, including platform support and partnerships for emerging markets; recruiting services to scale businesses; and marketing that helps founders and others navigate the frontier.

This is a rare opportunity at an established, prolific “direct media” operation — a model pioneered and proven by this team for over a decade at a16z — that has published influential industry reports, op-eds, builder playbooks, podcasts/ videos, newsletters, and other content distributed on various platforms. The marketing team is composed of experienced brand marketers, top communications/ PR experts, designers, and editors coming from both established media outlets and in-house content marketing operations; the social media will cover all these marketing functions, while reporting into editorial.

The Role

The Social Media Lead is responsible for growing a16z Frontier’s social channels, including engaging key communities across different audiences in different domains. They will work closely with the Frontier marketing team to (1) adapt and distribute existing content pieces into social media posts; and (2) help create content native to social media: clips, campaigns, and more. This spans everything from social media for external pod appearances/ media interviews to investment announcements; to events and major industry conferences; to editorial content; to special projects, campaigns, and more.

This person will also advise the broader a16z Frontier team (from investing to operations) — as well as our portfolio companies — in social media strategy and profile building.

This is a remote role (including on West Coast time), though occasional in-office presence will be required for regular team offsites, occasional conferences/events, and based on business needs.

To join our team, you are:

• Always online. You’re on top of internet culture and the latest online conversations, monitor sentiment as well as tracking industry trends and shifts. You’re able to use this context to craft and tailor compelling, informative, and entertaining social media

• Curious and constantly learning about new domains, including the latest advancements in science and technology

• Able to both strategize and build hands-on. You’re a doer who likes taking ideas to execution and is able to operationalize them into process, pipelines, and content calendars. But you’re not just good at the tactics: You’re also someone who is able to come up with fresh ideas — whether through collaboratively brainstorming with team members, proposing your own creative formats, or staying on top of the latest social media trends so you know which experiments to run and prioritize

• Always analyzing social media platforms. You’re data-driven and always optimizing, but also know how to trust your intuition beyond just data and think big-picture. You and we will have hypotheses around content packages — and you will (working closely with our audience development lead) know how to test them, evaluate what’s working or not, and report back so we build those learnings into our content programs

• A creator and a producer. You’re able to directly create social content when needed — but also able to help produce it with others, including overseeing our short-form clips operation (leveraging our technical A/V and production vendors). This includes identifying, adapting, editing, and timing the right clips — as well as other creative for social — so they’re compelling, engaging, and well-received on socials

• Able to be our voice. You would be the online brand voice for a16z Frontier. You’re able to regularly engage with relevant social media communities and different audiences — as well as identifying and engaging key influencers across various verticals/ domains

Minimum Qualifications

• Direct, hands-on experience owning social media for a high-visibility or high-growth brand — past experience embedded in a content operation is especially welcome

• Excellent communicator — through text, multimedia, design, or memes

• Proven ability to adapt style and voice across different formats, platforms, and audiences — able to be thoughtful, smart, accessible, direct… all while striking the right tone (not corporate, not cringe, not overly whimsical, not staid)

• Experience with X, LinkedIn, etc. required — and optionally, with crypto-native or alt social media tools and video

• Strong command of data — from implementing and using various analytics tools, to regularly interpreting and reporting insights

• Ability to collaborate well cross-functionally, meet multi-threaded deadlines, more

• Passionate about technology, open source, and more

• Low ego, high empathy, and the capacity to collaborate effectively with diverse teams

The anticipated salary range for this role is between $199,000 - $232,000, actual starting pay may vary based on a range of factors which can include experience, skills, and scope.

This role is eligible to participate in the a16z carry program and various discretionary bonus programs as well as benefit and perquisite plans including health, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, 401K plan, vacation, and sick leave.

a16z culture

• We do only first class business and only in a first class way

• We take a long view of relationships, because we are in the relationship business

• We believe in the future and bet the firm that way

• We are all different, we recognize that, and we win

• We celebrate the good times

• We do it for the team

• We play to win

At a16z we are always looking to hire the absolute best talent and recognize that diversity in our experiences and backgrounds is what makes us stronger. We hire candidates of any race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, marital or family status, disability, Veteran status, and any other status. These differences are what enables us to work towards the future we envision for ourselves, our portfolio companies, and the World.

Our organization participates in E-Verify. Click here to learn about E-Verify.

jobs.title: Senior Associate, FP&A
jobs.description:
We're hiring a Senior Associate, FP&A to be the analyst behind our marketplace levers — recruiter incentives and retainers, pricing and take rate, unit economics, and vertical P&Ls. You'll run the monthly budget vs. actuals review, maintain the operating model with our VP Finance, and be the analytical partner leadership leans on for pricing and incentive decisions. You'll report to our VP Finance and work closely with our accounting team.

This is a builder role. Marketplace economics are more interesting than a standard SaaS P&L — take rates, recruiter supply, roles posted, time-to-hire, and placement timing all drive revenue — and you'll build the analysis the company runs on.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Maintain the operating model with the VP Finance. Keep the drivers current — revenue, GMV, headcount, OpEx — and support the annual plan and quarterly reforecasts.

 - Model marketplace levers. Recruiter incentives and retainers, pricing and take rate, and fee structures — build the analysis behind each decision and track what happens after it ships.

 - Own unit economics. GMV, net revenue, take rate, recruiter payouts, cohort behavior, LTV:CAC, and payback — the numbers leadership makes pricing and incentive calls on.

 - Run budget vs. actuals. Monthly BvA and department-level flux review with our accounting team, with clear variance explanations for leadership.

 - Build the metrics layer. Partner with RevOps and BizOps to define metrics and build the dashboards leadership uses every week.

 - Automate with AI. We use AI heavily across the company and expect finance to as well — recurring reporting shouldn't be manual.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3–5 years in FP&A, strategic finance, investment banking, PE, or top-tier consulting, with at least 1–2 years building models an operating team actually used.

 - Expert spreadsheet modeling — three-statement, driver-based forecasts, and scenario analysis.

 - Comfortable presenting numbers to executives and turning an ambiguous question into a clear answer.

 - High ownership, low ego, and fast. Your work goes straight to the exec team and board.

 - Bonus: experience at a marketplace, fintech, or usage-based business; a Series B–C fundraise; hands-on with a planning tool (Pigment, Anaplan) or SQL/BI (Metabase, Looker).
   
   


THE IDEAL CANDIDATE BRINGS

 - Experience in multi-sided / marketplace businesses

 - Has owned analysis of a marketing subsidy or incentive program

 - Has built the take-rate or pricing model at a marketplace and defended it to leadership

 - Has run a monthly BvA where department leads had to explain their variances to them

 - Has worked from raw transaction data (SQL or exports), not just a finance system's outputs

 - Has gone through a raise on the company side: model, data room, diligence questions


ABOUT PARAFORM

Paraform is the first end-to-end AI recruiting marketplace, modernizing one of the largest and most fragmented markets in the world: hiring. We connect companies with thousands of specialized recruiters and AI agents that work together to fill roles faster and more accurately.

We believe recruiting works best when human judgment is paired with AI that truly understands hiring. That's why we treat recruiters like entrepreneurs, not vendors, and build the financial, operational, and technical infrastructure that powers their success.

Industry leaders like Decagon, Palantir, Rippling, Abridge, and Hightouch hire through Paraform, and we grew revenue 8× last year. We're backed by Scale, Felicis, A*, BOND, Liquid 2, DST Global, and the founders of YouTube, Instacart, Canva, and more.

Our mission is to make hiring fast, reliable, and scalable for every company in the world. For more on where we're headed, read our company vision https://www.paraform.com/blog/the-talent-company.

jobs.title: Consultant, Human Health Risk Assessment and Community Health
jobs.description:
Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
• Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
• Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
• Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
• Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company!  Successful candidates will typically possess:

• Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology

• Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
• Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
• 2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
• Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

• Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
• Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
• Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
• GIS capability is a plus.
• Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

What we can offer you

• Meaningful, high-impact work
• Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
• Competitive compensation and benefits
• Professional development and leadership opportunities
• A collaborative and inclusive culture
• The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company

Salary Transparency Statement

At Ramboll, we are committed to fair and transparent compensation practices that support our people and our purpose of creating sustainable societies. The anticipated base salary range for this position is $79,040–$98,800 per year. This range reflects the compensation we reasonably expect to offer at the time of posting. Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as location, skills, experience, education, and internal equity. Because we operate across multiple U.S. markets, pay may differ depending on the cost of labor in specific locations. In addition to base salary, this position may be eligible for bonus, overtime or other forms of compensation and we offer a comprehensive benefits package that supports well-being, professional development, and work-life balance. Our recruiters are happy to share more about the specific salary range and total rewards package applicable to your location during the hiring process.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll in the Americas

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Where People Flourish

Our mission is to create sustainable societies where people and nature flourish. This means that a culture of inclusion is embedded in everything we do.  Our people bring diverse backgrounds and experiences to the company, enabling us to deliver innovative and forward-thinking solutions to our clients. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. Ramboll wants to ensure opportunities are accessible to candidates with disabilities. So, please let us know if there are any changes we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. Ready to join us?

jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io http://www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

 
 
 
 
 

Mission | On Site | Full Time | U.S. Citizenship Required / No Active Clearance Required

 
 
 
 
 


ROLE SUMMARY

Twenty builds AI-enabled technology for mission-critical cyber operations. We're seeking a Staff Product Manager to help make agentic AI systems measurable, reliable, and continuously improvable. You’ll partner with AI and engineering teams to shape evaluation capabilities—from defining agent performance and product quality to turning results into useful workflows and product decisions.

The strongest candidates will bring meaningful experience building or managing agentic systems, either by directly building evaluations or by building the systems that enable teams to evaluate and improve agents. Cyber experience is a plus, but not required.

 


WHO YOU ARE

 - You're a product-minded, technically curious operator who is excited about how agentic systems work and how to make them better.

 - You bring strong product judgment and can turn complex technical needs into clear, usable product direction.

 - You enjoy partnering with engineers and AI teams, asking good questions, and working through ambiguity together.

 - You are rigorous about evidence and metrics, while recognizing that evaluation methods need to reflect real user and product needs.

 - You take ownership, communicate clearly, and are comfortable balancing learning, execution, and iteration.
   


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own or support the product roadmap for agentic AI evaluations, translating product-area goals into clear priorities and outcomes.

 - Partner closely with engineering and AI teams to understand evaluation needs, technical constraints, and user workflows.

 - Define how agent performance and product quality should be assessed, including useful measures of task success, reliability, and quality.

 - Turn technical evaluation needs into clear product requirements, workflows, and acceptance criteria.

 - Help operationalize evaluation workflows and success metrics so teams can consistently assess agent behavior and product changes.

 - Use evaluation results and feedback to identify gaps, inform product decisions, and improve the agent experience over time.
   


MUST HAVE

 - Strong product experience with AI or agentic systems, including experience building or managing agentic systems through product work.

 - Experience directly building evaluations for agents or building the evaluation product, tooling, or system used to assess them.

 - Ability to translate technical evaluation needs into product requirements, priorities, and workflows in partnership with engineering and AI teams.

 - Ability to define or operationalize meaningful measures of agent performance and product quality.

 - Strong communication, collaboration, and product judgment in an evolving, technically complex environment.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience in cybersecurity, offensive cyber, government, defense, intelligence, or another mission-driven environment.

 - Familiarity with evaluation approaches such as benchmarks, human or automated evaluation, regression testing, simulation, or analysis of agent traces.

 - Experience working with products that combine autonomous systems with meaningful human judgment and oversight.



Benefits 
What's on the table:

 - Health. Medical, dental, and vision plan options. Life / AD&D, disability coverage options.

 - Family. Paid parental leave for eligible full-time employees. 12 weeks for birthing parents, 4 for non-birthing parents, 6 weeks for adoptive, foster, or intended parents through surrogacy.

Benefits vary by location, role, and eligibility. Full plan details provided during the interview and offer process.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager/Tech Lead Manager - Runtime Engineering
jobs.description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


ENGINEERING MANAGER – SPARK RUNTIME ENGINEERING

Location: Bellevue, WA or Menlo Park, CA




ABOUT THE TEAM

The Spark Runtime Engineering Team brings Snowflake’s performance, efficiency, and reliability to Spark workloads. Our mission is to help customers scale data processing while preserving the familiar Spark APIs and semantics they rely on. We build the compiler and runtime integration that translate Spark workloads into efficient execution on Snowflake’s cloud-native query engine. This includes tackling complex challenges in compiler infrastructure, query-plan lowering, Spark compatibility, execution integration, and end-to-end observability to deliver faster, more cost-efficient data processing at scale.

We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Manager who combines deep technical expertise with strong people leadership. You will shape the team’s technical direction, stay actively engaged in architecture and critical engineering decisions, and hire, mentor, and grow a high-performing engineering team to advance the future of Spark on Snowflake.


ROLE OVERVIEW

You will lead a team of approximately 5–8 engineers building production compiler and runtime capabilities for Spark workloads on Snowflake. You will guide architectural decisions, review critical designs and code, and help investigate complex correctness, performance, and reliability issues. In partnership with compiler, query engine, runtime, and product teams, you will turn customer needs into a focused roadmap and measurable engineering outcomes.


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Set technical direction for Spark query compilation and runtime integration, including intermediate representations, type resolution, semantic compatibility, query-plan transformations, and efficient SQL generation.

 - Improve end-to-end workload performance and cost-efficiency through profiling, compilation-latency reduction, metadata-access improvements, and collaboration with query-engine teams.

 - Establish strong correctness and compatibility practices, including differential testing against Apache Spark, regression coverage, and clear handling of unsupported behavior.

 - Own the production quality of the team’s components, including observability, incident response, fault recovery, and safe rollout practices.

 - Hire, coach, and develop engineers; provide actionable feedback, manage performance, and support career growth across experience levels.

 - Partner with senior technical leaders and Product Management to prioritize investments, manage dependencies, and deliver a realistic roadmap.

 - Validate changes against representative customer workloads and track measurable improvements in compatibility, latency, reliability, and cost-efficiency.


MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

 - 2+ years of direct engineering management experience, with demonstrated success developing engineers and delivering production systems.

 - 5+ years of hands-on software engineering experience, including substantial work on compilers, query-processing systems, or runtime infrastructure.

 - Deep expertise in at least one relevant area, such as compiler architecture and IR transformations, relational query processing, language semantics and type systems, or runtime integration.

 - Proficiency in Scala, Java, C++, or a comparable implementation language, with the ability to review production code and guide technical decisions.

 - Strong systems fundamentals, including concurrency, memory behavior, and performance analysis, together with experience debugging complex production issues.

 - Ability to translate technical and customer requirements into engineering priorities and collaborate effectively across teams and locations.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Apache Spark internals, Catalyst, Spark Connect, or DataFrame APIs.

 - Experience with relational algebra, SQL generation, query optimization, or database execution systems.

 - Experience with Scala/JVM performance, native runtime functions, metadata caching, or compilation-performance optimization.

 - Experience building compatibility-test frameworks, differential testing, performance benchmarks, or production observability for data systems.

 - Experience leading systems through customer adoption, production hardening, and staged releases.

 - A degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.


WHY JOIN US?

Help shape how Spark workloads run on Snowflake. You will work on technically challenging compiler and runtime problems, grow a strong engineering team, and make a measurable difference to the correctness, reliability, and cost-efficiency of customers’ data processing.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com
